  5. 备份与恢复Backup and recovery

这一单元几乎全是「解释题」——考试不让你算，而是让你说清某类攻击怎么运作、某种防护为什么有效。背术语前先搞懂「敌人在想什么」。This unit is mostly "explain" questions — you won't calculate, you'll describe how an attack works and why a defence is effective. Understand the attacker's mindset before memorising terms.

1 威胁类型：谁在偷你的数据 Threat types: who wants your data malware · phishing · social engineering · DoS · SQL injection 恶意软件 · 网络钓鱼 · 社工 · DoS · SQL 注入
目标：认识六类常见安全威胁，考试能一句话说清每种是怎么攻击的。Goal: know the six common threats and say, in one line, how each one attacks.
安全威胁不是只有「黑客在电脑前敲键盘」这一种。真正最常见的，往往是骗人：一封伪装成银行的邮件、一个来路不明的 U 盘、一句「我是 IT 部门，请告诉我密码」。我们把这些威胁分成几类：恶意软件是坏程序自己动手，网络钓鱼是发假邮件骗你点链接，社工攻击是骗你说出秘密，DoS/DDoS是用海量请求把服务器压垮，内部威胁是「自己人」泄密，SQL 注入是在输入框里塞代码去偷数据库。 Threats aren't only "a hacker typing at a keyboard". The most common ones trick people: a fake bank email, a dodgy USB stick, a voice saying "I'm IT, tell me your password". We group them: malware is harmful programs acting on their own, phishing is fake mail that makes you click, social engineering tricks you into revealing secrets, DoS/DDoS crushes a server with traffic, insider threat is "one of us" leaking data, and SQL injection sneaks code into an input box to steal from the database.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 恶意软件 malware：病毒(virus)、蠕虫(worm)、木马(trojan)、勒索软件(ransomware)——病毒寄生于文件、蠕虫自我复制、木马伪装、勒索软件加密文件要赎金。Malware: virus, worm, trojan, ransomware — a virus attaches to files, a worm replicates itself, a trojan disguises itself, ransomware encrypts files for ransom.
  • 网络钓鱼 phishing：伪装成银行/官方发邮件或短信，诱导点假链接、输密码。Phishing: fake emails or texts posing as a bank, tricking you into clicking links or entering passwords.
  • 社工攻击 social engineering：不碰技术，靠「骗人」套取信息，比如冒充 IT 部门要密码。Social engineering: no hacking — just tricking people, e.g. posing as IT to ask for a password.
  • DoS / DDoS：用海量请求把服务器刷到瘫痪，让正常用户进不来；DDoS 是「很多台机器一起打」。DoS / DDoS: flooding a server with requests so real users can't get in; a DDoS comes from many machines at once.
  • 内部威胁 insider threat：有权限的员工故意或无意泄露、破坏数据。Insider threat: an authorised employee leaks or damages data, on purpose or by accident.
  • SQL 注入 SQL injection：在网页输入框里塞入恶意 SQL 语句，让数据库执行不该执行的命令。SQL injection: typing malicious SQL into an input box so the database runs commands it shouldn't.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Malware is malicious software such as viruses, worms, trojans and ransomware. Phishing uses fake emails to trick users into revealing credentials. A denial-of-service (DoS) attack floods a server with traffic so it cannot serve legitimate users.
例题Example
一封邮件说「你的账户异常，点击链接重新验证密码」，这是什么攻击？为什么危险？An email says "your account is abnormal, click this link to re-verify your password". What attack is this, and why is it dangerous?
这是网络钓鱼 phishing——伪装成可信机构，诱导你点假链接。It is phishing — posing as a trusted body to make you click a fake link. 你一输入密码，账号就被盗；链接还可能悄悄装上恶意软件。The moment you type your password it is stolen; the link may also install malware.
练习Practice
提示：想想是「骗人」还是「直接攻击程序」。Hint: think — tricking a person, or attacking a program directly?

一名员工把客户的姓名和电话卖给了外人，属于哪类威胁？An employee sells customers' names and phone numbers to outsiders. What type of threat is this?

点开看答案Show answer
内部威胁 insider threat——有权限的「自己人」故意泄露数据，再强的技术也难防。Insider threat — a trusted insider deliberately leaks data, which even strong technology can't easily stop.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 防护措施：一层层把数据围起来 Defences: layers that guard the data firewall · antivirus · authentication · encryption · access rights 防火墙 · 杀毒 · 认证 · 加密 · 权限
目标：认识六类常见防护，考试能说清每种防的是什么。Goal: know six common defences and say what each one protects against.
防威胁就像给家装门：防火墙是小区大门，把可疑的进出先挡一道；防病毒软件是安检，扫描有没有带坏东西进来；认证是门禁，得先证明「你是你」；加密是把值钱东西锁进保险箱，就算被偷走也看不懂；访问权限是规定每个房间谁能进；员工培训最容易被忽略——人永远是最薄弱的一环。 Defending is like securing a home: the firewall is the front gate that screens traffic; antivirus is the security check that scans for anything bad; authentication is the keypad that proves "you are you"; encryption locks valuables in a safe that's useless even if stolen; access rights decide who may enter each room; and staff training is the most overlooked — people are always the weakest link.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 防火墙 firewall：监视进出流量，按规则放行或拦截，挡住外部入侵。Firewall: monitors traffic in and out, allowing or blocking it by rules.
  • 防病毒软件 antivirus：扫描文件和程序，发现并清除恶意软件。Antivirus: scans files and programs, finding and removing malware.
  • 认证 authentication：证明身份——密码(password)、双因素(2FA)、生物识别(biometrics，指纹/人脸)。Authentication: proves identity — password, two-factor (2FA), biometrics (fingerprint/face).
  • 加密 encryption：把数据打乱成密文，没密钥就解不开，防窃听。Encryption: scrambles data into ciphertext that is useless without the key, preventing eavesdropping.
  • 访问权限 access rights：给不同用户不同级别的读写权限，遵循最小权限原则。Access rights: different read/write levels per user, following the least-privilege principle.
  • 员工培训 staff training：教会大家识别钓鱼、设强密码——因为人最容易被骗。Staff training: teaches spotting phishing and using strong passwords — people are the easiest to fool.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A firewall monitors and filters network traffic. Antivirus software detects and removes malware. Authentication verifies a user's identity, encryption protects data by making it unreadable without a key, and access rights limit what each user can do.
例题Example
为什么只有强密码还不够，还要「双因素认证 2FA」？Why is a strong password not enough, and why add two-factor authentication (2FA)?
密码是「你知道的东西」，可能被偷、被猜、被钓鱼骗走。A password is "something you know" — it can be stolen, guessed or phished. 2FA 再加一样「你有的东西」（手机验证码）或「你是什么」（指纹），即使密码泄露，攻击者还是进不来。2FA adds "something you have" (a phone code) or "something you are" (a fingerprint), so even a leaked password won't let an attacker in.
练习Practice
提示：想「数据在半路被偷看」这件事。Hint: think about data being read in transit.

一份工资表在发给会计前先被「加密」，请问这防的是哪类风险？A payroll file is encrypted before being sent to the accountant. What risk does this protect against?

点开看答案Show answer
防的是数据在传输/存储中被偷看（窃听）——加密后即使被截获，没有密钥也读不懂，保护的是数据的机密性。It protects against data being read in transit/storage (eavesdropping) — once encrypted, even if intercepted it can't be read without the key, protecting the data's confidentiality.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 验证 vs 校验（高频考点） Validation vs verification (hot topic) validation · verification · double entry 验证 · 校验 · 双重输入
目标：彻底分清 validation（合理性）和 verification（一致性），看到题目能对号入座。Goal: firmly separate validation (reasonableness) from verification (consistency), and match each example to the right one.
这两个词长得像、考得多，是 Paper 1 的「送分题也是丢分题」。验证 validation 关心的是「数据本身合不合理」——年龄不能是负数、邮箱得有 @、生日得是日期，检查的是值；校验 verification 关心的是「数据跟原始一不一样」——把同一串东西输两遍对照，或者照着原始文件目视核对，检查的是录入过程有没有抄错。一句话：validation 看「合不合理」，verification 看「一不一致」。 These two words look alike and get tested constantly — the easiest marks to win and to lose on Paper 1. Validation asks whether the data itself is reasonable — age can't be negative, an email must have @, a birthday must be a date; it checks the value. Verification asks whether the data matches the original — typing it twice and comparing, or visually checking against the source; it checks whether copying went wrong. In one line: validation = reasonableness, verification = consistency.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • validation = 合理性：范围检查、格式检查、类型检查、长度检查、存在性检查，都在输入时做。Validation = reasonableness: range, format, type, length and presence checks, all done at entry.
  • verification = 一致性：双重输入（double entry）、目视核对（visual check），防止抄错录错。Verification = consistency: double entry and visual check, to catch copying mistakes.
  • 高频陷阱：双重输入是 verification 不是 validation！它不是判断值合不合理，而是两份「对得上」。Hot trap: double entry is verification, not validation! It doesn't judge reasonableness — it checks the two copies agree.
  • 常见搭配：字段类型不对 → validation 类型检查；密码输两遍一致 → verification 双重输入。Common pairs: wrong field type → validation type check; typing a password twice → verification double entry.
避坑：看到「double entry / visual check」就选 verification；看到「range / format / type」就选 validation。「密码至少 8 位」是 validation（合理），「密码输两遍」是 verification（一致）。Avoid the trap: "double entry / visual check" → verification; "range / format / type" → validation. "Password at least 8 characters" is validation; "type the password twice" is verification.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Validation checks that data is reasonable, using range, format and type checks at the point of entry. Verification checks that data matches the original, for example by double entry or visual comparison, in order to catch copying errors.
例题Example
判断下列各是 validation 还是 verification，并说明理由：(a) 年龄字段必须 0–120；(b) 让用户把邮箱输两遍。For each, say whether it is validation or verification and why: (a) age must be 0–120; (b) the user must type the email twice.
(a) 是 validation——范围检查，判断值是否在合理范围内。(a) is validation — a range check judging whether the value is reasonable. (b) 是 verification——双重输入，两次录入一致才算没抄错。(b) is verification — double entry; two matching copies mean no copying error.
练习Practice
提示：看它是在查「合不合理」还是「对得上原样」。Hint: is it checking reasonableness, or matching the original?

工作人员录入身份证号后，再照着原始证件核对一遍，这是 validation 还是 verification？为什么？A clerk types an ID number, then checks it against the original document. Is this validation or verification, and why?

点开看答案Show answer
是 verification（目视核对 visual check）——它不判断号码合不合理，而是和原始证件比「是否一致」，目的是发现录入时的抄写错误。It is verification (a visual check) — it doesn't judge whether the number is reasonable, but whether it matches the original, to catch a typing error.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 数据完整性检查 Data integrity checks parity · checksum · echo check · hash 奇偶校验 · 校验和 · 回显检查 · 哈希
目标：会算奇偶校验位，能说出奇偶校验/校验和/回显/哈希各检查什么。Goal: compute a parity bit, and say what parity, checksum, echo check and hash each detect.
数据在传输、存储时可能被「改坏」——一个比特从 0 翻成 1。怎么发现？有几种「完整性检查」：奇偶校验 parity，数 1 的个数，凑成偶数（偶校验）或奇数（奇校验）；校验和 checksum，把数据当成数字加起来，接收方再算一遍比一比；回显检查 echo check，发过去再让对方原样发回来，对比是否一致；哈希值 hash，用一个函数把文件压缩成一串固定长度的「指纹」，文件哪怕改一个字节，指纹就完全变了——常用于验证下载的文件没被篡改。 Data can be corrupted in transit or storage — one bit flips from 0 to 1. How do we notice? There are several integrity checks: parity counts the 1s and makes them even (or odd); a checksum adds the data as numbers and recomputes it on receipt; an echo check sends the data back for comparison; and a hash squeezes a file into a fixed-length "fingerprint" — change one byte and the fingerprint changes completely, which is why hashes verify a downloaded file hasn't been altered.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 奇偶校验 parity：只加 1 个校验位，让 1 的总数为偶数（偶校验）或奇数（奇校验）。Parity: adds one bit so the number of 1s is even (even parity) or odd (odd parity).
  • 它只能发现奇数个位翻转；偶数个错，奇偶性不变，就漏掉了。It only detects an odd number of bit flips; an even number leaves parity unchanged and slips through.
  • 校验和 checksum：数据求和后重算比对，不一致说明出错；哈希值 hash 更狠，能验证文件没被篡改。Checksum: sums the data and recomputes it — a mismatch means an error; a hash goes further and verifies a file hasn't been tampered with.
  • 回显检查 echo check：接收方把数据原样发回，发送方对比是否一致。Echo check: the receiver sends the data straight back, and the sender compares it.
计算重点：给一串位问偶校验位是几——先数 1 的个数，是偶数补 0，是奇数补 1（偶校验）。它「偶数个错检测不到」是先天缺陷，考试常考。Key calculation: given bits, find the even parity bit — count the 1s; if even add 0, if odd add 1. Its "can't detect an even number of errors" weakness is a common exam point.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A parity bit is added so the number of 1s is even (or odd). Parity can only detect an odd number of bit errors — if two bits flip, the parity is unchanged. A checksum is a sum of the data that is recomputed on receipt, and a hash verifies that a file has not been altered.
例题Example
数据位是 1011011，采用偶校验（even parity），校验位应该是几？The data bits are 1011011. Using even parity, what should the parity bit be?
数 1 的个数：1、0、1、1、0、1、1 一共 5 个 1（奇数）。Count the 1s: 1,0,1,1,0,1,1 gives five 1s (odd). 偶校验要让总数变偶数，所以校验位补 1，变成 6 个 1。Even parity needs an even total, so the parity bit is 1, making 6 ones.
练习Practice
提示：先数 1 的个数。Hint: count the 1s first.

数据位是 1100101，用偶校验，校验位是几？The data bits are 1100101. Using even parity, what is the parity bit?

点开看答案Show answer
1、1、0、0、1、0、1 共 4 个 1（已是偶数），偶校验位补 0。1,1,0,0,1,0,1 has four 1s (already even), so the even parity bit is 0.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 备份与恢复 Backup and recovery full · incremental · differential · 3-2-1 全量 · 增量 · 差异 · 3-2-1
目标：分清全量/增量/差异备份，能解释恢复流程和 3-2-1 原则。Goal: tell full/incremental/differential backup apart, and explain recovery and the 3-2-1 rule.
数据丢了才想起备份就晚了。全量备份 full：每次都把整个数据拷一遍，最慢最占空间，但恢复最简单——只要一份最近的全量。增量备份 incremental：先做一次全量，之后只备上次备份之后变化的部分，最快最省空间，但恢复麻烦——要先恢复全量，再按顺序一层层叠上每次增量。差异备份 differential：先做一次全量，之后只备上次全量之后变化的部分，比增量稍慢，但恢复快——只要全量 + 最近一次差异。记住3-2-1 原则：3 份数据、存在 2 种不同介质、其中 1 份放在异地（比如云端），这样就算本地着火也不至于全没。 By the time data is gone, backing up is too late. Full backup: copies everything every time — slowest and most space-hungry, but restoring needs only the latest full. Incremental backup: one full first, then only what changed since the last backup — fastest and smallest, but restoring needs the full plus each increment in order. Differential backup: one full first, then only what changed since that full — a bit slower than incremental but faster to restore: full + latest differential. Remember the 3-2-1 rule: three copies, on two different media, with one kept offsite (like the cloud), so even a local fire won't wipe everything.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 全量 full：每次全拷；恢复最快，但最慢、最占空间。Full: copies everything; fastest to restore, but slowest and most space-hungry.
  • 增量 incremental：只备上次备份后变化的部分；最快最省，但恢复最麻烦（要按顺序叠）。Incremental: backs up changes since the last backup; fastest and smallest, but the hardest to restore (must replay in order).
  • 差异 differential：只备上次全量后变化的部分；恢复 = 全量 + 最近一次差异，比增量快。Differential: backs up changes since the last full; restore = full + latest differential, faster than incremental.
  • 3-2-1 原则：3 份、2 种介质、1 份异地；备份介质可以是磁盘/磁带，异地可以是云端。3-2-1 rule: three copies, two different media, one offsite; media can be disk/tape, offsite can be the cloud.
恢复流程别答错顺序：先找出最近可用的备份 → 恢复到一台正常机器 → 检查数据完整性 → 确认无误才重新上线。先「恢复」、再「验证」、最后「上线」。Get the recovery order right: find the latest usable backup → restore to a working machine → check integrity → go back online only once verified. Restore, then verify, then go live.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A full backup copies all data. An incremental backup copies only what changed since the last backup, while a differential backup copies what changed since the last full backup. Incremental is fastest but hardest to restore; differential is a compromise. The 3-2-1 rule means three copies, two different media, one offsite.
例题Example
某公司周一做全量备份，周二到周五做增量备份，周五硬盘坏了，恢复需要哪些文件？A company makes a full backup on Monday and incremental backups Tuesday to Friday. The disk fails on Friday. Which files are needed to restore?
需要周一的全量备份。You need Monday's full backup. 再按顺序叠加周二、周三、周四、周五每次的增量备份（假设周五增量在坏之前已完成）。Then replay Tuesday's, Wednesday's, Thursday's and Friday's increments in order (assuming Friday's completed before the failure).
练习Practice
提示：差异是相对「全量」来的。Hint: differential is measured against the full.

同样是周一全量、周二到周五备份，如果改做「差异备份」，周五恢复需要哪些文件？Same schedule — Monday full, then Tuesday-to-Friday backups — but using differential. What is needed to restore on Friday?

点开看答案Show answer
只要周一的全量 + 周五的差异备份两份，因为差异已经包含了自周一以来所有的变化，恢复比增量快。Only Monday's full + Friday's differential — the differential already contains all changes since Monday, so restoring is faster than incremental.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

第 6 单元小结Unit 6 wrap-up

这一单元讲了安全的三件事：谁在攻击（恶意软件、钓鱼、社工、DoS、内部威胁、SQL 注入），怎么防（防火墙、杀毒、认证、加密、权限、培训，一层套一层），以及怎么保证数据没坏（验证/校验、奇偶校验、校验和、哈希、备份与 3-2-1 原则）。主线只有一条：没有万能的防线，只有一层层叠加 + 时刻备份。This unit covered three sides of security: who attacks (malware, phishing, social engineering, DoS, insider threat, SQL injection), how to defend (firewall, antivirus, authentication, encryption, access rights, training — layer upon layer), and how to keep data intact (validation/verification, parity, checksum, hash, backup and the 3-2-1 rule). One thread runs through it: no single defence is enough — only layering them and always backing up.

  3. 数据隐私与法律Data privacy and the law
  4. AI 与社会伦理AI and social ethics

这一单元不考写代码，考的是「判断和表达」——记住术语、能讲道理，Paper 1 的解释题拿分就靠它。This unit tests judgement and expression, not code — remember the terms and make an argument, and Paper 1 "explain" questions become easy marks.

1 职业道德规范 Professional ethics ACM · IEEE · code of conduct ACM · IEEE · 职业规范
目标：知道软件工程师要遵守哪些职业操守，以及「举报机制」是用来干什么的。Goal: know the ethical duties of a software engineer, and what whistle-blowing is for.
医生有「希波克拉底誓言」，工程师也有——ACM（美国计算机学会）和 IEEE（电气电子工程师学会）联合制定了一套《软件工程职业道德规范》。它管的是「怎么做一个负责任的开发者」：诚实、尊重隐私、不写害人的代码、出了事不甩锅。如果发现同事在埋后门、偷数据，按规范应该先内部上报，处理不了再走 举报（whistle-blowing） 渠道——这是职业道德里「兜底」的一条。 Doctors have the Hippocratic oath, and engineers have one too — ACM and IEEE jointly wrote a Software Engineering Code of Ethics. It is about "how to be a responsible developer": be honest, respect privacy, write no harmful code, and don't dodge the consequences. If you catch a colleague planting a backdoor or stealing data, you should report it internally first, then escalate through whistle-blowing — the safety net of professional ethics.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • ACM/IEEE 职业道德准则是行业的「自律标准」，不是法律，但违反会被行业唾弃、丢饭碗。The ACM/IEEE code of conduct is professional self-regulation, not law — but breaking it can cost you your reputation and job.
  • 四条核心：诚实（不虚假宣传）、尊重隐私、不写恶意软件、为自己的代码负责。Four core duties: honesty (no false claims), respect privacy, no malware, and responsibility for your code.
  • 举报机制 whistle-blowing：发现严重违规，先内部反映；内部处理不了，再向监管机构或公众举报。Whistle-blowing: report serious misconduct internally first; if nothing is done, go to regulators or the public.
别混：职业道德和「法律」是两回事。写恶意软件违法，但「夸大产品性能」可能只算不道德、不一定违法——职业道德的网撒得比法律更早、更宽。Don't mix them up: ethics and law differ. Writing malware is illegal, but "overstating your product" may only be unethical, not illegal — the ethical net is cast earlier and wider than the law.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Professional bodies such as ACM and IEEE publish a code of conduct that requires honesty, respect for privacy, avoiding malware, and taking responsibility for one's work.
例题Example
一家公司让员工在代码里偷偷加入「悄悄收集用户数据」的功能。这违反了哪些职业道德？员工该怎么做？A company asks staff to secretly collect user data in the code. Which duties does this break, and what should an employee do?
违反了诚实和尊重隐私两条——偷偷收集不诚实，收集用户数据侵犯隐私。It breaks honesty and respect for privacy — secret collection is dishonest and invades privacy. 员工应先内部上报；若公司不理，再走举报（whistle-blowing）机制向监管机构举报。The employee should report it internally first; if ignored, use whistle-blowing to alert regulators.
练习Practice
提示：想想「自律」和「强制」的区别。Hint: think about "self-regulation" vs "enforcement".

职业道德规范和法律是一回事吗？为什么？Are a professional code of ethics and the law the same thing? Why or why not?

点开看答案Show answer
不是。职业道德是行业自律（如 ACM/IEEE 规范），由同行监督；法律由国家强制执行。违反道德不一定违法，但会被行业谴责。No. Ethics is professional self-regulation (e.g. the ACM/IEEE code), while law is enforced by the state. Unethical acts may not be illegal, but they damage your standing.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 版权与知识产权 Copyright and intellectual property open source · freeware · shareware 开源 · 免费 · 共享软件
目标：分清四种软件许可，并说清版权、专利、商标各保护什么。Goal: tell the four software licences apart, and know what copyright, patents and trademarks protect.
软件写出来就是「作品」，受知识产权保护。买软件买的其实是一份使用许可（licence），它规定你能怎么用。四种常见许可：开源（open source）源码公开、可自由修改分发，但不等于免费——作者照样能收费；免费软件（freeware）免费使用，但源码不给你看；共享软件（shareware）先让你试用，到期不付钱就停用；商业软件（commercial）付钱买授权。除了版权，还有专利保护发明、商标保护品牌名称。 Software is a "work" protected by intellectual property. Buying software really buys a licence that says how you may use it. Four common licences: open source — source public and modifiable, but not necessarily free; freeware — free to use but closed source; shareware — trial first, pay to keep using; commercial — pay for a licence. Beyond copyright, patents protect inventions and trademarks protect brand names.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 开源 open source：源码公开、可修改分发，可以收费；核心是「公开」不是「免费」。Open source: source public and modifiable, may be charged for; the point is "open", not "free".
  • 免费软件 freeware：免费使用，但闭源，不提供源码。Freeware: free to use but closed source — no source code.
  • 共享软件 shareware：先试用，到期需付费才能继续用完整功能。Shareware: trial first, pay after the trial to keep the full features.
  • 商业软件 commercial：付费购买授权，通常闭源。Commercial: pay for a licence, usually closed source.
类型Type保护什么What it protects例子Example
版权copyright作品（代码、文字、音乐等）works (code, text, music)软件源代码、歌词source code, song lyrics
专利patent发明 / 技术方案inventions / technical ideas新的加密算法a new encryption algorithm
商标trademark品牌名称 / 标志brand names / logosLogo、品牌名a logo, a brand name
最常考、最容易错：「开源一定免费」是错的。开源卖的是「源码公开 + 可修改」的自由，作者照样能收钱（比如卖技术支持、卖商业授权）。Most tested, most missed: "open source is free" is wrong. Open source sells the freedom of public, editable code — the author can still charge (e.g. for support or a commercial licence).
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Open source software makes its source code public and modifiable and may still be charged for; freeware is free but closed source, shareware is a trial that requires payment, and commercial software is paid.
例题Example
有人说「开源软件一定免费」。这句话对不对？为什么？Someone says "open-source software is always free". Is this correct? Why?
不对。开源强调「源码公开、可修改分发」，而不是「免费」。No. Open source means "public, modifiable source code", not "free of charge". 开源软件照样可以收费，比如卖技术支持；核心区别在源码是否公开。Open-source software can still be charged for, e.g. paid support; the real difference is whether the source is public.
练习Practice
提示：关键词是「试用」。Hint: the keyword is "trial".

一款软件可免费下载试用 30 天，30 天后要付费才能解锁全部功能。这属于哪种许可？A program can be downloaded and tried free for 30 days, then needs payment to unlock everything. Which licence is this?

点开看答案Show answer
是共享软件（shareware）——先免费试用，到期付费解锁。It is shareware — a free trial, then pay to unlock.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 数据隐私与法律 Data privacy and the law GDPR · data protection GDPR · 数据保护
目标：知道什么是个人数据，理解数据保护五原则，并能说出 GDPR / 个人信息保护法的要点。Goal: know what personal data is, understand the five principles, and name the key points of the GDPR / PIPL.
你的名字、电话、住址，甚至浏览记录，都是个人数据（personal data）——凡是能识别到具体某个人的信息都算。谁要收集、使用这些数据，都得守数据保护原则：合法收集、用途明确、只收最少必要的、保持准确、安全保存。欧洲有 GDPR（通用数据保护条例），中国有《个人信息保护法》，都是给数据上「紧箍咒」。公司要是泄露了用户数据，得负责、要罚款。 Your name, phone number, address, even your browsing history, are all personal data — anything that can identify a specific person. Anyone collecting or using it must follow the data protection principles: collect lawfully, state the purpose, keep only the minimum, stay accurate, store securely. Europe has the GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) and China has the Personal Information Protection Law — both put a "tight cap" on data. A company that leaks user data must answer for it and pay fines.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 个人数据：能识别到某个人的信息（姓名、电话、邮箱、位置、IP 等）。Personal data: information that identifies a person (name, phone, email, location, IP, etc.).
  • 五原则：合法收集、用途明确、最小化、准确、安全。Five principles: lawful collection, clear purpose, minimisation, accuracy, security.
  • GDPR 是欧盟的《通用数据保护条例》，中国对应的是《个人信息保护法》。The GDPR is the EU's General Data Protection Regulation; China's counterpart is the Personal Information Protection Law.
  • 数据泄露后，公司有责任尽快通知用户和监管机构，可能被重罚。After a data breach, the company must promptly notify users and regulators, and can be heavily fined.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Personal data must be collected lawfully, used only for a stated purpose, kept to the minimum, accurate, and secure, under laws such as the GDPR.
例题Example
一款 App 在没告知用户的情况下收集了大量定位数据，还转卖给广告商。违反了哪些数据保护原则？An app collects lots of location data without telling users, then sells it to advertisers. Which principles does this break?
违反合法收集（未告知、未获同意）和用途明确（转卖超出了原来的用途）。It breaks lawful collection (no notice or consent) and clear purpose (reselling goes beyond the stated use). 也违反数据最小化（收集过多），可能触犯 GDPR 或《个人信息保护法》。It also breaks minimisation (too much data), possibly violating the GDPR or the Personal Information Protection Law.
练习Practice
提示：从「只拿需要的」角度想。Hint: think "take only what is needed".

「数据最小化」是什么意思？What does "data minimisation" mean?

点开看答案Show answer
只收集完成任务所必需的最少数据，不要「顺手多收」用不到的信息。Collect only the minimum data needed for the task, not extra information you don't use.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 AI 与社会伦理 AI and social ethics bias · accountability 算法偏见 · 责任归属
目标：能说清 AI 带来的偏见、责任、就业、隐私问题，理解「技术有两面性」。Goal: explain AI's bias, accountability, employment and privacy issues, and understand that technology cuts both ways.
AI 很能干，但它不是「中立」的。如果训练数据里本身有偏见，AI 学出来的判断也会有偏见——比如招聘系统可能歧视某一类人，这叫算法偏见（algorithmic bias）。AI 出错算谁的？这叫责任归属（accountability），是个难题。它还会取代部分岗位（就业影响），也被用来大规模隐私监控。所以 AI 是「双刃剑」：用得好造福人类，用不好会伤人，需要伦理约束来「配平」。 AI is powerful, but not "neutral". If the training data is biased, the AI's judgements will be too — a hiring system may discriminate against a group; this is algorithmic bias. Who is to blame when AI errs? That is accountability, and it's hard. AI also replaces some jobs (employment impact) and enables mass surveillance. So AI is "double-edged": used well it helps, used badly it harms — it needs ethics to balance it.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 算法偏见：训练数据有偏，AI 的判断就跟着偏——歧视是「结果」不是「故意」。Algorithmic bias: biased training data leads to biased AI — the discrimination is an outcome, not an intention.
  • 责任归属：AI 做错决定（误诊、误判）时，责任在开发者、使用者还是数据方，目前仍存争议。Accountability: when AI errs (misdiagnosis, wrong decision), whether the developer, user or data provider is liable is still debated.
  • 就业影响：AI 会替代部分重复性岗位，同时也会创造新岗位。Employment impact: AI replaces some repetitive jobs while creating new ones.
  • 隐私监控：人脸识别等技术能大规模监控，需在安全与自由之间平衡。Surveillance: face recognition can monitor at scale, needing a balance between safety and freedom.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: AI can introduce algorithmic bias when training data is unrepresentative, and raises issues of accountability, employment impact, and privacy, so its use must be balanced against ethical concerns.
例题Example
某公司用一份「几乎全是男性简历」的数据训练招聘筛选 AI，结果 AI 倾向淘汰女性申请者。这反映了什么问题？A company trains a hiring AI on "almost all male" résumés, and the AI tends to reject female applicants. What problem does this show?
这是算法偏见（algorithmic bias）——训练数据有偏，导致 AI 输出歧视性结果。This is algorithmic bias — biased training data makes the AI output discriminatory results. 根源在数据，不在 AI「故意」歧视；应用多样、均衡的数据重新训练来纠正。The cause is the data, not deliberate AI discrimination; fix it by retraining on diverse, balanced data.
练习Practice
提示：想想「谁该负责」。Hint: think "who is responsible".

AI 自动驾驶汽车撞了人，责任算谁的？这属于哪类伦理问题？If a self-driving car hits someone, who is responsible? Which ethical issue is this?

点开看答案Show answer
属于责任归属（accountability）问题——责任可能在开发者、使用者或数据提供方，目前仍有争议。It is an accountability issue — the blame could fall on the developer, the user or the data provider, and is still debated.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —

第 7 单元小结Unit 7 wrap-up

这一单元讲的不是「怎么写代码」，而是「怎么像个负责任的开发者」：职业道德（诚实、尊重隐私、不写恶意软件、为后果负责）、版权（开源 ≠ 免费，分清四种许可和版权/专利/商标）、隐私（数据保护五原则 + GDPR/个人信息保护法）、AI 伦理（算法偏见、责任归属、就业、监控）。记住一条主线：技术是工具，怎么用取决于人——这也是 Paper 1 解释题的拿分关键。This unit isn't about "how to code" but "how to be a responsible developer": professional ethics (honesty, privacy, no malware, responsibility), copyright (open source ≠ free, four licences, copyright/patent/trademark), privacy (five principles + GDPR/PIPL), and AI ethics (bias, accountability, employment, surveillance). One thread runs through it: technology is a tool — how it's used is up to people, the key to Paper 1 "explain" questions.

第 8 单元 · 数据库Unit 8 · Databases Paper 1

CAIE 9618 Topic 8 · 6 站 · 关系数据库、ER 图、规范化，以及 SQLCAIE 9618 Topic 8 · 6 stops · relational databases, ER diagrams, normalisation and SQL

路线图Roadmap本单元 6 站，从「表是什么」一路写到「会建表、会查询、会改数据」6 stops, from "what a table is" to creating, querying and editing data

  1. 数据库基本概念：表、记录、字段、主键、外键Basics: table, record, field, primary key, foreign key
  2. 关系与 ER 图：一对一、一对多、多对多Relationships and ER diagrams: 1:1, 1:M, M:N
  3. 规范化 1NF / 2NF / 3NFNormalisation: 1NF / 2NF / 3NF
  4. DBMS 与 SQL 概览：DDL 与 DMLDBMS and SQL overview: DDL vs DML
  5. SQL 查询：SELECT、聚合、JOINSQL queries: SELECT, aggregates, JOIN
  6. DDL 与数据维护：建表、增删改DDL and maintenance: create, insert, update, delete

数据库是「有序地存、快速地查」的学问——先搞懂表长什么样，再学会用 SQL 指挥 DBMS 干活。Databases are about storing tidily and finding fast — learn what a table looks like, then use SQL to boss the DBMS around.

1 数据库基本概念：表、记录、字段、主键、外键 Basics: table, record, field, primary key, foreign key table · primary key · foreign key 表 · 主键 · 外键
目标：认识数据库里最基础的几个名词，并能说出「为什么不用电子表格」。Goal: learn the basic terms and say why we don't just use a spreadsheet.
数据库就像一个整理得井井有条的仓库，由很多张表（table）组成。每张表由行和列构成：一行是一条记录（record），一列是一个字段（field）。为了能精准找到某一条记录，我们给每张表指定一个主键（primary key）——它的值永远唯一、不能重复、不能为空，就像每个人的身份证号。而外键（foreign key）是另一张表的主键，用来把两张表「钩」在一起。 A database is a well-organised warehouse made of many tables. Each table is built from rows and columns: a row is a record, a column is a field. To find one exact record, we give each table a primary key — always unique, never empty, like an ID number. A foreign key is another table's primary key, used to hook two tables together.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 表 table = 相关数据的集合，由行和列组成。A table is a collection of related data, made of rows and columns.
  • 记录 record（行） = 关于一个对象的一条完整信息；字段 field（列） = 一个属性，如姓名、成绩。A record (row) is one complete piece of info about an object; a field (column) is one attribute, like name or mark.
  • 主键 primary key：唯一标识每条记录，不能重复、不能为空；外键 foreign key：引用另一张表的主键，建立联系。A primary key uniquely identifies each record (no repeats, no nulls); a foreign key references another table's primary key.
  • 为什么不用电子表格：数据库能管并发访问、权限安全、数据一致性，还能处理海量数据和复杂查询。Why not a spreadsheet: a database handles concurrent access, security, data consistency, plus huge data and complex queries.
注意：主键可以是一个 ID 字段，也可以是多个字段合起来（复合主键）；外键可以重复——因为它只是「引用」，不是「唯一」。Note: a primary key can be one ID field or several fields together (a composite key); a foreign key may repeat, since it just "references".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A table stores related data in rows and columns. A record is one row, and a field is one column. A primary key uniquely identifies each record, while a foreign key links to the primary key of another table.
例题Example
下表是学生表 Student。哪个字段最适合当主键？「姓名」为什么不行？ Below is the Student table. Which field is the best primary key, and why is "Name" unsuitable?
StudentIDNameClassMark
101Alice10A88
102Ben10A75
103Cara10B91
主键必须唯一、稳定。姓名可能重名，还可能改名，不适合当主键。A primary key must be unique and stable. Names can repeat or change, so Name is unsuitable. 因此给每个学生一个学号 StudentID，用它当主键。So give each student a StudentID and use it as the primary key.
练习Practice
提示：想想哪张表的主键会被引用。Hint: think about whose primary key gets referenced.

图书馆的借书记录表要同时关联「书」和「借阅者」，它最可能需要哪两个外键？A library's loan table links both "books" and "borrowers". Which two foreign keys does it most likely need?

点开看答案Show answer
需要两个外键：BookID（引用图书表的主键）和 MemberID（引用读者表的主键），再加一个借书日期字段。Two foreign keys: BookID (references the books table's primary key) and MemberID (references the readers table), plus a borrow-date field.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 关系与 ER 图：一对一、一对多、多对多 Relationships and ER diagrams: 1:1, 1:M, M:N entity · relationship · cardinality 实体 · 关系 · 基数
目标：画出简单的 ER 图，并分清一对一、一对多、多对多三种关系。Goal: draw a simple ER diagram and tell 1:1, 1:M and M:N apart.
现实世界里，学生「选」课程、顾客「下」订单、作者「写」书——这些都是关系（relationship）。参与关系的对象叫实体（entity）（如学生、课程），实体的特征叫属性（attribute）（如姓名、成绩）。关系有三种「配比」：一对一（1:1），如一个人一本护照；一对多（1:M），如一个班有很多学生、每个学生只属于一个班；多对多（M:N），如一个学生选很多课、一门课也有很多学生。 In the real world, students "enrol on" courses, customers "place" orders, authors "write" books — these are relationships. The objects involved are entities (students, courses), and their features are attributes (name, mark). Relationships come in three sizes: one-to-one (1:1), like one person one passport; one-to-many (1:M), like one class with many students; many-to-many (M:N), like students taking many courses and courses having many students.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 实体 entity：要存储信息的对象，画成矩形。An entity is an object to store, drawn as a rectangle.
  • 属性 attribute：实体的特征，画成椭圆，用线连到实体。An attribute is a feature of an entity, drawn as an ellipse joined by a line.
  • 关系 relationship：实体之间的联系，画成菱形；基数是 1:1、1:M、M:N 三种。A relationship links entities, drawn as a diamond; its cardinality is 1:1, 1:M or M:N.
  • 多对多无法直接落地，必须拆成「中间表 + 两个一对多」。Many-to-many cannot be stored directly; it becomes a junction table plus two one-to-many links.
注意：M:N 关系在数据库里要拆成中间表（如「选课表」），它两端各是一个一对多。Note: an M:N relationship becomes a junction table (like Enrolment) with a one-to-many at each end.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: An entity is a real-world object stored in the database, drawn as a rectangle. A relationship shows how entities are linked, drawn as a diamond. Relationships have cardinality: one-to-one, one-to-many or many-to-many.
例题Example
学生与课程是什么关系？数据库怎么实现它？What is the relationship between students and courses, and how does a database implement it?

3 规范化 1NF / 2NF / 3NF Normalisation: 1NF / 2NF / 3NF 1NF · 2NF · 3NF · redundancy 1NF · 2NF · 3NF · 冗余
目标：会判断一张表是第几范式，并能一步步把它拆到 3NF。Goal: judge which normal form a table is in, and split it to 3NF step by step.
一张表如果什么都往里塞，就会到处是冗余（重复数据）：改了一处忘了改另一处，就出异常（anomaly）。规范化（normalisation）就是把这锅「大杂烩」拆成几张只讲一件事的小表，一共三个关卡：1NF 保证每格只有一个值（原子值）、没有重复组；2NF 在 1NF 基础上消除部分依赖（非主属性不能只依赖复合主键的一部分）；3NF 在 2NF 基础上消除传递依赖（非主属性不能依赖另一个非主属性）。 If one table holds everything, it fills with redundancy (repeated data): change it in one place and forget another, and you get an anomaly. Normalisation splits this "mixed pot" into small tables each about one thing, through three gates: 1NF keeps one value per cell (atomic) with no repeating groups; 2NF removes partial dependencies; 3NF removes transitive dependencies.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 冗余的危害：改一处忘另一处 → 更新异常；删一条连累别的 → 删除异常；插不进去 → 插入异常。Redundancy hurts: forget one copy → update anomaly; delete one row and lose other info → delete anomaly; can't insert → insert anomaly.
  • 1NF：原子值、无重复组（每格一个值，没有「Product1、Product2」这种并列）。1NF: atomic values, no repeating groups (one value per cell, no "Product1, Product2" side by side).
  • 2NF：消除部分依赖——只有「复合主键」才有这个问题。2NF: remove partial dependency — only a composite key has this problem.
  • 3NF：消除传递依赖——非主属性依赖另一个非主属性。3NF: remove transitive dependency — a non-key field depending on another non-key field.
  • 口诀：1NF 拆格子，2NF 拆部分依赖，3NF 拆传递依赖。Mnemonic: 1NF splits cells, 2NF splits partial deps, 3NF splits transitive deps.
记传递依赖：A → B → C，C 其实该跟着 B 走，不该塞在这张表里，就把 B、C 单独拆出去。Transitive dependency: A → B → C — C really belongs with B, not this table, so move B and C out together.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Normalisation removes redundant data by splitting a table into smaller, well-structured tables. 1NF requires atomic values with no repeating groups, 2NF removes partial dependencies, and 3NF removes transitive dependencies.
例题Example
订单表 Order(OrderID, CustomerName, CustomerCity, ProductID, ProductName, Quantity) 规范化到 3NF。Normalise Order(OrderID, CustomerName, CustomerCity, ProductID, ProductName, Quantity) to 3NF.
1NF：让每格只有一个值，去掉重复组（如 Product1、Product2 两列拆成多行）。1NF: one value per cell, remove repeating groups (split Product1/Product2 into rows). 2NF：ProductName 只依赖 ProductID（主键 OrderID+ProductID 的一部分）→ 拆出 Product 表。2NF: ProductName depends only on ProductID (part of the key) → split out Product. 3NF：CustomerCity 依赖 CustomerName（传递依赖）→ 拆出 Customer 表。3NF: CustomerCity depends on CustomerName (transitive) → split out Customer. 最终拆成下面几张表：Final tables:
表名字段主键
OrdersOrderID, CustomerIDOrderID
OrderItemsOrderID, ProductID, QuantityOrderID + ProductID
CustomersCustomerID, CustomerName, CustomerCityCustomerID
ProductsProductID, ProductNameProductID
练习Practice
提示：先找出传递依赖。Hint: find the transitive dependency first.

表 R(StudentID, StudentName, TutorName, TutorRoom) 中，每个学生有一个导师，TutorRoom 是导师的办公室。它至少违反了几范式？怎么拆到 3NF？In R(StudentID, StudentName, TutorName, TutorRoom), each student has one tutor and TutorRoom is the tutor's office. Which normal form does it violate, and how do you split to 3NF?

点开看答案Show answer
违反 3NF：TutorRoom 传递依赖 TutorName（而 TutorName 又依赖 StudentID）。拆成 Student(StudentID, StudentName, TutorID) 和 Tutor(TutorID, TutorName, TutorRoom)。It violates 3NF: TutorRoom depends transitively on TutorName (which depends on StudentID). Split into Student(StudentID, StudentName, TutorID) and Tutor(TutorID, TutorName, TutorRoom).

4 DBMS 与 SQL 概览：DDL 与 DML DBMS and SQL overview: DDL vs DML DBMS · DDL · DML DBMS · DDL · DML
目标：说清楚 DBMS 干什么，并分清 DDL 和 DML。Goal: explain what a DBMS does, and tell DDL from DML.
DBMS（数据库管理系统）就是那套「管数据库」的软件（比如 MySQL、SQLite、Oracle）。程序不能直接伸手去硬盘里翻数据，必须通过 DBMS——它负责并发控制（很多人同时读写不乱）、安全与权限、备份与恢复、完整性（数据符合规则）。跟 DBMS 说话的语言叫 SQL，分两大类：DDL 定义「结构」（建表、改表），DML 操作「数据」（增删改查）。 A DBMS (Database Management System) is the software that runs the database (MySQL, SQLite, Oracle). Programs can't grab data straight from the disk — they must go through the DBMS, which handles concurrency, security, backup and recovery, and integrity. The language you use to talk to it is SQL, in two groups: DDL defines structure, DML works on data.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • DBMS 的职责：并发控制、安全、备份恢复、数据完整性。DBMS duties: concurrency control, security, backup and recovery, data integrity.
  • SQL = Structured Query Language，关系数据库的标准语言。SQL = Structured Query Language, the standard language for relational databases.
  • DDL（Data Definition Language）：管结构，如 CREATE、ALTER、DROP。DDL (Data Definition Language): structure — CREATE, ALTER, DROP.
  • DML（Data Manipulation Language）：管数据，如 SELECT、INSERT、UPDATE、DELETE。DML (Data Manipulation Language): data — SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE.
  • 应用 → DBMS → 数据，数据永远躲在 DBMS 后面。Application → DBMS → data; data always hides behind the DBMS.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A DBMS is software that manages databases, providing concurrency control, security, backup and recovery, and data integrity. SQL is the standard language for relational databases; DDL defines the structure while DML manipulates the data.
例题Example
判断 CREATE TABLE、ALTER TABLE、SELECT、INSERT 分别是 DDL 还是 DML？Are CREATE TABLE, ALTER TABLE, SELECT and INSERT DDL or DML?
CREATE TABLE、ALTER TABLE 定义或修改「结构」→ DDL。CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE define or change structure → DDL. SELECT、INSERT 操作「数据」→ DML。SELECT and INSERT work on data → DML.
命令类别作用
CREATE TABLEDDL建表create a table
ALTER TABLEDDL改结构change structure
SELECTDML查数据query data
INSERTDML插数据insert data
练习Practice
提示：看它动的是「结构」还是「数据」。Hint: does it change structure or data?

一条 DDL 命令改了表结构，一条 DML 命令改了表里的数据。哪个会影响「表长什么样」？One DDL command changes the structure, one DML command changes the data. Which one affects what the table looks like?

点开看答案Show answer
DDL 影响结构（表长什么样）；DML 只影响数据，不动结构。DDL affects the structure (what the table looks like); DML only changes data, not structure.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 SQL 查询：SELECT、聚合、JOIN SQL queries: SELECT, aggregates, JOIN SELECT · JOIN · GROUP BY SELECT · JOIN · GROUP BY
目标：会写基本的 SELECT 查询，会用聚合函数和 JOIN。Goal: write basic SELECT queries and use aggregate functions and JOIN.
查询就是「从表里按条件挑数据」。基本骨架是 SELECT 列 FROM 表 WHERE 条件，再加 ORDER BY 排序（ASC 升序 / DESC 降序）。要统计就上聚合函数：COUNT（数个数）、SUM（求和）、AVG（平均）、MAX（最大）、MIN（最小），配合 GROUP BY 按组统计。两张表合起来查，用 JOIN ... ON。 A query picks data from a table by condition. The skeleton is SELECT columns FROM table WHERE condition, plus ORDER BY to sort (ASC / DESC). To summarise, use aggregate functions — COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN — with GROUP BY. To combine two tables, use JOIN ... ON.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • SELECT 列 FROM 表 WHERE 条件 ORDER BY 列。SELECT columns FROM table WHERE condition ORDER BY column.
  • 聚合：COUNT、SUM、AVG、MAX、MIN；和 GROUP BY 一起按组统计。Aggregates: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN; use with GROUP BY to summarise per group.
  • JOIN：把两张表按 ON 的条件连起来；常见 INNER JOIN 只保留两边都匹配的行。JOIN links two tables on an ON condition; a common INNER JOIN keeps only rows that match on both sides.
  • WHERE 在分组前筛行，HAVING 在分组后筛组。WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after.
执行顺序：先 FROM 找到表 → WHERE 过滤 → GROUP BY 分组 → SELECT 选列 → ORDER BY 排序，记住这个顺序写题就不晕。Order of execution: FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → SELECT → ORDER BY. Remember this and queries won't confuse you.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A query uses SELECT columns FROM table WHERE condition, optionally ORDER BY a column. Aggregate functions COUNT, SUM, AVG, MAX and MIN are used with GROUP BY to summarise groups, and JOIN links two tables ON a matching condition.
例题Example

6 DDL 与数据维护：建表、增删改 DDL and maintenance: create, insert, update, delete CREATE · INSERT · UPDATE · DELETE 建表 · 插入 · 更新 · 删除
目标：会写建表语句，会用 INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE 维护数据，并知道主键、外键约束。Goal: write CREATE TABLE, maintain data with INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and know primary and foreign key constraints.
建表用 CREATE TABLE，同时把每个字段的类型、以及约束（constraint）写清楚：PRIMARY KEY（主键，唯一不空）、FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES（外键，指向别表主键）、NOT NULL、UNIQUE 等。结构要改就用 ALTER TABLE。数据维护三条：INSERT 加行、UPDATE 改行、DELETE 删行——不带 WHERE 的 UPDATE / DELETE 会动到整张表，务必小心。 Create a table with CREATE TABLE, writing each field's type and constraints: PRIMARY KEY (unique, not null), FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES (points at another table's key), NOT NULL, UNIQUE and so on. Change structure with ALTER TABLE. Maintain data with INSERT (add), UPDATE (change) and DELETE (remove) — without WHERE, UPDATE/DELETE hit the whole table, so be careful.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • CREATE TABLE 建表，写清字段类型和约束。CREATE TABLE builds a table with field types and constraints.
  • PRIMARY KEY 唯一不空；FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES 建立引用。PRIMARY KEY is unique and not null; FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES sets up the link.
  • ALTER TABLE 修改结构（加列、加约束等）。ALTER TABLE changes structure (add a column, add a constraint).
  • INSERT INTO ... VALUES 插入；UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE 更新；DELETE FROM ... WHERE 删除。INSERT INTO ... VALUES inserts; UPDATE ... SET ... WHERE updates; DELETE FROM ... WHERE deletes.
  • WHERE 一定要带，否则误伤全表。Always include WHERE, or you'll affect the whole table.
外键保证「引用的记录必须存在」——这叫参照完整性（referential integrity），DBMS 会拦下非法的插入。A foreign key guarantees the referenced record exists — called referential integrity; the DBMS rejects invalid inserts.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: CREATE TABLE defines a table with its fields and constraints such as PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY REFERENCES. INSERT adds rows, UPDATE changes rows, and DELETE removes rows; a missing WHERE clause affects the whole table.
例题Example
建一张学生表，插入一条记录，更新成绩，再删掉一条记录。Create a student table, insert a row, update a mark, then delete a row.
① 建表（DDL）：① Create the table (DDL):
CREATE TABLE Student ( StudentID INT PRIMARY KEY, Name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, Class VARCHAR(10), Mark INT );
② 插入（DML）：② Insert (DML):
INSERT INTO Student (StudentID, Name, Class, Mark) VALUES (101, 'Alice', '10A', 88);
③ 更新：把 101 号学生的 Mark 改成 90。③ Update: change student 101's Mark to 90.
UPDATE Student SET Mark = 90 WHERE StudentID = 101;
④ 删除：删掉 102 号学生。④ Delete: remove student 102.
DELETE FROM Student WHERE StudentID = 102;
⑤ 补充：带外键的选课表，StudentID 引用 Student 表。⑤ Extra: an enrolment table whose StudentID references Student.
CREATE TABLE Enrolment ( StudentID INT, CourseID INT, PRIMARY KEY (StudentID, CourseID), FOREIGN KEY (StudentID) REFERENCES Student(StudentID) );
练习Practice
提示：别忘了 WHERE。Hint: don't forget WHERE.

点开看答案Show answer
DELETE FROM Student WHERE Mark < 60;DELETE FROM Student WHERE Mark < 60;

第 8 单元小结Unit 8 wrap-up

这一单元把「怎么有序地存、快速地查」讲清了：表由记录和字段组成，主键唯一标识一行、外键把表连起来；ER 图画出实体和关系，规范化一步步消除冗余；最后用 SQL 指挥 DBMS 干活——DDL 建结构，DML 查改数据。记住一条主线：先设计好表，再写对查询，数据才不会乱。This unit covered storing tidily and finding fast: a table is records and fields, a primary key identifies a row and a foreign key links tables; ER diagrams draw entities and relationships, normalisation removes redundancy step by step; then SQL bosses the DBMS — DDL builds structure, DML queries and edits data. One thread: design the tables well, write the query right, and the data stays tidy.

本单元到此结束。数据库是 Paper 1 的重点之一，也常和 Paper 2 的编程题联动，回头要多练几遍 SQL。This is the end of the unit. Databases are a Paper 1 favourite and often pair with Paper 2 programming, so practise the SQL again later.

CAIE 9618 Topic 9 · 6 站 · 用「计算思维」把大问题拆成能写代码的小步骤CAIE 9618 Topic 9 · 6 stops · use "computational thinking" to break big problems into code-ready steps

路线图Roadmap本单元 6 站，从「计算思维」一路走到「自顶向下设计」6 stops, from computational thinking to top-down design

  1. 计算思维四要素Computational thinking — four skills
  2. 伪代码基础Pseudocode basics

这一单元是 Paper 2 的「动手」起点——不背名词，重在能把思路写成伪代码、画成结构图，为后面写程序打底。This unit is where Paper 2 gets hands-on — not memorising terms, but turning ideas into pseudocode and structure charts before you write code.

1 计算思维四要素 Computational thinking — four skills abstraction · decomposition · pattern recognition · algorithmic thinking 抽象 · 分解 · 模式识别 · 算法思维
目标：能说出计算思维的四个要素，并知道每个要素在解决实际问题时怎么用。Goal: name the four elements of computational thinking and see how each one helps solve real problems.
计算思维就是「像计算机科学家一样想问题」的一套方法，一共四招。抽象（abstraction）——做数学题时你只盯着已知条件和要求、不理会卷子上别的无关信息，这就是抽象。分解（decomposition）——写 800 字作文先列提纲、把大任务切成小段落，就是分解。模式识别（pattern recognition）——你发现「每次解方程都要先移项」这个套路，就是找规律。算法思维（algorithmic thinking）——把解法写成别人照着做也不会错的一步步，就是算法思维。 Computational thinking is a set of methods for "thinking like a computer scientist", with four moves. Abstraction — in a maths problem you focus only on the given facts and what is asked, ignoring the rest; that is abstraction. Decomposition — outlining an essay and cutting a big task into small paragraphs. Pattern recognition — noticing the same trick "move terms first" each time you solve an equation. Algorithmic thinking — writing the solution as clear steps that anyone can follow without mistakes.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 抽象：抓住关键信息、忽略无关细节（比如地图只画道路，不画每棵树）。Abstraction: keep the important details and ignore the irrelevant (a map shows roads, not every tree).
  • 分解：把复杂问题拆成更小、更好解决的子问题。Decomposition: split a complex problem into smaller, easier sub-problems.
  • 模式识别：找不同问题之间的相似之处，复用已有解法。Pattern recognition: spot similarities between problems and reuse known solutions.
  • 算法思维：设计清晰、一步步的解题步骤（可以写成伪代码）。Algorithmic thinking: design clear step-by-step instructions (which can be written as pseudocode).
小提醒：四招常常一起用——先分解再抽象，找到模式后写成算法。考试问「什么是计算思维」时，四个词各给一句解释就够。Tip: the four moves usually work together — decompose first, abstract, spot a pattern, then write the algorithm. In the exam, one line on each word is enough.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Computational thinking is the skill of solving problems by breaking them down (decomposition), focusing on the essential details (abstraction), recognising similarities with previous problems (pattern recognition), and designing step-by-step instructions (algorithmic thinking).
例题Example
把「做一顿三道菜的家宴」用计算思维分析，各要素分别对应什么？Analyse "cooking a three-dish family dinner" with computational thinking. What does each element correspond to?
分解：把家宴拆成「买菜、备菜、做三道菜、摆盘」几个子任务。Decomposition: split it into shopping, prep, cooking three dishes and plating. 抽象：抓住「多少人吃、有无忌口、预算」等关键信息，忽略「锅什么颜色」这种细节。Abstraction: keep the key facts (how many guests, allergies, budget) and ignore details like the colour of the pot. 模式识别：做红烧肉和做排骨都用到「先焯水再炖」的套路，直接复用。Pattern recognition: braised pork and ribs share the same "blanch then stew" routine — reuse it. 算法思维：写清每一步顺序——先备菜再开火，出锅前尝味。Algorithmic thinking: write the order clearly — prep before firing up, taste before serving.
练习Practice
提示：想一想你脑海里「去学校」的路线图，和真实街道比少了什么。Hint: compare the route in your head with the real street — what is missing?

你每天从家到学校，用计算思维概括一下，「抽象」体现在哪一步？In your daily walk to school, where does "abstraction" show up?

点开看答案Show answer
你脑子里只记住关键路口和转弯方向（关键信息），不会去记路边的每一棵树、每一家店（无关细节）——这就是抽象。You remember only the key junctions and turns (the essential), not every tree and shop along the way (the irrelevant) — that is abstraction.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 伪代码基础：赋值、输入输出与变量 Pseudocode basics: assignment, I/O and variables assignment · variable · input / output 赋值 · 变量 · 输入输出
目标：会用剑桥风格的伪代码写「输入 → 处理 → 输出」的顺序程序，会用 ← 赋值和 DECLARE 声明。Goal: write a "input → process → output" sequence in Cambridge-style pseudocode, using ← for assignment and DECLARE for declarations.
伪代码（pseudocode）不是真的编程语言，它是一套「人和计算机都能看懂」的草稿，用来把思路写成步骤。剑桥考试有自己的一套写法，得照着来：给变量起名、用 ← 赋值（把右边算完放进左边）、INPUT 输入、OUTPUT 输出。最朴素的程序就是「顺序结构」——像读食谱一样，从上到下一行一行执行，不拐弯。 Pseudocode is not a real programming language; it is a draft both people and computers can read, for turning ideas into steps. Cambridge has its own style you must follow: name your variables, use ← for assignment (put the right-hand value into the left), INPUT and OUTPUT. The simplest program is a "sequence" — like a recipe, top to bottom, no detours.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 赋值用 ←：Age ← 17 表示「把 17 存进变量 Age」。左边永远是变量，右边是值或算式。Assignment uses ←: Age ← 17 means "store 17 in Age". The left is always a variable, the right a value or expression.
  • 变量 = 一个有名字的「盒子」，用来存数据；用 DECLARE 声明它的类型。A variable is a named "box" that stores data; declare its type with DECLARE.
  • INPUT 从用户读入、OUTPUT 输出到屏幕；程序默认按顺序从上往下执行。INPUT reads from the user, OUTPUT writes to the screen; code runs top to bottom by default.
  • 剑桥风格：IF…THEN 写在同一行、结束写 ENDIF；循环 FOR…NEXT、WHILE…ENDWHILE、REPEAT…UNTIL。Cambridge style: IF…THEN on one line, closed with ENDIF; loops are FOR…NEXT, WHILE…ENDWHILE, REPEAT…UNTIL.
小提醒：← 不是「等于」，是「把右边放进左边」。所以 Age ← Age + 1 是合法的——先算 Age+1，再放回 Age，相当于「长大一岁」。Tip: ← is not "equals"; it means "put the right into the left". So Age ← Age + 1 is valid — compute Age+1, store it back, i.e. "grow one year older".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Pseudocode is a way of writing an algorithm in a language that is close to natural English but follows clear, consistent rules. The ← symbol means assignment: the value on the right is stored into the variable on the left.
例题Example
写一段伪代码：读入一个整数，把它加 5 后输出。Write pseudocode to read an integer, add 5, and output it.
DECLARE Num : INTEGER INPUT Num Num ← Num + 5 OUTPUT Num
先用 DECLARE 声明一个整型变量 Num。First DECLARE an integer variable Num. INPUT Num 读入；Num ← Num + 5 把原值加 5 存回。INPUT Num reads; Num ← Num + 5 adds 5 and stores it back. OUTPUT Num 打印结果。全程从上到下，这就是顺序结构。OUTPUT Num prints the result. All top to bottom — that is a sequence.
练习Practice
提示：交换两个数需要第三个「中转站」变量，避免覆盖。Hint: swapping two numbers needs a third "holding" variable so nothing is overwritten.

写伪代码：读入两个数 A、B，交换它们的值并输出。Write pseudocode to read two numbers A and B, swap their values, and output them.

点开看答案Show answer
DECLARE A, B, Temp : INTEGER INPUT A INPUT B Temp ← A A ← B B ← Temp OUTPUT A, B
先把 A 暂存到 Temp，再让 A 拿 B 的值、B 拿 Temp（原来的 A）的值，就交换了。Store A in Temp, then A takes B's value and B takes Temp (the old A) — swapped.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 选择与循环结构 Selection and iteration selection · iteration · FOR / WHILE / REPEAT 选择 · 循环 · 迭代
目标：会写 IF/CASE 的选择结构，分清 FOR、WHILE、REPEAT 三种循环并各写一段伪代码。Goal: write IF/CASE selection, tell the three loops apart and write each in pseudocode.
光会顺序执行不够——现实里要「如果怎样就怎样」，这就是选择结构（selection）；还要「同一件事反复做」，这是循环（iteration）。IF 就是「条件成立做 A，否则做 B」；CASE 是「按一个变量的不同取值走不同分支」。循环有三种：FOR 是「我已经知道要转几圈」；WHILE 是「先看条件，成立才进去，可能一次都不进」；REPEAT 是「先做一遍再说，直到条件成立才停，至少做一次」。 Sequence alone is not enough — real code needs "if this, then do that", which is selection, and "do the same thing again and again", which is iteration. IF means "do A if true, otherwise B"; CASE means "take a different branch for each value of a variable". There are three loops: FOR (you already know how many rounds), WHILE (test first — may run zero times), and REPEAT (do it once first, stop when the condition is true — runs at least once).
记住这几点：Remember:
  • IF…THEN…ELSE…ENDIF：二选一；IF 和 THEN 同行，结尾写 ENDIF。IF…THEN…ELSE…ENDIF: choose one of two; IF and THEN on the same line, closed with ENDIF.
  • CASE OF…OTHERWISE…ENDCASE：多选一，按变量取值分支。CASE OF…OTHERWISE…ENDCASE: choose one of many, branching on a variable's value.
  • FOR…NEXT 次数已知；WHILE…ENDWHILE 先判断、可能 0 次；REPEAT…UNTIL 后判断、至少 1 次。FOR…NEXT for a known count; WHILE…ENDWHILE tests first (maybe 0); REPEAT…UNTIL tests last (at least 1).
  • 判断用 =、<>、<、>、<=、>=，组合用 AND / OR / NOT。Compare with =, <>, <, >, <=, >=; combine with AND / OR / NOT.
小提醒：三种循环都能互相改写，但「用最贴切的那个」最清晰：知道次数用 FOR，可能一次都不做用 WHILE，必须先做一次用 REPEAT。Tip: the three loops can be rewritten into each other, but pick the one that fits: FOR when you know the count, WHILE when it might run zero times, REPEAT when it must run at least once.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Selection lets a program choose between branches (IF…THEN…ELSE…ENDIF, or CASE OF…ENDCASE). Iteration repeats code: a FOR loop is used when the number of repeats is known, a WHILE loop tests the condition before each pass, and a REPEAT loop tests after, so it always runs at least once.
例题Example
写伪代码：用 FOR 输出 1 到 10 的平方；再用 WHILE 写「读入数字，直到输入 0 为止」。Write pseudocode: use FOR to output 1 to 10 squared; use WHILE to read numbers until 0 is entered.
FOR i ← 1 TO 10 OUTPUT i * i NEXT i DECLARE Num : INTEGER INPUT Num WHILE Num <> 0 OUTPUT Num INPUT Num ENDWHILE
FOR 循环：i 从 1 数到 10，每圈输出 i*i，圈数已知。FOR: i runs 1 to 10, each round outputs i*i — the count is known. WHILE 循环：先读一个数，只要不是 0 就继续——先判断后执行，第一次就是 0 则一次都不进。WHILE: read once, keep going while not 0 — test first, so an initial 0 runs zero times.
练习Practice
提示：−1 是「哨兵值」；注意要先读一次才能判断，−1 不能累加进总和。Hint: −1 is a "sentinel"; you must read once before testing, and −1 must not be added.

写伪代码：读入一串数，求它们的和，直到读入 −1 停止（−1 不算进和）。Write pseudocode to read numbers and sum them until −1 is entered (−1 is not counted).

点开看答案Show answer
DECLARE Num, Total : INTEGER Total ← 0 REPEAT INPUT Num IF Num <> -1 THEN Total ← Total + Num ENDIF UNTIL Num = -1 OUTPUT Total
用 REPEAT…UNTIL 因为「至少要读入一个数」；−1 通过 IF 排除，不累加。Use REPEAT…UNTIL because at least one number must be read; −1 is excluded by the IF so it is not added.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 查找算法：线性查找与二分查找 Search: linear search and binary search linear search · binary search · O(log n) 线性查找 · 二分查找 · 复杂度
目标：会用伪代码写线性查找和二分查找，并说出两者的时间复杂度和适用条件。Goal: write linear and binary search in pseudocode, and state their complexity and when each applies.
查找（searching）就是在列表里找目标值。最老实的方法是线性查找（linear search）：从第一个元素开始，一个一个比，找到就停。它不要求列表有序，但最坏要看完整个列表。聪明一点的是二分查找（binary search）：前提是列表已经排好序，每次都和「正中间」那个比，目标更小就只看左半边、更大就看右半边，一次砍掉一半，所以特别快。代价就是——必须先排序。 Searching means finding a target in a list. The honest way is linear search: start at the first item and compare one by one until found. It needs no sorting but may scan the whole list. The clever way is binary search: the list must already be sorted; each time compare with the middle, look left if the target is smaller or right if larger, halving the space — very fast. The price: you must sort first.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 线性查找：逐个比较，最坏 O(n)；列表无需有序，元素少时简单直接。Linear search: check each in turn, worst case O(n); no sorting needed, simple for small lists.
  • 二分查找：先排序，每次与中间元素比较并砍半，复杂度 O(log n)。Binary search: sort first, compare the middle and halve each time, complexity O(log n).
  • 二分查找要求数据有序、能随机访问（如数组）；线性查找对任何列表都适用。Binary search needs sorted data with random access (e.g. an array); linear search works on any list.
  • n 个元素二分查找最多约 log₂n 次比较（1024 个只要 10 次左右）。Binary search needs at most about log₂n comparisons for n items (1024 items ≈ 10).
小提醒：记忆口诀——线性「从头到尾扫」，二分「先排序、砍一半」。考试常问「为什么二分更快」，答案就是 O(log n) 对比 O(n)。Tip: remember — linear "scans front to back", binary "sort first, then halve". Exam questions often ask why binary is faster: O(log n) versus O(n).
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Linear search checks each item in turn and works on any list, but takes O(n) time in the worst case. Binary search needs a sorted list, repeatedly compares the middle item and halves the search space, giving O(log n) time.
例题Example
分别写线性查找和二分查找的伪代码，在有序数组 [2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38] 里找 23。Write pseudocode for both linear and binary search, finding 23 in the sorted array [2, 5, 8, 12, 16, 23, 38].
// 线性查找：逐个比 FOR i ← 1 TO 7 IF Arr[i] = Target THEN OUTPUT i ENDIF NEXT i // 二分查找：先排序，每次砍半 DECLARE Low, High, Mid, Found : INTEGER Low ← 1 High ← 7 Found ← FALSE WHILE Low <= High AND Found = FALSE Mid ← (Low + High) DIV 2 IF Arr[Mid] = Target THEN Found ← TRUE ELSE IF Arr[Mid] < Target THEN Low ← Mid + 1 ELSE High ← Mid - 1 ENDIF ENDIF ENDWHILE IF Found = TRUE THEN OUTPUT Mid ENDIF
线性查找：从头到尾逐个比，最坏要看完全部 7 个，是 O(n)。Linear search: compare front to back; worst case scans all 7, that is O(n). 二分查找：Low=1、High=7，Mid=(1+7) DIV 2=4，Arr[4]=12 小于 23，去右半边，Low=5。Binary search: Low=1, High=7, Mid=(1+7) DIV 2=4, Arr[4]=12 < 23, so Low=5 (right half). Mid=(5+7) DIV 2=6，Arr[6]=23 命中，只比了 2 次——这就是 O(log n)。Mid=(5+7) DIV 2=6, Arr[6]=23 — found after just 2 comparisons, that is O(log n).
练习Practice
提示：每次算中间下标，看是命中还是砍半。Hint: compute the middle index each time; see if it hits or halves.

在有序数组 [1, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18] 里用二分查找找 6，共比较几次？Using binary search on [1, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18] to find 6, how many comparisons are needed?

点开看答案Show answer
Mid = (1+6) DIV 2 = 3，Arr[3] = 6 直接命中，所以比较 1 次。Mid = (1+6) DIV 2 = 3, Arr[3] = 6 — a direct hit, so 1 comparison.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 排序算法：冒泡排序与插入排序 Sorting: bubble sort and insertion sort bubble sort · insertion sort · O(n²) 冒泡排序 · 插入排序
目标：会用冒泡排序和插入排序，能对 [5,2,9,1,6] 逐步演示，并知道冒泡每轮把最大「冒」到最后。Goal: use bubble and insertion sort, trace them on [5,2,9,1,6], and see how each pass bubbles the largest to the end.
排序（sorting）就是把一堆数据从小到大（或从大到小）排好，是查找和很多算法的基础。冒泡排序（bubble sort）最形象：相邻两个两两比较，谁大谁往后换，像气泡一样，每轮把当前最大的那个「冒」到最后面，下一轮就不用再管它。插入排序（insertion sort）像打扑克牌理牌：每摸一张新牌，就把它插到手里已经排好的那摞牌的正确位置。n 个元素的冒泡最坏要 O(n²) 次比较。 Sorting puts data into ascending (or descending) order, and underlies searching and many algorithms. Bubble sort is the most vivid: compare each adjacent pair and swap the larger one back, like bubbles — each pass floats the current largest to the end, which is then skipped. Insertion sort is like sorting playing cards: take each new card and insert it into its correct place among the cards you already hold. n items take O(n²) comparisons in the worst case.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 冒泡排序：相邻两两比较交换，每轮把最大（或最小）元素送到末尾；最坏/平均 O(n²)。Bubble sort: compare and swap adjacent pairs, sending the largest (or smallest) to the end each pass; worst/average O(n²).
  • 插入排序：维护一个「已排序」前缀，把下一个元素插入正确位置；平均 O(n²)，接近有序时接近 O(n)。Insertion sort: keep a sorted prefix and insert the next item in place; average O(n²), close to O(n) when nearly sorted.
  • 冒泡每轮少比较一个（末尾已排好）；插入排序适合「数据基本有序」或「边输入边排」。Bubble compares one fewer each pass (the tail is done); insertion suits nearly-sorted or streaming data.
  • 两者都是原地排序（不需要额外的大数组）。Both are in-place (no extra large array needed).
小提醒：冒泡「越排越安静」——每轮末尾固定一个最大值，所以第 2 轮比第 1 轮少比一次。Tip: bubble gets quieter each pass — one more maximum is fixed at the tail, so pass 2 compares once fewer than pass 1.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Bubble sort repeatedly compares adjacent items and swaps them if they are in the wrong order; each pass moves the largest remaining value to the end. Insertion sort builds a sorted section by inserting each new item into its correct position. Both are O(n²) in the average case.
例题Example
用冒泡排序排 [5, 2, 9, 1, 6]，写出第一轮过程和最终结果。Bubble-sort [5, 2, 9, 1, 6]; write pass 1 and the final result.
DECLARE Arr : ARRAY[1:5] OF INTEGER DECLARE n, i, j, Temp : INTEGER n ← 5 FOR i ← 1 TO n - 1 FOR j ← 1 TO n - i IF Arr[j] > Arr[j+1] THEN Temp ← Arr[j] Arr[j] ← Arr[j+1] Arr[j+1] ← Temp ENDIF NEXT j NEXT i
第一轮：5↔2 换 → [2,5,9,1,6]；5<9 不换；9↔1 换 → [2,5,1,9,6]；9↔6 换 → [2,5,1,6,9]，最大 9 冒到最后。Pass 1: swap 5↔2 → [2,5,9,1,6]; keep 5<9; swap 9↔1 → [2,5,1,9,6]; swap 9↔6 → [2,5,1,6,9] — largest 9 bubbles to the end. 继续几轮后得到 [1,2,5,6,9]。共需 4 轮，最坏 4+3+2+1=10 次比较。Further passes give [1,2,5,6,9]. That is 4 passes, worst case 4+3+2+1=10 comparisons.
练习Practice
提示：第一轮把最大送到最后，第二轮只处理前面三个。Hint: pass 1 sends the largest to the end; pass 2 only works on the first three.

用冒泡排序排 [3, 1, 4, 2]，第二轮结束时数组是什么样？Bubble-sorting [3, 1, 4, 2], what does the array look like at the end of pass 2?

点开看答案Show answer
第一轮：[3,1,4,2]→[1,3,4,2]（3↔1）→[1,3,4,2]（3<4）→[1,3,2,4]（4↔2）；第二轮处理前三个 [1,3,2]→[1,3,2]（1<3）→[1,2,3]（3↔2），此时数组为 [1,2,3,4]。Pass 1: [3,1,4,2]→[1,3,4,2] (3↔1)→[1,3,4,2] (3<4)→[1,3,2,4] (4↔2). Pass 2 works on the first three [1,3,2]→[1,3,2] (1<3)→[1,2,3] (3↔2), giving [1,2,3,4].
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 自顶向下设计与逐步求精 Top-down design and stepwise refinement top-down design · stepwise refinement 自顶向下设计 · 逐步求精
目标：会用结构图把大问题自顶向下拆成子任务，并对每个子任务用伪代码逐步细化。Goal: break a big problem top-down into sub-tasks with a structure chart, then refine each into pseudocode.
大程序没法一口气写完，得「自顶向下设计（top-down design）」：先把总任务画成一棵倒过来的树，最上面是总目标，下面一层层拆成子任务，一直拆到每个小任务都简单到能直接写代码。这个把大任务不断「变具体」的过程叫逐步求精（stepwise refinement）。它让大问题变得清晰、好分工、好测试，是结构化编程的看家本领。 A big program cannot be written in one go. Top-down design draws the task as an upside-down tree: the goal at the top, split layer by layer into sub-tasks until each one is simple enough to code. Repeatedly making a task more concrete is stepwise refinement. It keeps large problems clear, easy to split up and easy to test — the bread and butter of structured programming.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 自顶向下设计 = 从总目标开始，逐层分解成子任务，直到每块都容易实现。Top-down design = start from the goal and split into sub-tasks until each is easy to build.
  • 逐步求精 = 先用文字/结构图描述，再不断细化成伪代码、最终代码。Stepwise refinement = describe in words/a chart first, then keep refining into pseudocode and finally code.
  • 好处：逻辑清晰、便于分工协作、每块可单独测试、容易定位错误。Benefits: clear logic, easy to share the work, each part testable on its own, easy to find bugs.
  • 子任务之间尽量独立（低耦合），每个子任务只做一件事。Keep sub-tasks as independent as possible (low coupling); each does one job.
小提醒：判断「拆到位没有」的标准：每个子任务能不能一句话说清、并且直接写成一小段伪代码。能，就停。Tip: to know you have split enough, check whether each sub-task can be stated in one sentence and written as a short block of pseudocode. If so, stop.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Top-down design breaks a large problem into smaller sub-tasks, each refined again until every part is simple enough to code. Stepwise refinement means starting with a broad outline and repeatedly making each step more detailed.
例题Example
用自顶向下设计拆解「算平均分并找最高分」，并把每个子任务细化成伪代码。Use top-down design to break "calculate the average and find the highest mark" into sub-tasks, and refine each into pseudocode.
PROCEDURE CalculateAverage Total ← 0 FOR i ← 1 TO n Total ← Total + Marks[i] NEXT i Average ← Total / n OUTPUT Average ENDPROCEDURE PROCEDURE FindHighest Highest ← Marks[1] FOR i ← 2 TO n IF Marks[i] > Highest THEN Highest ← Marks[i] ENDIF NEXT i OUTPUT Highest ENDPROCEDURE
顶层任务「统计成绩」拆成两个子任务：算平均分、找最高分。The top task "process marks" splits into two sub-tasks: find average and find highest. 每个子任务再细化：算平均分 = 累加 n 个分数再除以 n；找最高分 = 假设第一个最高，逐个比。Refine each: average = sum n marks then divide by n; highest = assume the first is max, compare the rest. 分别用 PROCEDURE…ENDPROCEDURE 封装，主程序依次调用即可。Wrap each in PROCEDURE…ENDPROCEDURE; the main program calls them in turn.
练习Practice
提示：先拆成「算面积」和「判断是否正方形」两块。Hint: split into "calculate area" and "check if square".

把「计算长方形面积并判断是否正方形」拆成子任务，并写出判断部分的伪代码。Break "calculate a rectangle's area and check if it is a square" into sub-tasks, and write the check in pseudocode.

点开看答案Show answer
IF Length = Width THEN OUTPUT "square" ELSE OUTPUT "not a square" ENDIF
拆成两个子任务：① 算面积 Area ← Length * Width；② 判断是否正方形（比较长宽是否相等），各自独立。Split into two sub-tasks: ① area Area ← Length * Width; ② check square by comparing Length and Width — each independent.
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

第 9 单元小结Unit 9 wrap-up

这一单元把「怎么把一个模糊的大问题，变成能写代码的精确步骤」这条主线走通了：先靠计算思维（抽象、分解、模式识别、算法思维）想清楚，再用伪代码的三种结构（顺序、选择、循环）表达，查数据用查找算法、整理数据用排序算法，最后用自顶向下设计把大工程拆小。This unit walked the main thread of turning a vague big problem into precise, code-ready steps: think it through with computational thinking (abstraction, decomposition, pattern recognition, algorithmic thinking), express it in pseudocode's three structures (sequence, selection, iteration), find data with search algorithms, tidy data with sorting algorithms, and finally split the project with top-down design.

这一单元是 Paper 2 的「地基」——写程序时你每声明一个变量、每挑一种结构，都在用今天讲的这些东西。栈、队列、链表更是面试和考试反复出现的三种经典结构。This unit is the foundation for Paper 2 — every variable you declare and every structure you choose uses what is covered here. Stacks, queues and linked lists are three classic structures that keep coming up in exams and interviews.

1 六种基本数据类型 Six basic data types INTEGER · REAL · CHAR · STRING · BOOLEAN · DATE 整数 · 实数 · 字符 · 字符串 · 布尔 · 日期
目标：认识六种内置数据类型，会写变量声明，并说清「为什么要分类型」。Goal: know the six built-in types, write declarations, and explain why we need types at all.
想象学校的储物柜：每个格子贴了标签，有的放鞋、有的放书、有的放乐器——放错位置会出乱子。计算机的内存也一样，存东西之前得先告诉它「这一格放的是什么」。这就是数据类型（data type）：它规定了变量能存哪种值、占多少内存、能做哪些运算。整数和整数能加减乘除，字符串和字符串能拼在一起，但「年龄 + 名字」就说不通。 Think of school lockers: each has a label — some for shoes, some for books, some for instruments — and putting things in the wrong place causes chaos. Computer memory is the same: before storing something you must tell it "what goes in this slot". That is a data type: it says what kind of value a variable holds, how much memory it takes and which operations make sense. Integers add and multiply, strings join together, but "age + name" is nonsense.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • INTEGER 整数（无小数点）、REAL 实数（带小数点）、CHAR 单个字符、STRING 一串字符、BOOLEAN 只有 TRUE/FALSE、DATE 日期。INTEGER (no decimal point), REAL (has a decimal point), CHAR (one character), STRING (a run of characters), BOOLEAN (only TRUE/FALSE), DATE.
  • 为什么分类型：① 决定占多少内存；② 决定能做的操作（数字能算、字符串能拼、布尔能判断）。Why types: (1) how much memory to use; (2) which operations are allowed (numbers calculate, strings join, booleans test).
  • 声明语法：DECLARE 名字 : 类型，比如 DECLARE Age : INTEGER。Declaration syntax: DECLARE name : type, e.g. DECLARE Age : INTEGER.
  • 类型不匹配会报错：数字和字符串不能直接相加，得先转换。Mismatched types cause errors: you cannot add a number and a string without converting first.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A data type defines the kind of value a variable can hold and the operations that can be performed on it. Declaring a variable's type tells the computer how much memory to reserve.
例题Example
写三个声明语句：Age 是整数，Name 是字符串，Score 是实数。Write three declarations: Age is an integer, Name is a string, Score is a real.
DECLARE Age : INTEGER DECLARE Name : STRING DECLARE Score : REAL
整数用 INTEGER，字符串用 STRING，实数用 REAL。Integer is INTEGER, string is STRING, real is REAL. 冒号前面是变量名，后面是类型——这是剑桥伪代码的标准写法。The name goes before the colon, the type after — that is standard Cambridge pseudocode.
练习Practice
提示：想一想「只有两种可能」的答案是什么类型。Hint: what type has only two possible values?

变量 IsRainy 要存「今天是否下雨」，该声明为什么类型？写出声明语句。A variable IsRainy stores "whether it rains today". What type is it? Write the declaration.

点开看答案Show answer
是 BOOLEAN，因为只有 TRUE / FALSE 两种值：DECLARE IsRainy : BOOLEAN。BOOLEAN, since there are only two values, TRUE / FALSE: DECLARE IsRainy : BOOLEAN.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 记录 RECORD：把不同类型字段打包 Records: bundling different-typed fields RECORD · TYPE · field access 记录 · 类型 · 字段访问
目标：会用 RECORD 把不同类型字段打包成一个类型，并用「点字段」访问。Goal: bundle different-typed fields into a record type and access them with a dot.
一个学生有名字（文字）、年龄（整数）、成绩（实数）——三样不同类型，却是同一个人。分开存会散成一地，记录（RECORD） 就是一张「个人档案卡」，把这些字段打包成一个整体。定义好之后，用 点号 就能取到某个字段，像翻开档案卡找到某一栏。 A student has a name (text), an age (integer) and a score (real) — three different types, yet one person. Storing them separately scatters them everywhere; a record is one "profile card" that packs the fields into a whole. Once defined, a dot reaches any field, like flipping to one column on the card.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • RECORD 是复合类型：一个记录包含多个字段，字段类型可以不同。A record is a composite type: one record holds several fields, whose types may differ.
  • 定义用 TYPE ... ENDTYPE；访问用点号：Student.Name、Student.Age。Define it with TYPE ... ENDTYPE; access a field with a dot: Student.Name, Student.Age.
  • 用途：一条数据库记录、一个员工档案、一份学生成绩——天然是一组相关字段。Used for: a database row, an employee profile, a student result — naturally a set of related fields.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A record is a composite data type that groups related fields of possibly different types under one name. Each field is accessed using a dot, for example Student.Name.
例题Example
定义学生记录 Student（含 Name、Age、Score 三个字段），并把 S1 的名字设为 "Alex"。Define a Student record (fields Name, Age, Score) and set S1's name to "Alex".
TYPE Student DECLARE Name : STRING DECLARE Age : INTEGER DECLARE Score : REAL ENDTYPE DECLARE S1 : Student S1.Name <- "Alex"
TYPE 块里列出所有字段及其类型，ENDTYPE 收尾。The TYPE block lists every field with its type, closed by ENDTYPE. 声明一个 Student 类型的变量 S1，用 S1.Name <- "Alex" 给字段赋值。Declare S1 of type Student, then assign S1.Name <- "Alex".
练习Practice
提示：字段访问用「记录名.字段名」。Hint: access a field as record.field.

给 S1 的 Age 字段赋值为 16、Score 赋值为 92.5，写出两条语句。Assign 16 to S1's Age and 92.5 to its Score. Write the two statements.

点开看答案Show answer
S1.Age <- 16 和 S1.Score <- 92.5。S1.Age <- 16 and S1.Score <- 92.5.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 数组：一排格子和一张表格 Arrays: one row and a grid ARRAY · index from 1 · row-major 数组 · 索引从 1 · 行优先
目标：会用一维/二维数组存数据，知道索引从 1 开始，会写遍历循环。Goal: store data in 1D/2D arrays, know indices start at 1, and write a traversal loop.
数组（array）就是一排贴了编号的格子，能一口气存很多同类型的值，像宿舍楼的储物柜：1 号柜、2 号柜……注意编号从 1 开始，不是 0（这和很多真语言如 Python 不一样，考试按剑桥规则来）。一维是一条线，二维就是一张表格（行和列），存成绩表、棋盘、像素图都靠它。 An array is a row of numbered slots that store many values of the same type, like dorm lockers: locker 1, locker 2 ... Note the numbering starts at 1, not 0 (unlike real languages such as Python — the exam follows Cambridge rules). A 1D array is a line; a 2D array is a table of rows and columns, used for mark sheets, chess boards and pixel images.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 声明：DECLARE Scores : ARRAY[1:10] OF INTEGER，索引从 1 到 10。Declaration: DECLARE Scores : ARRAY[1:10] OF INTEGER, indices 1 to 10.
  • 二维：DECLARE Grid : ARRAY[1:3, 1:4] OF INTEGER，先写行再写列；Grid[2,3] 是第 2 行第 3 列。2D: DECLARE Grid : ARRAY[1:3, 1:4] OF INTEGER, rows then columns; Grid[2,3] is row 2, column 3.
  • 遍历用 FOR Index <- 1 TO 10 ... NEXT Index。Traverse with FOR Index <- 1 TO 10 ... NEXT Index.
  • 二维数组按行优先顺序存进内存（一行一行排）。A 2D array is stored in row-major order (row by row).
最容易扣分的坑：把索引 0 当成第一个元素。剑桥伪代码里数组下标从 1 开始，做题先看清题目给的数组范围。The classic trap: treating index 0 as the first element. In Cambridge pseudocode subscripts start at 1 — always check the range given in the question.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: An array is a collection of elements of the same data type, accessed by an index. In Cambridge pseudocode, array indices start at 1. A two-dimensional array has rows and columns and is stored in row-major order.
例题Example
声明一个 3 行 4 列的二维数组 Grid，并把第 2 行第 3 列设为 7。Declare a 3-by-4 two-dimensional array Grid, and set row 2, column 3 to 7.
DECLARE Grid : ARRAY[1:3, 1:4] OF INTEGER Grid[2, 3] <- 7
ARRAY[1:3, 1:4] 表示 3 行、4 列。ARRAY[1:3, 1:4] means 3 rows and 4 columns. Grid[2, 3] 是第 2 行第 3 列（先写行，再写列），索引都从 1 起。Grid[2, 3] is row 2, column 3 (row first, then column), with indices starting at 1.
练习Practice
提示：用 FOR 循环，索引从 1 到 5，累加到 Total。Hint: use a FOR loop, index 1 to 5, adding into Total.

数组 Scores[1:5] 已存好数，用伪代码把五个元素的和放进 Total。Scores[1:5] is already filled. Write pseudocode that puts the sum of its five elements into Total.

点开看答案Show answer
Total <- 0 FOR I <- 1 TO 5 Total <- Total + Scores[I] NEXT I
先清零 Total，再让 I 从 1 走到 5，每次把 Scores[I] 加进去。Start Total at 0, then let I run 1 to 5, adding Scores[I] each time.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 文件：文本/二进制与打开读写关闭 Files: text vs binary and open-read-write-close OPENFILE · READFILE · WRITEFILE · CLOSEFILE 打开 · 读 · 写 · 关闭
目标：分清文本/二进制文件、顺序/随机访问，会写打开→读/写→关闭的伪代码。Goal: tell text from binary files and sequential from random access, and write open-read/write-close pseudocode.
文件（file）是数据长期保存的地方——程序一关，内存里的变量就没了，只有写进文件才留得住。文件分两种：文本文件存的是能直接读的字符；二进制文件存的是原始字节，人看不懂、程序能懂。读文件有两种姿势：顺序访问像听磁带，只能从头挨着放；随机访问像点歌，想听哪首直接跳过去。 A file is where data lives long-term — close the program and memory variables vanish; only what is written to a file survives. Files come in two kinds: text files store readable characters, while binary files store raw bytes that humans can't read but programs can. Reading has two modes: sequential access is like a cassette, only played from the start; random access is like skipping straight to a song.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 文本文件存字符（人能读）；二进制文件存原始字节（人读不懂、程序能读）。Text files store readable characters; binary files store raw bytes that only programs can read.
  • 顺序访问只能从头依次读；随机访问能直接跳到任意位置。Sequential access reads in order from the start; random (direct) access jumps straight to any position.
  • 四步：OPENFILE（打开）→ READFILE/WRITEFILE（读写）→ CLOSEFILE（关闭）。Four steps: OPENFILE → READFILE/WRITEFILE → CLOSEFILE.
  • 用完一定要关闭，否则数据可能没写完、或一直占用资源。Always close the file, or data may be lost and resources stay locked.
判断题常考：「随机访问一定比顺序访问快吗？」——只有需要频繁跳来跳去时才快；顺序读一大段反而差不多，还更简单。Exam favourite: "Is random access always faster?" — only when you keep jumping around; for reading a long run, sequential is just as good and simpler.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Text files store human-readable characters, while binary files store raw bytes. Sequential access reads from the beginning in order, whereas random access can jump to any position. A file must be opened before use and closed afterwards.
例题Example
写伪代码，逐行读文件 scores.txt 并输出每一行，直到文件结束。Write pseudocode to read scores.txt line by line and output each line until the end of file.
OPENFILE "scores.txt" FOR READ READFILE "scores.txt", Line WHILE NOT EOF("scores.txt") OUTPUT Line READFILE "scores.txt", Line ENDWHILE CLOSEFILE "scores.txt"
先 OPENFILE 打开，再读第一行。Open with OPENFILE, then read the first line. 用 WHILE 判断是否到文件尾（EOF），每读一行就输出。Use WHILE to check for end-of-file (EOF), outputting each line read. 循环结束后 CLOSEFILE 关闭文件。After the loop, close the file with CLOSEFILE.
练习Practice
提示：顺序读 = 从头开始；随机读 = 直接跳到某条记录。Hint: sequential reads from the start; random jumps straight to a record.

读一本 1 万条记录的文件，只想看第 5000 条。用顺序访问还是随机访问更好？为什么？A file holds 10 000 records and you only want record 5000. Is sequential or random access better, and why?

点开看答案Show answer
随机访问更好。顺序访问要挨个读前 4999 条；随机访问能直接跳到第 5000 条，快得多。Random access is better: sequential would read through the first 4999 records first, while random jumps straight to record 5000, much faster.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 栈 Stack：后进先出 Stacks: last in, first out LIFO · push · pop · top pointer 后进先出 · 压入 · 弹出 · 栈顶指针
目标：理解栈的后进先出，会 push/pop，知道栈顶指针，能说出它的应用。Goal: understand LIFO, do push/pop, know the top pointer, and name where stacks are used.
栈（stack）就像一摞盘子：只能从最上面拿、也只能往最上面放，最下面的盘子最晚才能碰到。这叫后进先出（LIFO，Last In First Out）。往里放叫 push（压入），往外拿叫 pop（弹出）。计算机里到处是栈：你按「撤销」就是弹出一个操作，函数一层层调用也靠栈记着「该回到哪一行」。 A stack is like a pile of plates: you can only take from the top and only add to the top, so the bottom plate is reached last. This is last in, first out (LIFO). Adding is push, taking off is pop. Stacks are everywhere: pressing "undo" pops an operation, and nested function calls use a stack to remember which line to return to.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 栈：LIFO，只能在一端（栈顶）进出。A stack is LIFO, entering and leaving only at one end (the top).
  • push 压入栈顶；pop 从栈顶弹出。push adds to the top; pop removes from the top.
  • 用数组实现：一个 Stack[1:n] 数组 + 一个栈顶指针 Top 记录当前位置。Implement with an array: a Stack[1:n] plus a top pointer holding the current top position.
  • 应用：函数调用栈、撤销（undo）操作、括号匹配。Uses: function call stack, undo operations, bracket matching.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A stack is a last-in-first-out (LIFO) data structure. Items are added by pushing onto the top and removed by popping from the top. It is used for function calls and undo operations.
例题Example
用数组实现栈，写出 Push 和 Pop 两个过程的伪代码。Implement a stack with an array, writing the Push and Pop procedures.
DECLARE Stack : ARRAY[1:10] OF INTEGER DECLARE Top : INTEGER Top <- 0 PROCEDURE Push(Value : INTEGER) Top <- Top + 1 Stack[Top] <- Value ENDPROCEDURE PROCEDURE Pop() Top <- Top - 1 ENDPROCEDURE
Top 指向当前栈顶；压入时先 Top <- Top + 1，再把值放进 Stack[Top]。Top points at the current top; to push, first Top <- Top + 1, then store the value in Stack[Top]. 弹出时 Top <- Top - 1，栈顶元素就被「丢弃」了（下次压入会覆盖它）。To pop, Top <- Top - 1; the top element is discarded (the next push overwrites it).
练习Practice
提示：栈是后进先出，想想「最后放进去的是哪个」。Hint: it's LIFO — think about which item went in last.

依次 push 5、push 3、pop、push 8、pop。第一次 pop 出来的是几？最后栈顶是几？Do: push 5, push 3, pop, push 8, pop. What does the first pop return, and what is left on top?

点开看答案Show answer
第一次 pop 出 3（最后压入的）。之后 push 8、再 pop 出 8，栈顶回到 5。The first pop returns 3 (the last pushed). Then push 8 and pop returns 8, leaving 5 on top.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 队列 Queue 与链表 Linked list Queues and linked lists FIFO · enqueue · dequeue · node · pointer 先进先出 · 入队 · 出队 · 节点 · 指针
目标：理解队列 FIFO 和链表结构，说清链表与数组的优劣。Goal: understand FIFO queues and the linked-list structure, and compare them with arrays.
队列（queue）像食堂排队打饭：先来的先打、后来的排在后面，叫先进先出（FIFO）。入队（enqueue）在队尾，出队（dequeue）在队头。链表（linked list）则是另一套思路：不用一整块连续格子，而是每个节点里装两样东西——数据和指向下一个节点的指针。想在中途插一个节点，只要改两根指针，不用像数组那样把后面元素全都往后挪。 A queue is like a canteen line: first come, first served — first in, first out (FIFO). Enqueue adds at the rear, dequeue removes from the front. A linked list takes a different approach: instead of one solid block of cells, each node holds two things — its data and a pointer to the next node. To insert in the middle you only change two pointers; there is no shifting of later elements as in an array.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 队列：FIFO，enqueue 在队尾加入，dequeue 在队头移除。Queue: FIFO, enqueue adds at the rear, dequeue removes at the front.
  • 链表节点 = 数据 + 指向下一节点的指针；最后一个节点的指针是 NULL。A linked-list node = data + a pointer to the next node; the last node's pointer is NULL.
  • 链表插入/删除（已知位置）只需改指针，是 O(1)；数组要移动元素，是 O(n)。Inserting/deleting in a linked list (position known) only changes pointers — O(1); an array must shift elements — O(n).
  • 数组能随机访问（按下标直接取），链表要从头逐个找。Arrays support random access (direct by index); linked lists must be searched from the head.
考试最爱问「什么时候用谁」：频繁在中间增删 → 链表；经常按下标查 → 数组。The favourite "which to use" question: frequent mid-insert/delete → linked list; frequent index lookup → array.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A queue is a first-in-first-out (FIFO) structure: items are enqueued at the rear and dequeued from the front. A linked list stores each item in a node containing data and a pointer to the next node, so insertion and deletion do not require shifting other elements.
例题Example
用数组实现队列，写出 enqueue 和 dequeue 的关键步骤。Implement a queue with an array, writing the key enqueue and dequeue steps.
DECLARE Queue : ARRAY[1:10] OF INTEGER DECLARE Front, Rear : INTEGER Front <- 1 Rear <- 0 // enqueue：从队尾加入 Rear <- Rear + 1 Queue[Rear] <- Value // dequeue：从队头取出 Item <- Queue[Front] Front <- Front + 1
enqueue 时 Rear 加 1，把值放进 Queue[Rear]（队尾）。To enqueue, add 1 to Rear and store the value in Queue[Rear] (the rear). dequeue 时从 Queue[Front] 取值，Front 加 1（队头后移）。To dequeue, take Queue[Front], then add 1 to Front (the front moves on).
练习Practice
提示：数组插中间要把后面的全往后挪；链表只要改两根指针。Hint: an array shifts everything after the middle; a linked list just changes two pointers.

在 1000 个元素的中间插入一个新元素，数组和链表（已知插入位置）分别要动多少元素？Inserting a new element in the middle of 1000 elements — how many elements must an array move, versus a linked list (position known)?

点开看答案Show answer
数组要移动后面的约 500 个元素（O(n)）；链表只需改指针，不动其他元素（O(1)）。The array must move about 500 elements (O(n)); the linked list only changes pointers, moving nothing else (O(1)).
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

第 10 单元小结Unit 10 wrap-up

这一单元讲了数据的两件事：怎么分类（INTEGER / REAL / CHAR / STRING / BOOLEAN / DATE）和怎么组织（记录、数组、文件，以及栈、队列、链表三种结构）。记住两条主线：栈是后进先出、队列是先进先出；链表靠指针连接，插入删除快但查找慢，数组正好相反。This unit covered two sides of data: how to classify it (INTEGER / REAL / CHAR / STRING / BOOLEAN / DATE) and how to organise it (records, arrays, files, plus stacks, queues and linked lists). Keep two threads in mind: a stack is LIFO, a queue is FIFO; and a linked list is joined by pointers — fast to insert/delete, slow to search — while an array is the opposite.
