1 变量、常量与运算符 Variables, constants and operators variable · CONSTANT · operator 变量 · 常量 · 运算符
目标：会用 ← 声明并赋值变量，会用 CONSTANT 定义常量，分清三类运算符和它们的优先级。Goal: declare and assign variables with ←, define constants with CONSTANT, and tell the three operator groups and their precedence apart.
变量就像贴了标签的储物盒，你可以随时把新东西放进去、把旧的拿出来看；常量则像门牌号，一旦定下就不许改。往盒子里放东西这个动作叫赋值，用 ← 表示——注意箭头是从右往左，意思是「把右边的值装进左边的盒子」。而运算符就是对这些盒子里的数做加工的「动作」：算出来、比大小、拼条件。 A variable is a labelled storage box — you can put new things in and read the old ones out anytime; a constant is like a door number, fixed once set. Putting something in the box is called assignment, written ←. Note the arrow points right-to-left: "put the value on the right into the box on the left". Operators are the "actions" that process those boxes: calculate, compare, combine conditions.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 声明变量：DECLARE age : INTEGER，赋值：age ← 17（← 把右边的值放进左边的变量）。Declare a variable: DECLARE age : INTEGER; assign: age ← 17 (← puts the right value into the left variable).
  • 常量：CONSTANT PI ← 3.14159，之后不能再改。Constant: CONSTANT PI ← 3.14159, and it cannot change afterwards.
  • 算术：+ - * / 是四则；DIV 是整数除法（丢掉余数），MOD 是取余，^ 是乘方。Arithmetic: + - * / are the four operations; DIV is integer division (drops the remainder), MOD gives the remainder, ^ is power.
  • 比较：= <> > < >= <=，结果只有 TRUE 或 FALSE。Comparison: = <> > < >= <=, giving only TRUE or FALSE.
  • 逻辑：AND 两边都真才真，OR 一个真就真，NOT 取反。Logical: AND is true only if both sides are true, OR if either is true, NOT flips the value.
  • 优先级：括号 > 算术 > 比较 > 逻辑，先算乘除再算加减，再比大小，最后拼条件。Precedence: brackets > arithmetic > comparison > logical — multiply/divide before add/subtract, then compare, then combine.
别搞混：17 DIV 5 = 3（商），17 MOD 5 = 2（余数），17 / 5 = 3.4（带小数）。DIV 和 / 不是一回事，考试最爱在这里挖坑。Don't mix them up: 17 DIV 5 = 3 (quotient), 17 MOD 5 = 2 (remainder), 17 / 5 = 3.4 (with decimals). DIV and / are not the same — examiners love to test this.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: In pseudocode, ← assigns a value to a variable, CONSTANT declares a fixed value, DIV is integer division and MOD gives the remainder. AND, OR and NOT combine conditions.
例题Example
求 17 DIV 5、17 MOD 5、2^3 各是多少？Work out 17 DIV 5, 17 MOD 5 and 2^3.
17 DIV 5 = 3（整数除法，商 3 余 2，丢掉余数）。17 DIV 5 = 3 (integer division: 3 remainder 2, drop the remainder). 17 MOD 5 = 2（取余数）。17 MOD 5 = 2 (the remainder). 2^3 = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8。2^3 = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
练习Practice
提示：DIV 取商，MOD 取余。Hint: DIV takes the quotient, MOD the remainder.

求 23 DIV 4、23 MOD 4、3^2 各是多少？Work out 23 DIV 4, 23 MOD 4 and 3^2.

点开看答案Show answer
23 DIV 4 = 5；23 MOD 4 = 3；3^2 = 9。23 DIV 4 = 5; 23 MOD 4 = 3; 3^2 = 9.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 字符串操作 String operations LENGTH · SUBSTRING · concatenation 长度 · 子串 · 拼接
目标：会用 LENGTH、SUBSTRING、MID/LEFT/RIGHT、& 操作字符串，会大小写转换和比较字符串。Goal: use LENGTH, SUBSTRING, MID/LEFT/RIGHT and &, plus case conversion and string comparison.
字符串就是一串字符，像串起来的珠子。每个珠子有一个编号，而且从 1 开始——这跟很多编程语言从 0 开始不一样，千万别记错。想数有多少颗珠子用 LENGTH；想取中间一段用 SUBSTRING；想把两串接成一串用 &（拼接）。 A string is a sequence of characters, like beads on a thread. Each bead has a number, and numbering starts at 1 — unlike many languages that start at 0, so don't get it wrong. LENGTH counts the beads, SUBSTRING takes a slice out of the middle, and & joins two strings into one (concatenation).
记住这几点：Remember:
  • LENGTH(str) 返回字符个数；SUBSTRING(str, start, length) 从第 start 个字符起取 length 个（位置从 1 起）。LENGTH(str) returns the character count; SUBSTRING(str, start, length) takes length characters starting at position start (positions start at 1).
  • LEFT(str, n) 取左边 n 个，RIGHT(str, n) 取右边 n 个，MID 和 SUBSTRING 类似。LEFT(str, n) takes the leftmost n, RIGHT(str, n) the rightmost n, and MID is like SUBSTRING.
  • 拼接用 &："Hello" & "World" = "HelloWorld"。Join with &: "Hello" & "World" = "HelloWorld".
  • 大小写转换（如 UPPER / LOWER）把整串转成大写或小写。Case conversion (UPPER / LOWER) turns a whole string into upper or lower case.
  • 比较字符串按字母顺序（字典序）逐个字符比，如 "cat" < "dog" 为 TRUE。Strings compare by alphabetical (dictionary) order, character by character, so "cat" < "dog" is TRUE.
位置从 1 开始：SUBSTRING 的第 1 个字符不是 0 号位。这是剑桥伪代码和 Python/Java 最大的区别之一，写答案时先数清楚。Positions start at 1: the first character is not position 0. This is one of the biggest differences between Cambridge pseudocode and Python/Java — count carefully before you answer.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: LENGTH returns the number of characters; SUBSTRING(string, start, length) extracts characters from position start, where positions start at 1; the & operator concatenates two strings.
例题Example
设 S = "Computer"，求 LENGTH(S)、SUBSTRING(S, 4, 3)、LEFT(S, 3)、RIGHT(S, 3)。Let S = "Computer". Find LENGTH(S), SUBSTRING(S, 4, 3), LEFT(S, 3) and RIGHT(S, 3).
LENGTH("Computer") = 8（一共 8 个字符）。LENGTH("Computer") = 8 (8 characters in total). SUBSTRING(S, 4, 3) = "put"（第 4 个字符 p 起取 3 个）。SUBSTRING(S, 4, 3) = "put" (3 characters from the 4th, p). LEFT(S, 3) = "Com"；RIGHT(S, 3) = "ter"。LEFT(S, 3) = "Com"; RIGHT(S, 3) = "ter".
练习Practice
提示：先数清楚位置，第 1 个字符是 P。Hint: count carefully — the first character is P.

设 S = "Programming"，求 SUBSTRING(S, 1, 4) 和 RIGHT(S, 3)。Let S = "Programming". Find SUBSTRING(S, 1, 4) and RIGHT(S, 3).

点开看答案Show answer
SUBSTRING("Programming", 1, 4) = "Prog"；RIGHT(S, 3) = "ing"。SUBSTRING("Programming", 1, 4) = "Prog"; RIGHT(S, 3) = "ing".
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 过程与函数 Procedures and functions PROCEDURE · FUNCTION · parameter 过程 · 函数 · 参数
目标：分清 PROCEDURE 和 FUNCTION，理解参数按值/按引用传递，知道局部变量只在子程序里有效。Goal: tell PROCEDURE apart from FUNCTION, understand by-value vs by-reference parameters, and know that local variables live only inside a sub-program.
过程像叫外卖：你说一句话（CALL），它去办，办完不给你回任何东西；函数像问计算器：你问一个算式，它算好把答案递回给你。递给它们的信息叫参数。参数有两种递法：按值是只把「复印件」递过去，原件不会被改；按引用是直接递「原件」，里面一改，外面也跟着变。子程序里自己声明的变量是局部变量，干完活就消失，外面看不见。 A procedure is like ordering takeaway: you say the word (CALL), it does the job, and hands nothing back. A function is like asking a calculator: you ask a formula, it works it out and hands the answer back. The information you pass in is the parameter. There are two ways to pass it: by value passes only a "photocopy", so the original is untouched; by reference passes the "original" itself, so changes inside are seen outside. Variables declared inside a sub-program are local — they vanish when it finishes and are invisible outside.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • PROCEDURE 做一件事、无返回值，用 CALL 调用，以 ENDPROCEDURE 结束。A PROCEDURE does a task and returns nothing; it is called with CALL and ends with ENDPROCEDURE.
  • FUNCTION 算一个值、RETURNS 返回，以 ENDFUNCTION 结束，可放在表达式里。A FUNCTION computes a value, returns it with RETURNS, ends with ENDFUNCTION, and can appear in expressions.
  • 按值传递：传的是副本，函数里改了不影响原变量；按引用传递：传的是原变量，改了会影响外面。By value: a copy is passed, so changes inside don't affect the original; by reference: the original is passed, so changes are seen outside.
  • 局部变量只在该过程/函数里有效，用完就没了，和外面的同名变量互不干扰。Local variables exist only inside that procedure/function, disappear when it ends, and don't clash with same-named variables outside.
按值 vs 按引用是高频考点：按值安全（改不到外面），按引用能「把修改带出来」。看清题里写的是 BYVAL 还是 BYREF。By value vs by reference is a favourite exam point: by value is safe (the outside is untouched), by reference "carries changes out". Check whether the question says BYVAL or BYREF.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A procedure performs a task and returns nothing, while a function returns a value using RETURNS. By value passes a copy; by reference passes the original, so changes inside affect it.
例题Example
下面的过程按值（BYVAL）传递参数，程序最后 OUTPUT N 是多少？The procedure below passes its parameter by value (BYVAL). What does the program finally OUTPUT for N?
DECLARE N : INTEGER N ← 5 CALL Change(N) OUTPUT N PROCEDURE Change(BYVAL X : INTEGER) X ← 100 ENDPROCEDURE
按值传递时，X 只是 N 的副本。By value, X is only a copy of N. X ← 100 改的是副本，不影响 N，所以 N 仍是 5，输出 5。X ← 100 changes the copy, not N, so N is still 5; the output is 5.
练习Practice
提示：按引用传的是原变量本身。Hint: by reference passes the original variable itself.

若把上面 BYVAL 改成 BYREF（按引用），程序最后 OUTPUT N 是多少？If BYVAL is changed to BYREF (by reference) above, what does the program finally OUTPUT for N?

点开看答案Show answer
BYREF 时 X 就是 N 本身，X ← 100 即 N ← 100，所以输出 100。With BYREF, X is N itself, so X ← 100 means N ← 100; the output is 100.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 结构化编程 Structured programming modular · top-down · scope 模块化 · 自顶向下 · 作用域
目标：理解模块化与自顶向下设计，分清局部/全局变量，会用有意义的变量名，避免 goto。Goal: understand modular, top-down design, tell local from global variables, use meaningful names, and avoid goto.
写程序像盖房子——不会一口气盖好，而是拆成「打地基、砌墙、装门窗」一个个工序。先想好整体怎么搭（自顶向下），再把每个大块拆成小模块（模块化），每个小模块只干一件事。这样代码好写、好测、坏了也好找。模块里自己声明的变量是局部变量，只在模块内管用；整个程序都能用的叫全局变量，虽然方便但谁都能改，容易出乱子。 Writing a program is like building a house — you don't build it all at once, but in steps: foundations, walls, doors and windows. First decide the overall shape (top-down), then break each big part into small modules (modular), each doing one job. Code becomes easy to write, test and fix. Variables declared inside a module are local and only work there; global variables are usable everywhere — convenient, but anyone can change them, which invites bugs.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 模块化：把程序拆成若干独立模块（过程/函数），便于编写、测试和维护。Modular: split a program into self-contained modules (procedures/functions) for easier writing, testing and maintenance.
  • 自顶向下：先设计整体结构，再逐步细化每个部分，而不是一上来就抠细节。Top-down: design the overall structure first, then refine each part — not diving into details at once.
  • 局部变量只在模块内可见；全局变量整个程序都能访问（要少用，容易出错）。Local variables are visible only inside the module; global variables are accessible everywhere (use sparingly — they cause bugs).
  • 用有意义的变量名（如 totalMarks 而不是 x），提高可读性。Use meaningful identifiers (like totalMarks rather than x) to make the code readable.
  • 避免 goto：它会打乱结构、让程序难以理解，用循环和判断替代。Avoid goto: it breaks the structure and makes programs hard to follow — use loops and selection instead.
全局变量虽方便但危险：任何地方都能改它，出了问题难排查。能不用就不用，优先把变量声明成局部的。Global variables are convenient but risky: any part of the code can change them, so bugs are hard to trace. Avoid them when you can — prefer local variables.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Structured programming breaks a problem into self-contained modules using top-down design, uses meaningful identifiers, and avoids goto to keep the control flow clear and maintainable.
例题Example
下面的程序里，过程里的 X 和外面的 X 是同一个变量吗？最后 OUTPUT X 是多少？Is the X inside the procedure the same as the X outside? What does it finally OUTPUT?
DECLARE X : INTEGER X ← 10 CALL Show() OUTPUT X PROCEDURE Show() DECLARE X : INTEGER X ← 99 ENDPROCEDURE
Show 里重新 DECLARE 了一个局部 X，它和外面的 X 是两个不同的变量。Show declares its own local X, which is a different variable from the one outside. 所以外面的 X 仍是 10，输出 10。So the outside X is still 10; the output is 10.
练习Practice
提示：删掉 DECLARE 后，X 就指外面的那个了。Hint: without the DECLARE, X refers to the one outside.

若把 Show 里那句 DECLARE X : INTEGER 删掉，程序最后 OUTPUT X 是多少？If the line DECLARE X : INTEGER inside Show is removed, what does the program finally OUTPUT?

点开看答案Show answer
删掉后 Show 里的 X ← 99 改的是外面的 X，所以输出 99。Without the DECLARE, X ← 99 inside Show changes the outer X, so the output is 99.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 完整程序示例 A complete program example full program · pseudocode 完整程序 · 伪代码
目标：读懂一个完整伪代码程序，能逐段说出每一块在干什么，并算出手工运行的结果。Goal: read a complete pseudocode program, explain what each block does, and work out its output by tracing.
把前几站学的东西拼起来，就是一个能用的程序。看下面这个例子：输入 n 个数，求平均分并统计及格人数——输入、循环、判断、函数，它全用上了。别急着往下看，先自己读一遍，想想每一行在做什么。 Put the earlier stops together and you get a working program. Look at this one: read n numbers, find the average and count how many passed — it uses input, a loop, selection and a function all at once. Don't rush on — read it yourself first and think about what each line does.
DECLARE n : INTEGER DECLARE i, total, passCount : INTEGER DECLARE average : REAL total ← 0 passCount ← 0 OUTPUT "How many numbers?" INPUT n FOR i ← 1 TO n INPUT mark total ← total + mark IF mark >= 60 THEN passCount ← passCount + 1 ENDIF NEXT average ← total / n OUTPUT "Average: ", average OUTPUT "Pass count: ", passCount
逐段讲解：Block by block:
  • 开头 DECLARE 声明变量：n、i、total、passCount 是 INTEGER，average 是 REAL（因为除法可能出小数）。The DECLARE lines set up variables: n, i, total, passCount are INTEGER, average is REAL (division may give decimals).
  • total ← 0、passCount ← 0 是初始化——累加和计数前先清零。total ← 0 and passCount ← 0 are initialisation — clear the sum and count before accumulating.
  • FOR i ← 1 TO n 循环 n 次，每次 INPUT 一个分数，total ← total + mark 累加。FOR i ← 1 TO n loops n times, reading one mark each time and adding it with total ← total + mark.
  • IF mark >= 60 THEN 判断是否及格，及格就 passCount ← passCount + 1 计数。IF mark >= 60 THEN checks a pass, incrementing passCount when it does.
  • 最后 average ← total / n 用 / 求带小数的平均值，再 OUTPUT 输出结果。Finally average ← total / n uses / for a decimal average, then OUTPUT shows the results.
累加器必须先清零：total ← 0 少了这一步，累加就从没定义的值开始，结果不可预知——这是新手最常犯的错。Accumulators must start at zero: without total ← 0, the sum starts from an undefined value and the result is unpredictable — the most common beginner mistake.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: The program uses a FOR loop to read n marks, accumulates the total, uses an IF statement to count passes, and finally computes the average with total / n.
例题Example
如果输入 n = 3，三个分数是 50、60、70，程序输出什么？If n = 3 and the three marks are 50, 60, 70, what does the program output?
total = 0 + 50 + 60 + 70 = 180。total = 0 + 50 + 60 + 70 = 180. 及格线 60：60 和 70 及格，passCount = 2。Pass mark 60: both 60 and 70 pass, so passCount = 2. average = 180 / 3 = 60，所以输出 "Average: 60" 和 "Pass count: 2"。average = 180 / 3 = 60, so it outputs "Average: 60" and "Pass count: 2".
练习Practice
提示：及格线是 60（>= 60）。Hint: the pass mark is 60 (>= 60).

输入 n = 4，四个分数是 40、59、60、61，求 average 和 passCount。With n = 4 and marks 40, 59, 60, 61, find average and passCount.

点开看答案Show answer
total = 40 + 59 + 60 + 61 = 220；及格的是 60 和 61，passCount = 2；average = 220 / 4 = 55。total = 40 + 59 + 60 + 61 = 220; 60 and 61 pass, so passCount = 2; average = 220 / 4 = 55.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 三类错误与调试 Three kinds of errors and debugging syntax · logic · runtime 语法 · 逻辑 · 运行时
目标：分清三类错误，会用「打印中间值」和「走查」定位逻辑错误。Goal: tell the three error types apart and locate logic errors using trace tables and print statements.
程序出错分三种，就像三种「翻车」：语法错误像写错别字，编译器一眼就看出，压根跑不起来；逻辑错误像算错账，程序照跑，但结果不对——它不会报错，最难找；运行时错误像跑到半路踩坑摔倒，比如除以 0、数组越界，运行到那一句才崩。找逻辑错误的笨办法最管用：打印中间值（每步把变量打出来看），或者走查（自己拿张纸一步步模拟代码）。 Programs fail in three ways, like three kinds of crash: a syntax error is a typo the compiler spots at once, so the program never runs; a logic error is a miscalculation — the program runs but the answer is wrong, and since nothing reports it, it's the hardest to find; a runtime error is tripping over mid-run, like dividing by zero or an out-of-bounds index, crashing only at that line. The simplest tools find logic errors best: print intermediate values (output variables at each step) or trace (simulate the code line by line on paper).
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 语法错误：违反语言规则（少括号/引号、拼错关键字），编译时就报错，程序跑不起来。Syntax error: breaks the language rules (missing bracket/quote, misspelled keyword), reported at compile time, so the program won't run.
  • 逻辑错误：语法没错、能运行，但算法想错了，结果错误——最难发现。Logic error: the syntax is fine and it runs, but the algorithm is wrong, so the result is wrong — the hardest to spot.
  • 运行时错误：运行到某处才失败，如除零（DIV 0）、数组越界、类型不匹配。Runtime error: fails only during execution, such as division by zero (DIV 0), an out-of-bounds index, or a type mismatch.
  • 定位逻辑错误：打印中间值（每步 OUTPUT 变量）、走查（一步步模拟代码执行）。Locating logic errors: print intermediate values (OUTPUT variables at each step) and trace (simulate execution step by step).
逻辑错误不会自动报错：只能靠「打印中间值 + 走查」一点点揪出来，这是解释题和排错题的最爱。Logic errors never report themselves: only "print intermediates + trace" can flush them out — a favourite in explain and debug questions.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A syntax error breaks the language rules and is caught at compile time; a logic error runs but gives the wrong result; a runtime error only fails during execution, such as division by zero.
例题Example
判断下面三种情况各属于哪类错误。（1）x ← a DIV 0（2）PRINT("hi" 少了右括号（3）求平均写成 average ← total * n。Classify each case. (1) x ← a DIV 0 (2) PRINT("hi" missing a bracket (3) averaging written as average ← total * n.
(1) 运行时错误——除零，运行到这一句才崩。(1) Runtime error — division by zero, fails when that line runs. (2) 语法错误——少了括号，编译时就被发现。(2) Syntax error — missing bracket, caught at compile time. (3) 逻辑错误——能跑，但该除却乘，结果错了。(3) Logic error — it runs, but multiplies instead of dividing, so the result is wrong.
练习Practice
提示：想想它是什么时候被发现。Hint: think about when it gets detected.

程序里写了 arr[10] ← 5，但数组只声明了 8 个元素，这属于哪类错误？The program has arr[10] ← 5 but the array was declared with 8 elements. What kind of error is this?

点开看答案Show answer
运行时错误——越界访问，语法没问题，运行到这一句才失败。Runtime error — out-of-bounds access: the syntax is fine, but it fails when that line executes.
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

第 11 单元小结Unit 11 wrap-up

这一单元把「写程序」的基本功讲全了：变量存数据、运算符加工数据、字符串处理文本、过程与函数拆分任务。记住三条主线：过程做事不给回值、函数算值给回来；DIV 取商、MOD 取余；错误分语法、逻辑、运行时三类，逻辑错误靠打印中间值和走查来抓。把这些拼起来，你就能看懂、也能写出一个完整程序了。This unit covered the basics of writing programs: variables store data, operators process it, strings handle text, and procedures and functions split up tasks. Three threads run through it: a procedure does a task and returns nothing, a function returns a value; DIV gives the quotient, MOD the remainder; and errors come in three kinds — syntax, logic, runtime — with logic errors caught by printing intermediates and tracing. Put these together and you can read and write a complete program.

第 12 单元 · 软件开发Unit 12 · Software development Paper 2

CAIE 9618 Topic 12 · 5 站 · 一个软件从想法到上线，再到维护，怎么一步步来CAIE 9618 Topic 12 · 5 stops · how software goes from idea to release, then maintenance, step by step

路线图Roadmap本单元 5 站，从「软件怎么一步步做出来」走到「上线后怎么照顾它」5 stops, from "how software is built step by step" to "how to look after it after release"

  1. 程序开发生命周期：五步一个环The development life cycle: five steps in a loop
  2. 生命周期模型：瀑布、迭代与 RADLife cycle models: waterfall, iterative and RAD
  3. 程序设计工具：结构图与状态转移图Design tools: structure charts and state-transition diagrams
  4. 测试策略：白盒黑盒与四类测试数据Testing: white-box, black-box and four kinds of test data
  5. 维护类型：修、适应、加功能Maintenance: fix, adapt and add features

这一单元不考具体代码，考的是「怎么组织一个软件项目」的脑子。Paper 2 里画结构图、选测试数据、判断维护类型，都是高频题。This unit is not about specific code — it is about how to organise a software project. In Paper 2, drawing structure charts, choosing test data and classifying maintenance are all frequent questions.

1 程序开发生命周期 Program development life cycle analysis · design · coding · testing · maintenance 分析 · 设计 · 编码 · 测试 · 维护
目标：说出软件开发的五个阶段、顺序，以及每个阶段各产出什么。Goal: name the five stages in order and say what each one produces.
盖房子不会上来就砌墙，得先画图、打地基、验收，住进去以后还要修修补补。做软件也一样，有一条固定的流水线，叫程序开发生命周期。它一共五步：先分析——想清楚到底要解决什么问题、做不做得成；再设计——把方案画成蓝图；接着编码——照着蓝图写代码；然后测试——挑毛病、修毛病；最后维护——上线以后继续照顾它。五步走完一圈，往往又会回到起点，开始下一个版本。 You don't build a house by piling up bricks first — you draw plans, lay foundations, inspect, then keep repairing after moving in. Software is the same: there is a fixed pipeline called the program development life cycle. It has five steps: first analysis — work out what problem to solve and whether it is doable; then design — draw the blueprint; then coding — write code from the plan; then testing — find and fix faults; finally maintenance — look after it after release. Once the five steps finish, the project often loops back to the start for the next version.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 五个阶段按顺序是：分析 → 设计 → 编码 → 测试 → 维护，别记反。The five stages in order are: analysis → design → coding → testing → maintenance.
  • 分析：弄清问题、做可行性研究，产出需求规格说明。Analysis: understand the problem, do a feasibility study, and produce a requirements specification.
  • 设计：规划数据、界面、算法，产出设计文档。Design: plan the data, interface and algorithms, producing a design document.
  • 编码：把设计翻译成程序代码，产出可运行的程序。Coding: translate the design into program code, producing a working program.
  • 测试：找 bug 并修，确认符合需求，产出测试报告。Testing: find and fix bugs, check it meets the requirements, producing a test report.
  • 维护：上线后持续修 bug、加功能、适应变化，是一个长期过程。Maintenance: after release, keep fixing bugs, adding features and adapting — a long-term process.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: The program development life cycle has five stages: analysis, design, coding, testing and maintenance. Each stage produces a deliverable that feeds into the next stage.
例题Example
软件开发生命周期五个阶段按顺序是什么？各阶段结束时产出什么？List the five stages of the development life cycle in order. What does each stage produce?
顺序：分析 → 设计 → 编码 → 测试 → 维护。Order: analysis → design → coding → testing → maintenance. 产出：分析→需求规格，设计→设计文档，编码→程序，测试→测试报告，维护→持续的修正与改进。Deliverables: analysis → requirements spec, design → design document, coding → program, testing → test report, maintenance → ongoing fixes and improvements.
练习Practice
提示：想「把设计翻译成代码」这个动作。Hint: think of the action "translate the design into code".

「照着设计文档写出程序」属于哪个阶段？Which stage turns a design document into a program?

点开看答案Show answer
编码阶段——它的任务就是把设计变成可运行的代码。The coding stage — its job is to turn the design into runnable code.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 生命周期模型 Life cycle models waterfall · iterative · RAD 瀑布 · 迭代 · 快速应用开发
目标：分清瀑布、迭代、RAD 三种模型，会判断什么项目该用哪个。Goal: tell waterfall, iterative and RAD apart, and judge which project suits which.
同样是五步，怎么走很有讲究。瀑布模型像一条笔直的瀑布：一个阶段做完、签字确认，才能进入下一阶段，中间几乎不回头。它适合需求一开始就清清楚楚的项目，缺点是想改就难了。迭代模型像捏泥人：先做个粗糙的版本，一轮一轮地循环「设计→实现→测试」，每轮都更接近用户真正想要的，适合需求还没想明白、边做边改的情况。快速应用开发（RAD）是迭代的「加速版」：先快速搭一个原型给用户看，用户说不行就马上改，靠用户频繁反馈来逼近需求。 How you walk the five steps matters a lot. The waterfall model is like a straight waterfall: finish one stage, sign it off, then move on, with almost no turning back. It suits projects whose requirements are clear from the start, but changes are hard later. The iterative model is like moulding clay: build a rough version, then loop "design → implement → test" round after round, getting closer to what users want each time — good when requirements are not yet clear. Rapid application development (RAD) is an accelerated iteration: quickly build a prototype to show users, change it the moment they complain, and rely on frequent user feedback to home in on the requirements.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 瀑布模型：线性、阶段分明，前一阶段完成后才进下一阶段；适合需求明确且稳定的项目。Waterfall: linear with distinct stages, each finished before the next begins; suits clear, stable requirements.
  • 迭代模型：反复循环改进；适合需求多变、边做边明确的项目。Iterative: repeated cycles of improvement; suits changing, evolving requirements.
  • RAD：原型 + 用户频繁反馈，快速交付；适合时间紧、需求可探索的项目，但需要用户深度参与。RAD: prototypes plus frequent user feedback for fast delivery; suits tight deadlines and explorable requirements, but needs deep user involvement.
  • 一条判断线：需求明确→瀑布；需求多变→迭代；要快且用户能配合→RAD。A rule of thumb: clear requirements → waterfall; changing requirements → iterative; fast and users can join in → RAD.
别踩坑：考试最爱问「某项目该用哪种模型」。别背名字，抓住「需求稳不稳、要不要快速见效果」这两条就行。Watch out: exams love "which model for this project". Don't memorise names — just check "are the requirements stable, and must we see results fast".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: The waterfall model is linear with distinct stages and suits projects whose requirements are well understood and unlikely to change. Iterative development repeats cycles of building and improving, which suits projects with changing requirements.
例题Example
一个需求还没想清楚、要边做边改的小程序，选哪种模型最合适？为什么？A small app whose requirements are unclear and change as it is built — which model fits best, and why?
选迭代模型。Choose the iterative model. 因为它循环改进，能适应多变的需求；瀑布要求需求一开始就确定，不合适。Because it improves in cycles and handles changing requirements; waterfall needs requirements fixed up front, so it does not fit.
练习Practice
提示：需求几乎不变、规则写得很死，选哪种？Hint: requirements barely change and rules are fixed — which model?

一个银行结算系统，需求非常明确且几乎不变，选哪种模型？A bank settlement system with very clear, almost fixed requirements — which model?

点开看答案Show answer
瀑布模型——需求明确稳定，正好发挥它线性、阶段分明的优点。The waterfall model — clear, stable requirements play to its strength of being linear with distinct stages.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 程序设计工具 Program design tools structure chart · state-transition diagram 结构图 · 状态转移图
目标：会读、会画结构图和状态转移图，并知道各用在什么场景。Goal: read and draw structure charts and state-transition diagrams, and know when each is used.
写大程序之前，得先画两张「地图」。结构图（structure chart）像公司的组织架构图：把一个大任务从上往下拆成一堆小模块，方框是模块，连线表示「谁调用谁」，一眼看清程序的结构。状态转移图（state-transition diagram）像地铁线路图：系统有几个状态（比如交通灯的红、绿、黄），遇到什么事件（比如「定时到」）就跳到哪个状态。一句话：结构图讲程序怎么组织，状态图讲系统怎么切换。 Before writing a big program, draw two "maps". A structure chart is like a company org chart: it splits a big task into smaller modules from the top down — boxes are modules, lines show "who calls whom". A state-transition diagram is like a metro map: the system has states (say a traffic light's red, green, yellow) and moves to a new state when some event (like "timer done") fires. In one line: the structure chart shows how the program is organised, the state diagram shows how the system switches.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 结构图：自上而下分解，方框 = 模块，连线 = 调用关系，展示程序结构。Structure chart: top-down breakdown, boxes = modules, lines = calls, showing program structure.
  • 状态转移图：圆/椭圆 = 状态，箭头 = 转移，箭头上标触发条件，展示系统行为。State-transition diagram: circles/ellipses = states, arrows = transitions labelled with the trigger, showing system behaviour.
  • 结构图回答「程序怎么组织」；状态图回答「系统在不同状态间怎么切换」。A structure chart answers "how is the program organised"; a state diagram answers "how does the system move between states".
  • 带「开机/关机/运行/故障」这类状态词的场景，多半用状态转移图。Scenarios with state words like "on/off/running/fault" usually call for a state-transition diagram.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A structure chart shows how a program is broken down into modules and how they call each other. A state-transition diagram shows the states of a system and the events that cause it to move between them.
例题Example
自动售货机的「等待投币 → 收到钱 → 吐出饮料」过程，该用结构图还是状态转移图？A vending machine goes "waiting for money → money received → drink dispensed". Which diagram — structure chart or state-transition diagram?
用状态转移图。Use a state-transition diagram. 因为「等待投币」「收到钱」「吐饮料」都是状态，投币、确认是触发状态切换的事件。Because "waiting", "received" and "dispensing" are all states, and inserting money and confirming are the events that trigger switching.
练习Practice
提示：想想「拆成模块、画调用关系」是哪种图的活。Hint: splitting into modules and drawing call relationships is which diagram's job?

把一个点餐程序拆成「下单、结账、出餐」三个模块并画出调用关系，该用什么图？Splitting an ordering program into "order, pay, serve" modules and showing their calls — which diagram?

点开看答案Show answer
结构图——它专门用来展示模块的分解与调用关系。A structure chart — it is made for showing how modules are broken down and call each other.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 测试策略 Testing strategies white-box · black-box · normal · boundary 白盒 · 黑盒 · 正常 · 边界
目标：分清白盒、黑盒测试，会为程序挑出四类测试数据。Goal: tell white-box from black-box testing, and pick all four kinds of test data for a program.
测试有两种「看法」。白盒测试是掀开盖子看里面——测试者看得见源代码，专门检查每条路径、每个分支是不是都走到了。黑盒测试是只看盒子外面——不管里面怎么写，只管「给了这个输入，输出对不对」。挑测试数据时，要凑齐四类：正常（normal），合理范围里的普通数据；异常（abnormal），类型或格式错、本不该出现的数据；边界（boundary），正好踩在范围边上、或者刚刚越界一格的数据；极端（extreme），大得离谱、远远超范围的数据。 There are two "views" of testing. White-box testing opens the lid and looks inside — the tester can see the source code and checks that every path and branch is exercised. Black-box testing only looks at the outside — never mind the internals, just check "given this input, is the output right". When picking test data, cover all four kinds: normal — ordinary data inside the valid range; abnormal — wrong type or format that should never appear; boundary — exactly on the edge, or just one step past it; extreme — ridiculously large, far beyond the range.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 白盒测试：看得见代码内部，做语句覆盖、分支覆盖，检查逻辑是否都走到。White-box testing: sees the code inside, does statement and branch coverage, checking every logic path.
  • 黑盒测试：只看输入输出，不看代码，依据规格说明书。Black-box testing: only inputs and outputs, no code, judged against the specification.
  • 正常 normal：范围内合理数据；异常 abnormal：格式错、不该有的数据。normal: sensible in-range data; abnormal: wrongly-formatted data that should not occur.
  • 边界 boundary：正好在边界或旁边一格；极端 extreme：远超大范围的数据。boundary: exactly on or next to the edge; extreme: far beyond the range.
别踩坑：abnormal 和 boundary 别搞混——异常是「类型/格式不对」（比如该填数字却填了字母），边界是「数值刚好越界一格」（比如范围 1–100，填了 101）。Watch out: don't mix up abnormal and boundary — abnormal is "wrong type/format" (letters where a number should go), boundary is "just one step out of range" (101 for a 1–100 range).
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: White-box testing examines the internal logic and code paths, while black-box testing only checks inputs and outputs against the specification. Test data should include normal, abnormal, boundary and extreme values.
例题Example
一个程序要求输入 1–100 的整数，请为四类测试数据各举一例。A program accepts an integer from 1 to 100. Give one example for each of the four kinds of test data.
正常：70；异常：abc（字母）。Normal: 70; abnormal: abc (letters). 边界：0、1、100、101；极端：999999。Boundary: 0, 1, 100, 101; extreme: 999999.
练习Practice
提示：1–100 的范围，101 在什么位置？Hint: for a 1–100 range, where does 101 sit?

程序仍接受 1–100，输入「101」属于哪类测试数据？The program still accepts 1–100. Which kind of test data is "101"?

点开看答案Show answer
边界（boundary）——它正好在边界外一格（100 的旁边），最容易触发越界 bug。Boundary — it is exactly one step past the edge (next to 100), the classic spot for off-by-one bugs.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 维护类型 Types of maintenance corrective · adaptive · perfective 正确性 · 适应性 · 完善性
目标：能判断一件事属于哪类维护，并解释为什么维护是软件成本的大头。Goal: classify a change as the right kind of maintenance, and explain why maintenance dominates software cost.
软件上线不是终点，而是漫长照料的开始。维护分三类：正确性维护（corrective）是「补漏洞」——软件出 bug 了，赶紧修；适应性维护（adaptive）是「换环境」——操作系统、硬件、法律法规变了，软件得跟着改；完善性维护（perfective）是「加新功能」——用户想要新菜单、新按钮，或者想让程序跑得更快。为什么维护这么贵？因为一个软件要用好多年，而这些年里需求和环境一直在变，所以整个生命周期里，维护往往吃掉最大一块成本。 Release is not the finish line — it is the start of long-term care. Maintenance comes in three kinds: corrective maintenance is "patching holes" — the software has bugs, so fix them fast; adaptive maintenance is "changing with the surroundings" — when the OS, hardware or laws change, the software must follow; perfective maintenance is "adding features" — users want a new menu, a new button, or faster running. Why is maintenance so expensive? Because software lives for years, and in those years needs and environments keep changing, so maintenance usually eats the biggest slice of the whole life-cycle cost.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • corrective（正确性维护）：修 bug、纠正错误。corrective maintenance: fix bugs and errors.
  • adaptive（适应性维护）：适应外部变化，如新系统、新硬件、新法规。adaptive maintenance: adapt to outside changes like a new OS, hardware or laws.
  • perfective（完善性维护）：加新功能、提升性能，满足新需求。perfective maintenance: add features and boost performance to meet new needs.
  • 维护占成本大头：软件寿命长，需求和环境持续变化。Maintenance is the biggest cost because software lasts long while needs and environments keep changing.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Corrective maintenance fixes errors, adaptive maintenance changes software to work in a new environment, and perfective maintenance adds new features. Maintenance is the most expensive stage because software lasts for years while requirements and environments keep changing.
例题Example
判断三件事各属哪类维护：①软件在 Windows 11 上崩溃要修；②升级到新系统要改代码；③用户想要一个「导出报表」按钮。Classify three changes: ① the software crashes on Windows 11 and must be fixed; ② code must change for a new OS; ③ users want an "export report" button.
① corrective——修 bug。① corrective — fixing a bug. ② adaptive——适应新系统；③ perfective——加新功能。② adaptive — fitting a new system; ③ perfective — adding a feature.
练习Practice
提示：从英文进中文市场，是「外部环境」还是「内部 bug」？Hint: entering the Chinese market — outside environment or internal bug?

把软件界面从英文改成中文以进入中国市场，属于哪类维护？Localising the interface from English to Chinese to enter the Chinese market — which kind of maintenance?

点开看答案Show answer
adaptive（适应性维护）——软件本身没坏，是为了适应新市场、新环境而改。adaptive maintenance — the software is not broken; it is changed to fit a new market and environment.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

第 12 单元小结Unit 12 wrap-up

这一单元把「一个软件怎么从想法走到维护」串了起来：生命周期五步（分析→设计→编码→测试→维护），模型三种（瀑布适合需求明确、迭代适合需求多变、RAD 靠原型和用户反馈），设计工具两张图（结构图画模块、状态图画切换），测试两种看法加四类数据，最后是维护三类——修 bug、适应环境、加功能。抓住一条主线：先想清楚再做，做完还要一直照顾。This unit strung together how software goes from idea to maintenance: the life cycle has five steps (analysis → design → coding → testing → maintenance), the models are three (waterfall for clear needs, iterative for changing needs, RAD via prototypes and user feedback), the design tools are two diagrams (structure chart for modules, state diagram for switching), testing has two views plus four data kinds, and finally maintenance has three kinds — fix bugs, fit the environment, add features. One thread runs through it: think before you build, and keep looking after it once it is built.

下一步：第 13 单元 · 数据表示进阶，把这些概念往更深的 Paper 3 内容延伸。Next: Unit 13 · Advanced data representation to extend these ideas into the deeper Paper 3 material.

第 13 单元 · 数据表示进阶Unit 13 · Data Representation (advanced) Paper 3

CAIE 9618 Topic 13 · 5 站 · 用户自定义类型、文件组织，以及小数在计算机里怎么存CAIE 9618 Topic 13 · 5 stops · user-defined types, file organisation, and how decimals are stored

路线图Roadmap本单元 5 站，从「自定义类型」一路走到「小数怎么存、为什么存不准」5 stops, from user-defined types to how decimals are stored (and why they go wrong)

  1. 用户自定义类型：枚举、指针、集合、记录、类User-defined types: enum, pointer, set, record, class
  2. 文件组织：顺序、索引顺序、随机/直接File organisation: sequential, indexed sequential, random/direct
  3. 浮点数表示：符号 + 指数 + 尾数Floating point: sign + exponent + mantissa
  4. 规格化与转换：小数怎么变成浮点Normalisation and conversion: turning decimals into floats
  5. 精度与误差：为什么 0.1 存不准Precision and errors: why 0.1 is never exact

这一单元是 Paper 3 的「数据表示」：前半讲怎么自己造类型、怎么组织文件，后半讲小数（浮点数）在计算机里怎么存、以及它的天生缺陷。This Paper 3 unit covers advanced data representation: how to build your own types and organise files, then how decimals (floating point) are stored — and their built-in flaws.

1 用户自定义类型：枚举、指针、集合、记录、类 User-defined types: enum, pointer, set, record, class ENUM · POINTER · SET · RECORD · CLASS 枚举 · 指针 · 集合 · 记录 · 类
目标：看懂为什么要自定义类型，能说出枚举、指针、集合、记录、类各是什么。Goal: understand why we need user-defined types, and say what enum, pointer, set, record and class each are.
语言自带的类型（integer、real、string、char、boolean）只够存「一个值」。可现实里的数据常常是一坨：一个学生有名字、年龄、成绩；颜色只能从几种里挑；牌堆有一串顺序。所以几乎所有语言都让你自己「造类型」。枚举就是从有限几个值里选一个（红绿灯的红/黄/绿）；记录把不同类型打包成一条（名字+年龄+成绩）；指针存的是内存地址；集合装一组不重复的值；类在记录上再加能操作它的方法，是面向对象的起点。 Built-in types (integer, real, string, char, boolean) only hold a single value. But real data comes in lumps: a student has a name, age and grade; a colour is one of a few choices; a deck has an order. So almost every language lets you create your own types. An enumerated type is a fixed list of values (red/amber/green). A record packs different types into one (name + age + grade). A pointer stores a memory address. A set holds values with no repeats. A class adds the methods that operate on a record — the start of object-oriented programming.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 内置类型只存单一值；自定义类型让数据更贴近现实、程序更清晰、更不易出错。Built-in types hold one value; user-defined types make data match reality, and code clearer and less error-prone.
  • 枚举 ENUM：有限个取值（红/绿/蓝、周一到周日）。Enumerated type (ENUM): a fixed list of values (red/green/blue, Monday–Sunday).
  • 指针 POINTER：存的是内存地址，能指向变量或记录。Pointer: stores a memory address, pointing at a variable or record.
  • 集合 SET：一组无序、不重复的值。Set: an unordered collection with no repeated values.
  • 记录 RECORD：把不同类型的字段（名字、年龄、成绩）组合成一个整体。Record: groups fields of different types (name, age, grade) into one item.
  • 类 CLASS：记录 + 操作它的方法，是面向对象的基础。Class: a record plus the methods that work on it — the basis of OOP.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A user-defined type is a data type created by the programmer, such as an enumerated type, pointer, set, record or class. A record groups fields of different types together, while a class also includes the methods that operate on that data.
例题Example
定义一个表示「学生」的记录类型，需要包含哪些字段？What fields should a "student" record type contain?
用 RECORD 把不同类型打包：姓名（字符串 string）、年龄（整数 integer）、成绩（实数 real）。Use a RECORD to pack different types: name (string), age (integer), grade (real). 这样「一个学生」就是一条记录，读写时按字段名访问，清晰又不易错。Now "a student" is one record, accessed by field name — clear and less error-prone.
练习Practice
提示：想想红绿灯有哪几种颜色。Hint: think of the colours of a traffic light.

写出「交通灯」枚举类型的所有取值。List all the values of a "traffic light" enumerated type.

点开看答案Show answer
RED（红）、AMBER（黄）、GREEN（绿）。RED, AMBER, GREEN.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 文件组织：顺序、索引顺序、随机/直接 File organisation: sequential, indexed sequential, random/direct sequential · indexed · random 顺序 · 索引 · 随机
目标：分清顺序、索引顺序、随机/直接三种文件组织，并说出各自适合的场景。Goal: tell apart sequential, indexed sequential and random/direct files, and say what each is good for.
文件是一堆记录的集合，怎么「摆」这些记录，决定了读取快不快。顺序文件像一盘磁带——只能从头一条条读，要删一条得把后面的全复制一遍，但它适合「每次都要处理全部记录」的批处理。索引顺序文件给记录建了张「目录」（索引），按主键先查索引、定位后再顺序读。随机/直接文件用哈希函数或地址直接算出记录在哪，想读第几条立刻跳到第几条。 A file is a collection of records, and how they are laid out decides how fast you can read them. A sequential file is like a tape — you must read one after another from the start, and deleting one means copying everything after it, but it is perfect for batch jobs that process every record. An indexed sequential file adds a "directory" (index): look up the key, locate, then read in sequence. A random/direct file computes where a record lives with a hash function or address, so you can jump straight to any record.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 顺序 sequential：按写入顺序存放、从头到尾读；查找慢（平均读一半），但适合批处理（工资单、对账单）。Sequential: stored in order, read start to end; slow search (half on average) but great for batch jobs (payroll, statements).
  • 索引顺序 indexed sequential：有索引（主键→位置），先查索引再顺序访问；查找快、还能顺序遍历。Indexed sequential: an index maps keys to positions; look up first, then access — fast search and still sequential.
  • 随机/直接 random/direct：用哈希函数或记录地址直接定位，不依赖顺序；能立即访问任意记录。Random/direct: a hash function or address locates a record directly — instant access to any record.
  • 更新时：顺序文件插入/删除要重写整个文件；随机文件可以直接改一条。When updating: sequential files must be rewritten to insert/delete; random files can edit one record directly.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: In a sequential file, records are stored in order and must be read one after another, which is slow for search but efficient for processing every record. A random file uses a hash function to compute a record's address, allowing any record to be accessed directly.
例题Example
银行每天要给所有账户算利息，客服又要能立即查某个账户余额。这两种操作分别适合哪种文件组织？A bank calculates interest on all accounts daily, but staff must instantly check one account's balance. Which file organisation suits each?
算利息要处理全部记录 → 顺序文件最合适（从头到尾全部读一遍）。Interest touches every record → a sequential file is best (read all, start to end). 查单个账户要立即定位 → 随机/直接文件（或用哈希定位）最合适。Looking up one account needs instant access → a random/direct file (via a hash) is best.
练习Practice
提示：从「要立即定位某一条」想。Hint: think about locating one record instantly.

订票系统要立即查出某航班的余票，最适合哪种文件组织？A booking system must instantly find a flight's remaining seats. Which file organisation is best?

点开看答案Show answer
随机/直接文件：用哈希或地址直接定位到该航班的记录，不必从文件头顺序查找。Random/direct file: a hash or address locates that flight's record directly, with no need to search from the start.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 浮点数表示：符号 + 指数 + 尾数 Floating point: sign + exponent + mantissa mantissa · exponent · sign bit 尾数 · 指数 · 符号位
目标：看懂浮点的「符号 + 指数 + 尾数」三段结构，明白它和定点的区别、为什么要浮点。Goal: read the sign + exponent + mantissa structure, and see how it differs from fixed point and why we need it.
定点数的小数点位置固定，整数能表示的范围太小、小数又没法精确。浮点数像科学计数法：把数写成「尾数 × 2^指数」，小数点（其实是二进制点）可以「浮动」，所以既能表示 0.000…0001 这种极小值，也能表示 10³⁸ 这种极大值。存的时候拆成三段：符号位（正负）、指数（决定大小/范围）、尾数（决定有效数字/精度）。 Fixed point keeps the decimal point in one place, so integers have a tiny range and fractions cannot be stored precisely. Floating point works like scientific notation: write a number as "mantissa × 2^exponent", so the (binary) point can "float" — it can hold a tiny value like 0.000…0001 or a huge one like 10³⁸. It is stored in three parts: the sign bit (sign), the exponent (size/range) and the mantissa (significant digits/precision).
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 浮点 = 尾数 × 2^指数；存成三段：符号位 + 指数 + 尾数。Floating point = mantissa × 2^exponent; stored as sign bit + exponent + mantissa.
  • 指数决定能表示的范围（极大/极小），尾数决定精度（有效数字多少位）。The exponent decides the range (how big/small); the mantissa decides the precision (significant digits).
  • 定点小数点固定、范围小但实现简单；浮点范围大得多，代价是运算更复杂。Fixed point has a fixed point and a small range but is simple; floating point has a far bigger range at the cost of more complex arithmetic.
  • 二进制里「小数点」其实是「二进制点」，每一位权重是 1/2、1/4、1/8……In binary the "decimal point" is really a "binary point": each place is worth 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, …
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A real number can be stored in floating-point form as mantissa × 2^exponent. The sign bit stores the sign, the exponent determines the range of values that can be represented, and the mantissa determines the precision.
例题Example
为什么定点表示很难同时精确存下 0.0001 和 1 000 000？Why is it hard for fixed point to store both 0.0001 and 1 000 000 exactly?
定点的小数点位置固定，位数有限，整数部分和小数部分互相挤占。Fixed point keeps the point in one place with limited bits, so the integer and fraction parts crowd each other out. 浮点让「点」浮动、用指数调节大小，所以极小值和极大值都能表示。Floating point lets the point float and uses the exponent to scale, so both tiny and huge values can be stored.
练习Practice
提示：回想三段各自负责什么。Hint: recall what each of the three parts does.

在浮点格式中，「精度」由哪一段决定，「范围」由哪一段决定？In a floating-point format, which part decides the precision and which the range?

点开看答案Show answer
精度由尾数位数决定，范围由指数位数决定。The precision is set by the mantissa bits; the range is set by the exponent bits.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 规格化与转换：小数怎么变成浮点 Normalisation and conversion: turning decimals into floats normalisation · bias 规格化 · 偏移
目标：会把十进制小数转成规格化二进制浮点，理解偏移量（移码）的作用。Goal: convert a decimal fraction into a normalised binary float and understand the role of the bias.
浮点有个「规范写法」叫规格化（normalisation）：把尾数调整到固定范围（比如 0.1 ≤ 尾数 < 1，即最高有效位是 1），这样同样的位数能存更多有效数字、精度最高。指数直接存正负很麻烦，于是用偏移量（bias）：把真实指数加上一个固定数，存进去的全是正数，读出来再减掉。转换四步：十进制→二进制 → 规格化 → 指数加偏移 → 组装三段。 Floating point has a "standard form" called normalisation: adjust the mantissa to a fixed range (say 0.1 ≤ mantissa < 1, so its top bit is 1), which fits more significant digits into the same bits and gives the best precision. Storing a signed exponent is awkward, so we use a bias: add a fixed number to the real exponent so the stored value is always positive, and subtract it again on read. Four steps: denary→binary → normalise → add bias → assemble the three parts.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 规格化：移动二进制点，让尾数最高位为 1（0.1… 或 1.… 格式），精度最高。Normalisation: shift the binary point so the mantissa's most significant bit is 1, giving maximum precision.
  • 规格化后数写成：尾数 × 2^指数。After normalisation the number is mantissa × 2^exponent.
  • 偏移（移码）：存储的指数 = 真实指数 + 偏移量（常见 bias 如 7、127、1023）。Bias: stored exponent = real exponent + bias (common biases: 7, 127, 1023).
  • 转换流程：十进制 → 二进制 → 规格化 → 指数加偏移 → 组装 符号 | 指数 | 尾数。Conversion flow: denary → binary → normalise → add bias → assemble sign | exponent | mantissa.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Normalisation shifts the binary point so that the most significant bit of the mantissa is 1, maximising precision. The exponent is stored with a bias added so that it can always be stored as a positive number.
例题Example
把 10.25 转成 12 位浮点（1 符号 + 4 指数 + 7 尾数，偏移量 7）。Convert 10.25 into a 12-bit float (1 sign + 4 exponent + 7 mantissa, bias 7).
十进制 → 二进制：10.25 = 8 + 2 + 0.25 = 1010.01₂。Denary → binary: 10.25 = 8 + 2 + 0.25 = 1010.01₂. 规格化：二进制点左移 4 位 → 0.101001 × 2⁴。Normalise: shift the point left 4 → 0.101001 × 2⁴. 指数加偏移：4 + 7 = 11 = 1011。Add the bias: 4 + 7 = 11 = 1011. 组装（尾数补到 7 位）：0 | 1011 | 1010010。Assemble (pad mantissa to 7 bits): 0 | 1011 | 1010010.
练习Practice
提示：先转二进制，再规格化，再加偏移。Hint: convert to binary, normalise, then add the bias.

把 6.5 转成 12 位浮点（1 符号 + 4 指数 + 7 尾数，偏移量 7）。Convert 6.5 into a 12-bit float (1 sign + 4 exponent + 7 mantissa, bias 7).

点开看答案Show answer
6.5 = 110.1₂ = 0.1101 × 2³；指数 3 + 7 = 10 = 1010；尾数补成 7 位 1101000；结果 0 | 1010 | 1101000。6.5 = 110.1₂ = 0.1101 × 2³; exponent 3 + 7 = 10 = 1010; pad mantissa to 1101000; result 0 | 1010 | 1101000.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 精度与误差：为什么 0.1 存不准 Precision and errors: why 0.1 is never exact rounding · overflow · underflow 舍入 · 溢出 · 下溢
目标：解释浮点的精度和范围各由谁决定，说出舍入误差、溢出、下溢是什么。Goal: explain what decides a float's precision and range, and what rounding error, overflow and underflow are.
浮点不是「无限精确」的——它只有固定那么多位，尾数位决定「能精确到几位有效数字」，指数位决定「能大到多小/多大」。这两样像天平两端，位数就那么多，精度高范围就窄，范围广精度就低。0.1 转成二进制是 0.0001100110011…无限循环，存进去只能截断，所以 0.1 + 0.2 在计算机里不等于 0.3。太小被当成 0 叫下溢（underflow），太大装不下叫溢出（overflow）。 Floating point is not infinitely precise — it only has so many bits: the mantissa bits decide "how many significant digits", and the exponent bits decide "how big or small". They are two sides of a balance: more precision means less range, more range means less precision. 0.1 in binary is 0.0001100110011…, an endless fraction, so it must be truncated — which is why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3 in a computer. Too small and it becomes 0 (underflow); too big and it cannot fit (overflow).
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 精度由尾数位数决定；范围由指数位数决定；总位数固定，二者此消彼长。Precision depends on the mantissa bits; range on the exponent bits; with fixed total bits, one trades off against the other.
  • 0.1 等小数在二进制里是无限循环小数，无法精确表示，只能近似 → 舍入误差。Decimals like 0.1 are endless fractions in binary, so they can only be approximated → rounding error.
  • 舍入误差：截断/四舍五入造成的微小误差，反复运算会累积。Rounding error: a tiny error from truncation/rounding that accumulates over repeated calculations.
  • 溢出 overflow：数值超出能表示的最大值；下溢 underflow：数值太接近 0，被当成 0。Overflow: the value exceeds the largest representable number; underflow: the value is so close to 0 it becomes 0.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: The precision of a floating-point number depends on the number of mantissa bits, while the range depends on the number of exponent bits. Some decimal fractions such as 0.1 cannot be represented exactly in binary, which causes rounding errors.
例题Example
为什么 0.1 + 0.2 在计算机里不等于 0.3？Why is 0.1 + 0.2 not equal to 0.3 in a computer?
0.1 和 0.2 转二进制都是无限循环小数，存储时被截断，产生舍入误差。0.1 and 0.2 are both endless binary fractions, truncated on storage, causing a rounding error. 两个近似值相加再截断，结果约 0.30000000000000004，而不是精确的 0.3。Adding the two approximations and truncating again gives about 0.30000000000000004, not exactly 0.3.
练习Practice
提示：位数给了谁，谁的「本事」就变大。Hint: give bits to one side and that side grows stronger.

8 位浮点（1 符号 + 3 指数 + 4 尾数）改成（1 符号 + 4 指数 + 3 尾数），精度和范围各怎么变？If an 8-bit float changes from (1 sign + 3 exponent + 4 mantissa) to (1 + 4 + 3), how do its precision and range change?

点开看答案Show answer
指数从 3 位变 4 位 → 能表示的范围更大；尾数从 4 位变 3 位 → 精度变低。The exponent grows from 3 to 4 bits → a bigger range; the mantissa shrinks from 4 to 3 bits → lower precision.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

第 13 单元小结Unit 13 wrap-up

这一单元把「更复杂的数据怎么表示」讲透了：自定义类型（枚举/指针/集合/记录/类）让程序更贴近现实；文件组织（顺序/索引顺序/随机）决定读取效率；浮点用「符号 + 指数 + 尾数」存小数，规格化提升精度，但精度看尾数、范围看指数，0.1 这种数终究存不精确。记住一条主线：数据都是位，区别在于怎么解释这些位——以及固定的位数里，精度和范围永远在互相让路。This unit covered how richer data is represented: user-defined types (enum/pointer/set/record/class) make programs match reality; file organisation (sequential/indexed/random) decides read speed; floating point stores decimals as "sign + exponent + mantissa", with normalisation boosting precision — but precision comes from the mantissa and range from the exponent, so 0.1 can never be exact. One thread runs through it: data is just bits, and within a fixed bit count, precision and range are always trading places.

CAIE 9618 Topic 14 · 5 站 · 协议怎么分层、TCP 与 UDP、电路交换与分组交换CAIE 9618 Topic 14 · 5 stops · protocol layering, TCP vs UDP, circuit vs packet switching

路线图Roadmap本单元 5 站，从「为什么要分层」讲到「应用层有哪些协议」5 stops, from "why layering" to "which application-layer protocols exist"

  1. 协议分层：OSI 与 TCP/IPProtocol layering: OSI and TCP/IP
  2. TCP vs UDP：可靠与快速TCP vs UDP: reliable vs fast
  3. 电路交换 vs 分组交换Circuit vs packet switching
  4. 分组交换详解：拆包·寻路·重组Packet switching: split · route · reassemble
  5. 常见应用层协议：HTTP·FTP·SMTP·DNSCommon protocols: HTTP · FTP · SMTP · DNS

这一单元把「数据怎么在网络里可靠、高效地传」讲清楚——分层是骨架，TCP/UDP 与交换方式是血肉，应用层协议是每天都在用的面孔。This unit explains how data travels reliably and efficiently — layering is the skeleton, TCP/UDP and switching are the flesh, and application-layer protocols are the familiar faces.

1 协议分层 Protocol layering OSI · TCP/IP · encapsulation OSI · TCP/IP · 封装
目标：理解「分层」的思想，知道 TCP/IP 四层与 OSI 七层各层的职责，以及「封装/解封装」是怎么回事。Goal: understand the idea of layering, know the jobs of the TCP/IP four layers and OSI seven layers, and grasp encapsulation/de-encapsulation.
把网络通信想象成寄快递：你先写好内容（应用层），交给快递公司打包、写收件地址（传输层），物流网络决定包裹走哪条路到哪个城市（网际层），最后卡车或飞机真正把包裹运过去（网络接口层）。每一层只管自己那一段，出了问题也容易定位——这就是「分层」的好处：把一件复杂的大工程拆成几件独立的小活。 Think of networking as sending a parcel: you write the content (application layer), the courier packs it and writes the address (transport layer), the logistics network decides which route to which city (internet layer), and finally trucks or planes physically move it (link layer). Each layer only minds its own step, so problems are easier to pin down — that is the benefit of layering: split one big, complex job into several independent small ones.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 为什么要分层：把复杂问题拆成小块，各层独立设计、修改，互不干扰，也方便排错。Why layer? It splits a complex problem into small pieces; each layer is designed and changed independently, without disturbing the others, and faults are easier to find.
  • TCP/IP 四层（自下而上）：网络接口层 → 网际层 → 传输层 → 应用层。The four TCP/IP layers (bottom-up): link → internet → transport → application.
  • OSI 是七层「参考模型」更细；真正跑在互联网上的是 TCP/IP 四层。OSI is a seven-layer reference model; the internet actually runs on the four-layer TCP/IP.
  • 封装：发送时每层往下加自己的「头」；解封装：接收时每层剥掉对应的头。Encapsulation: when sending, each layer adds its own header; de-encapsulation: the receiver strips each header off in turn.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Protocol layering divides network communication into layers, each responsible for one task. This makes the system easier to design, modify and troubleshoot, because each layer works independently.
例题Example
发送一条网页请求时，数据在传输层和网际层分别会被加上什么？When a web request is sent, what does the transport layer and the internet layer each add?
传输层把应用层数据封装成段（segment），加上 TCP 头（含端口号、序号等）。The transport layer wraps the data into a segment, adding a TCP header (port numbers, sequence numbers, etc.). 网际层再加上 IP 头（含源/目标 IP 地址），变成包（packet）。The internet layer adds an IP header (source/destination IP) to make a packet.
练习Practice
提示：想「谁真正被使用、谁只是参考」。Hint: think about which is actually used and which is just a reference.

OSI 七层模型和 TCP/IP 四层模型，哪一个真正被互联网使用？Which is actually used on the internet — the seven-layer OSI model or the four-layer TCP/IP model?

点开看答案Show answer
TCP/IP 四层模型。OSI 是理论参考模型，互联网实际按 TCP/IP 四层工作。The four-layer TCP/IP model. OSI is a theoretical reference model; the internet works on the four-layer TCP/IP.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 TCP vs UDP TCP vs UDP reliable · handshake · UDP 可靠 · 握手 · UDP
目标：分清 TCP（可靠、面向连接）和 UDP（快、不可靠、无连接），知道各自适合什么场景。Goal: tell TCP (reliable, connection-oriented) from UDP (fast, unreliable, connectionless) and know when each fits.
TCP 像挂号信：先确认双方都在（三次握手），每封信都要签收（确认），丢了就重寄（重传），顺序也不会乱。UDP 像扔纸飞机：不管对方在不在，直接扔过去——快是快，但可能丢、可能乱序。所以「一个字都不能错」的网页、邮件、文件下载用 TCP；「卡一下没关系、快才重要」的视频、直播、游戏用 UDP。 TCP is like registered mail: both sides confirm they are ready (three-way handshake), every letter is signed for (acknowledgement), lost ones are resent (retransmission), and order never breaks. UDP is like a paper plane: you throw it whether or not the other side is ready — fast, but it may be lost or out of order. So web pages, email and downloads, where every bit matters, use TCP; video, streaming and games, where speed beats a rare glitch, use UDP.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • TCP：面向连接（先三次握手）、可靠（确认 + 重传）、有序。TCP: connection-oriented (three-way handshake first), reliable (ACK + retransmission), ordered.
  • UDP：无连接、不确认、不重传，快但可能丢包、乱序。UDP: connectionless, no ACK, no retransmission — fast but packets may be lost or out of order.
  • 三次握手：SYN → SYN+ACK → ACK。Three-way handshake: SYN → SYN+ACK → ACK.
  • TCP 用于网页、邮件、文件；UDP 用于视频流、在线游戏、VoIP。TCP serves web, email and files; UDP serves video streaming, online games and VoIP.
小心：别把 UDP 的「不可靠」当缺点——它是「用可靠换速度」的主动选择：实时场景宁可快，也不要慢吞吞的重传。Note: don't read UDP's "unreliable" as a flaw — it is a deliberate trade of reliability for speed: real-time apps prefer fast over slow retransmission.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: TCP is connection-oriented and reliable: it establishes a connection with a three-way handshake and uses acknowledgements and retransmission. UDP is connectionless and faster, but it does not guarantee delivery or order.
例题Example
为什么在线游戏通常用 UDP 而不是 TCP？Why do online games usually use UDP rather than TCP?
游戏要低延迟；TCP 的握手、确认、重传会带来额外等待。Games need low latency; TCP's handshake, ACK and retransmission add extra waiting. 丢一两个包影响不大（下一帧会覆盖），所以用 UDP 换速度。Losing a packet or two hardly matters (the next frame overwrites it), so UDP trades reliability for speed.
练习Practice
提示：按顺序回忆三步。Hint: recall the three steps in order.

写出 TCP 三次握手的三个步骤。Write the three steps of the TCP three-way handshake.

点开看答案Show answer
SYN → SYN+ACK → ACK。SYN → SYN+ACK → ACK.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 电路交换 vs 分组交换 Circuit vs packet switching dedicated line · packets 专用线路 · 分组
目标：讲清两种交换方式的机制与优缺点，能举出各自的应用。Goal: explain how the two switching methods work, their pros and cons, and where each is used.
电路交换像老式电话总机：你拨号后，接线员给你拉一条专用线，这通电话从头到尾这条线就归你俩用，别人插不进来——稳定，但线路利用率低。分组交换像现代快递：把要送的东西拆成一个个包裹，各自找路、共用公路和仓库——线路利用率高、更灵活，但可能延迟、乱序。 Circuit switching is like an old telephone exchange: once you dial, the operator wires you a dedicated line held for the whole call — stable, but the line is poorly used. Packet switching is like a modern courier: the goods are split into parcels that each find their own route and share the roads and depots — efficient and flexible, but possibly delayed or out of order.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 电路交换：通信前先建立一条专用通道，全程独占；例如老式电话网。Circuit switching: a dedicated path is set up before communicating and held for the whole call; e.g. the old telephone network.
  • 分组交换：数据拆成小包，每个包独立寻路、共享线路；例如互联网。Packet switching: data is split into packets that route independently and share the line; e.g. the internet.
  • 电路交换优点：专用、稳定、延迟固定；缺点：空闲也占用线路，利用率低。Circuit: dedicated, stable, fixed delay; drawback — the line is reserved even when idle, so it is inefficient.
  • 分组交换优点：线路利用率高、容错好；缺点：可能延迟、乱序、需重组。Packet: high line utilisation, good fault tolerance; drawback — possible delay, disorder and reassembly.
记忆口诀：电路交换 = 一条路包给你；分组交换 = 大家拼车。Memory hook: circuit switching = the road is yours; packet switching = carpooling.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: In circuit switching a dedicated path is set up for the whole communication, so the line stays reserved even when no data is sent. In packet switching data is split into packets that are routed independently and share the line, using bandwidth more efficiently.
例题Example
为什么互联网采用分组交换，而不是电路交换？Why does the internet use packet switching rather than circuit switching?
数据拆成包后，多个用户的数据可以共享同一条线路，利用率高。Split into packets, many users' data share one line, so utilisation is high. 某条线路断了，包还能绕别的路走，容错更好。If one line breaks, packets reroute around it — better fault tolerance.
练习Practice
提示：从「线路会不会闲置」想。Hint: think about whether the line sits idle.

说出电路交换的一个缺点。Name one drawback of circuit switching.

点开看答案Show answer
即使双方没在传数据，专用线路仍被占用，线路利用率低。The dedicated line stays reserved even when no data is being sent, so utilisation is low.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 分组交换详解 Packet switching in detail packet · routing · reassembly 包 · 路由 · 重组
目标：说清一个数据包的结构，以及「拆包 → 寻路 → 重组」全过程，并解释优缺点。Goal: describe a packet's structure and the whole split → route → reassemble process, and explain the pros and cons.
你要寄一本 1000 页的书，塞不进一个信封，就拆成 100 个小包裹，每个写上「第几页 + 收件地址」，分开寄。有的走高速、有的走国道，到达顺序可能和寄出顺序不一样；收件人按「第几页」重新排好，就是原来那本书。分组交换就是这样：每个 packet 带目标地址和序号，各自寻路，最后按序号重组。 Sending a 1000-page book that won't fit one envelope means splitting it into 100 parcels, each labelled with its page number and the address, posted separately. Some take the motorway, some the back roads, so they may arrive in a different order; the receiver re-sorts them by page number and gets the original book back. Packet switching works this way: each packet carries a destination address and a sequence number, routes independently, and is reassembled by number.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 每个 packet 包含：目标地址、序号、数据（可能还有校验信息）。Each packet holds: destination address, sequence number, and the data (maybe a checksum).
  • 每个包独立寻路，可能走不同路径、乱序到达。Each packet routes independently, possibly by different paths, arriving out of order.
  • 接收端按序号把包重新排序、重组。The receiver reorders and reassembles the packets by sequence number.
  • 优点：线路利用率高、某条路断了能绕行（容错）；缺点：延迟、乱序、需重组。Pros: high utilisation, rerouting when a path fails (fault tolerance); cons: delay, disorder, reassembly.
小心：「乱序」不是错误——接收端手里有「序号」这张王牌，会把它们排回正确顺序。Note: "out of order" is not an error — the receiver holds the sequence number as its trump card and sorts them back into order.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Each packet carries the destination address and a sequence number. Packets are routed independently and may take different paths, so they can arrive out of order; the receiver uses the sequence numbers to reassemble them.
例题Example
一个文件被拆成 4 个包，到达顺序是 3、1、4、2，接收端怎么处理？A file is split into 4 packets arriving in the order 3, 1, 4, 2. What does the receiver do?
读出每个包的序号：3、1、4、2。Read each packet's sequence number: 3, 1, 4, 2. 按序号重排成 1、2、3、4，再拼回完整文件。Re-sort into 1, 2, 3, 4 and rebuild the complete file.
练习Practice
提示：回想分组交换的两个「代价」。Hint: recall packet switching's two "costs".

说出分组交换的两个缺点。Name two drawbacks of packet switching.

点开看答案Show answer
可能带来延迟；包可能乱序到达，接收端需要重组。It can introduce delay, and packets may arrive out of order so the receiver must reassemble them.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 常见应用层协议 Common application-layer protocols HTTP · FTP · SMTP · DNS HTTP · FTP · SMTP · DNS
目标：记住 HTTP/HTTPS、FTP、SMTP、POP3/IMAP、DNS 各自的用途，理解端口号的作用。Goal: remember what HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, SMTP, POP3/IMAP and DNS each do, and understand port numbers.
一栋大楼有很多窗口，寄信不仅要写大楼地址（IP 地址），还要写「哪个窗口」（端口号）——网页窗口 80/443、邮件窗口 25、文件窗口 21。协议就是这个窗口「按什么规矩办事」：HTTP/HTTPS 管网页，FTP 管传文件，SMTP 管寄邮件，POP3/IMAP 管收邮件，DNS 把域名（比如 google.com）翻译成 IP 地址。 A building has many windows; addressing a letter needs the building address (IP address) and also which window (port number) — web at 80/443, mail at 25, files at 21. A protocol is "the rules that window follows": HTTP/HTTPS handles web pages, FTP transfers files, SMTP sends mail, POP3/IMAP receives mail, and DNS translates a domain name (like google.com) into an IP address.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • HTTP：网页传输；HTTPS = HTTP + TLS 加密，更安全。HTTP: transfers web pages; HTTPS = HTTP + TLS encryption, more secure.
  • FTP：文件传输。FTP: file transfer.
  • SMTP：发送邮件；POP3 / IMAP：接收邮件（IMAP 在服务器保留、可多设备同步）。SMTP: sends email; POP3 / IMAP: receives email (IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs across devices).
  • DNS：把域名解析成 IP 地址。DNS: resolves a domain name into an IP address.
  • 端口号：标识主机上「哪个服务」收数据（80=HTTP、443=HTTPS、21=FTP、25=SMTP、110=POP3、143=IMAP、53=DNS）。A port number says which service on a host receives the data (80=HTTP, 443=HTTPS, 21=FTP, 25=SMTP, 110=POP3, 143=IMAP, 53=DNS).
记忆口诀：S 开头是「发」——SMTP 发邮件；P 开头是「收」——POP3 收邮件；HTTPS 多一个 S = Secure（安全）。Memory hook: S = send (SMTP sends); P = pick up (POP3 receives); HTTPS adds an S for Secure.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: HTTP transfers web pages and HTTPS is HTTP encrypted with TLS. FTP transfers files, SMTP sends email, POP3 and IMAP receive email, and DNS translates domain names into IP addresses. A port number identifies which service on a host should receive the data.
例题Example
你在浏览器输入 www.example.com 回车，依次用到了哪些协议？You type www.example.com into a browser and press Enter. Which protocols are used, in order?
DNS：把 www.example.com 解析成 IP 地址。DNS: resolves www.example.com into an IP address. HTTPS（或 HTTP）：向该 IP 请求网页，服务器把网页内容发回。HTTPS (or HTTP): requests the page from that IP and the server sends the page back.
练习Practice
提示：多出来的那个字母是什么意思？Hint: what does the extra letter stand for?

HTTPS 比 HTTP 多了什么？What does HTTPS add over HTTP?

点开看答案Show answer
HTTPS = HTTP + TLS，数据在传输中被加密，更安全。HTTPS = HTTP + TLS, so data is encrypted in transit and is more secure.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

第 14 单元小结Unit 14 wrap-up

一条主线：通信靠分层把复杂任务拆开；传输层用 TCP（可靠）或 UDP（快）；底层用分组交换（拆包·共享·重组）代替电路交换（独占线路）；顶层是 HTTP/HTTPS、FTP、SMTP/POP3/IMAP、DNS 这些各司其职的协议。One thread: communication uses layering to split a complex task; the transport layer uses TCP (reliable) or UDP (fast); underneath, packet switching (split · share · reassemble) replaces circuit switching (dedicated line); on top sit the protocols HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, SMTP/POP3/IMAP and DNS, each doing its own job.

All are Paper 3 advanced topics.

1 RISC vs CISC：两种「CPU 说话方式」 RISC vs CISC: two ways a CPU "talks" RISC · CISC · instruction set RISC · CISC · 指令集
目标：分清 RISC 和 CISC，说出各自优缺点和典型应用。Goal: tell RISC from CISC and give their pros, cons and typical uses.
把 CPU 想象成厨房里的帮工。RISC 像只给「切菜」「点火」「装盘」这种简单口令的帮工——每句话都短、都一个动作，但要凑出一整桌菜得喊很多句。CISC 像给「做一份宫保鸡丁」这种复杂口令的帮工——一句话顶十句，但口令本身又长又难记。手机里的 ARM 走 RISC 路线（省电、简单），桌面电脑的 Intel/AMD x86 走 CISC 路线（一条指令能完成复杂操作）。 Think of the CPU as a kitchen helper. RISC is like a helper who only takes simple orders — "chop", "light the stove", "plate up" — each short and one action, but you must shout many to finish a meal. CISC is like a helper who takes complex orders such as "make kung pao chicken" — one order replaces ten, but the order itself is long and hard to memorise. ARM in phones takes the RISC route (low power, simple), while desktop Intel/AMD x86 takes the CISC route (one instruction does a complex job).
记住这几点：Remember:
  • RISC：指令简单、数量少、定长；完成同样任务要用更多条指令。典型：ARM（手机、平板）。RISC: simple, few, fixed-length instructions; needs more instructions per task. Typical: ARM (phones, tablets).
  • CISC：指令复杂、变长；一条指令能做很多事，用更少指令。典型：x86（台式机、笔记本）。CISC: complex, variable-length instructions; one instruction does a lot. Typical: x86 (desktops, laptops).
  • RISC 优点：定长易流水线、硬件简单、功耗低；缺点：程序需要更多指令、更占内存。RISC pros: fixed length suits pipelines, simple hardware, low power; cons: longer programs.
  • CISC 优点：程序更短、省内存；缺点：硬件复杂、功耗高、难做流水线。CISC pros: shorter programs, less memory; cons: complex hardware, high power, hard to pipeline.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: RISC processors use a small set of simple, fixed-length instructions, so programs need more instructions. CISC processors use complex, variable-length instructions that do more per instruction. RISC suits low-power devices like phones, while CISC suits desktops.
例题Example
为什么手机芯片多用 RISC，而台式机芯片多用 CISC？Why do phone chips mostly use RISC, while desktop chips use CISC?
RISC 指令简单、定长，硬件也简单，所以功耗低、省电——正好适合手机这种电池供电的设备。RISC instructions are simple and fixed-length, so the hardware is simple and low-power — perfect for battery-powered phones. CISC 一条指令能完成复杂操作，程序更短、省内存，适合性能要求高、不太在乎功耗的台式机。CISC does complex work per instruction, so programs are shorter — ideal for high-performance desktops that don't mind power use.
练习Practice
提示：从「指令长度是否固定」想。Hint: think about whether instruction length is fixed.

为什么 RISC 的指令比 CISC 更适合做流水线？Why are RISC instructions better suited to pipelining than CISC?

点开看答案Show answer
RISC 指令定长，每条指令耗时接近，流水线各阶段节奏整齐、容易重叠；CISC 指令变长、复杂，耗时不一，流水线难以整齐安排。RISC instructions are fixed-length, so each takes a similar time and pipeline stages overlap cleanly; CISC instructions are variable-length and complex, so the pipeline is hard to keep in step.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 并行处理：多核、流水线、SIMD Parallel processing: multi-core, pipeline, SIMD pipeline · multi-core · SIMD 流水线 · 多核 · SIMD
目标：会解释三种并行方式（多核、流水线、SIMD），并知道并行加速有上限。Goal: explain multi-core, pipelining and SIMD, and know that parallel speedup has a limit.
为什么并行能加速？想象一条洗车流水线，分「冲水、打泡沫、擦干」三步。不流水的话，每辆车要等上一辆完全洗完才开进来，一辆 3 分钟；流水之后，三辆车同时处于不同步骤，每隔 1 分钟就出一辆车。CPU 的流水线同理——把指令拆成取指、译码、执行、写回，让它们重叠。除此之外还有多核（多个帮工同时洗不同的车）和 SIMD（一个人同时拿两块海绵擦两个轮子）。但要记住 Amdahl 定律的思想：程序里不能并行的部分越多，能得到的加速就越少，所以加速有上限。 Why does parallel work speed things up? Picture a car wash with three steps: rinse, soap, dry. Without a line, each car waits for the last to finish — 3 minutes each. With a line, three cars are in different steps at once, so a car comes out every minute. A CPU pipeline does the same — it splits an instruction into fetch, decode, execute and write-back, and overlaps them. There is also multi-core (several helpers washing different cars) and SIMD (one person scrubbing two wheels at once). But remember the idea of Amdahl's law: the more of a program cannot be parallelised, the less speedup you get — so speedup has a ceiling.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 多核：多个 CPU 核心同时处理不同任务，是真正的「同时」执行。Multi-core: several CPU cores run different tasks at the same time — truly simultaneous.
  • 流水线：把指令拆成取指/译码/执行/写回，不同指令处于不同阶段重叠执行，提高吞吐量。Pipeline: split an instruction into fetch/decode/execute/write-back; different instructions overlap in different stages, raising throughput.
  • SIMD（单指令多数据）：一条指令同时对多份数据做同样操作，适合图形、视频处理。SIMD (single instruction, multiple data): one instruction does the same operation on many data items at once — great for graphics and video.
  • Amdahl 定律思想：加速受「不能并行的部分」限制，串行部分越多，加速上限越低。Amdahl's law idea: speedup is limited by the part that cannot be parallelised; the more serial work, the lower the ceiling.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A pipeline splits instruction execution into stages (fetch, decode, execute) so several instructions are processed at once, increasing throughput. Multi-core processors run tasks on separate cores, and SIMD applies one instruction to many data items at once.
例题Example
一个 4 阶段流水线，每阶段耗时 1 ns。执行 10 条指令，无流水线（每条 4 ns）和有流水线各需多久？A 4-stage pipeline takes 1 ns per stage. For 10 instructions, how long without a pipeline (4 ns each) and with one?
无流水线：10 × 4 = 40 ns。Without pipeline: 10 × 4 = 40 ns. 有流水线：第 1 条要 4 ns 走完，之后每 1 ns 出一条，共 4 + (10−1) × 1 = 13 ns。With pipeline: the first takes 4 ns, then one every 1 ns, total 4 + (10−1) × 1 = 13 ns.
练习Practice
提示：先算第一条走完的时间，再加「每拍一条」。Hint: time the first instruction, then add one cycle per instruction.

4 阶段流水线、每阶段 2 ns，执行 20 条指令要多久？A 4-stage pipeline with 2 ns per stage runs 20 instructions. How long?

点开看答案Show answer
第一条 4 × 2 = 8 ns，之后 19 条各 2 ns，共 8 + 19×2 = 46 ns。First takes 4 × 2 = 8 ns, then 19 more at 2 ns each: 8 + 19×2 = 46 ns.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 虚拟机与仿真 Virtual machines and emulation VM · hypervisor · JVM 虚拟机 · 监视器 · JVM
目标：知道虚拟机是什么，分清「系统虚拟机」和「进程虚拟机」，并说出优点与开销。Goal: know what a VM is, tell system VMs from process VMs, and give the benefits and overhead.
想象你只有一台真电脑，却想同时玩 Windows、Linux 和 macOS——虚拟机（VM）就是干这个的：它用软件模拟出一台完整的计算机（CPU、内存、硬盘全给你虚拟出来），于是你可以在里面装一整个操作系统，像开新电脑一样。负责管理和调度这些虚拟机的软件叫 hypervisor（虚拟机监视器）。虚拟机分两种：系统虚拟机模拟整台机器（如 VirtualBox、VMware）；进程虚拟机只提供一个程序运行的环境（如 JVM，专门跑 Java 程序）。代价是：软件模拟总比直接跑在硬件上慢一些。 Imagine having one real computer but wanting to run Windows, Linux and macOS at once — a virtual machine (VM) does exactly that: it uses software to emulate a whole computer (virtual CPU, memory and disk), so you can install a full operating system inside, like a brand-new machine. The software that manages these VMs is called the hypervisor. There are two kinds: a system VM emulates a whole machine (VirtualBox, VMware), while a process VM only provides a runtime environment for one program (like the JVM, which runs Java). The cost: software emulation is always slower than running directly on hardware.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 虚拟机 = 用软件模拟一台完整计算机；hypervisor 负责在一台物理机上管理多个 VM。A virtual machine is software that emulates a whole computer; the hypervisor manages several VMs on one physical machine.
  • 系统虚拟机：模拟整台机器（含硬件），可装完整 OS，如 VirtualBox、VMware。System VM: emulates a whole machine (with hardware) and runs a full OS, e.g. VirtualBox, VMware.
  • 进程虚拟机：只提供一个程序运行的环境，如 JVM 跑 Java 字节码。Process VM: provides a runtime for one program, e.g. the JVM running Java bytecode.
  • 优点：隔离、快照/迁移、资源利用率高；开销：软件模拟有性能损失，比原生运行慢。Benefits: isolation, snapshots/migration, high resource use; overhead: software emulation is slower than running natively.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A virtual machine is software that emulates a complete computer, allowing several isolated operating systems to run on one physical machine. A system VM emulates a whole machine, while a process VM such as the JVM provides a runtime environment for one language.
例题Example
解释「系统虚拟机」和「进程虚拟机（如 JVM）」的区别。Explain the difference between a system VM and a process VM (such as the JVM).
系统虚拟机模拟整台计算机（CPU、内存、外设），能在上面装一个完整的操作系统。A system VM emulates a whole computer (CPU, memory, devices), so a full OS can be installed on it. 进程虚拟机只模拟一个程序的运行环境（如 JVM 只提供 Java 字节码的执行环境），不模拟整台机器。A process VM only emulates one program's runtime (the JVM just runs Java bytecode), not a whole machine.
练习Practice
提示：从「隔离」「资源」「快照」想。Hint: think about isolation, resources and snapshots.

给出使用虚拟机的两个优点。Give two benefits of using virtual machines.

点开看答案Show answer
① 隔离——一个 VM 崩溃或中毒不影响其他 VM；② 资源利用——一台物理机同时跑多个系统；③ 快照/迁移——可整机保存或搬到别的物理机。（任写两个即可）① Isolation — one VM crashing or catching malware doesn't affect others; ② resource use — one physical machine runs many systems; ③ snapshots/migration — the whole VM can be saved or moved to another machine. (Any two)
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 布尔代数：定律与化简 Boolean algebra: laws and simplification De Morgan · distributive 德摩根 · 分配律
目标：记住基本定律，会用代数方法化简布尔表达式。Goal: learn the basic laws and simplify Boolean expressions algebraically.
布尔代数就像数字世界里的「代数运算」，只不过数字只有 0 和 1，运算只有「与（·）」「或（+）」「非（¬）」。学它干嘛？——把一个啰嗦的电路表达式化简短，就能少用几个门、省芯片。化简靠的是一组定律，最常用的是德摩根定律：把「与的否定」变成「两个否定的或」，把「或的否定」变成「两个否定的与」。就像把「不是（又高又帅）」翻译成「要么不高、要么不帅」。 Boolean algebra is like arithmetic for the digital world, except the numbers are only 0 and 1, and the operations are just AND (·), OR (+) and NOT (¬). Why learn it? To turn a clumsy circuit expression into a short one, so you use fewer gates and save silicon. Simplification relies on a set of laws, the most useful being De Morgan's law: the negation of an AND becomes an OR of negations, and the negation of an OR becomes an AND of negations. It's like turning "not (tall AND handsome)" into "either not tall OR not handsome".
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 交换律 A·B=B·A、A+B=B+A；结合律 A·(B·C)=(A·B)·C；分配律 A·(B+C)=A·B+A·C。Commutative A·B=B·A, A+B=B+A; associative A·(B·C)=(A·B)·C; distributive A·(B+C)=A·B+A·C.
  • 德摩根：¬(A·B)=¬A+¬B；¬(A+B)=¬A·¬B。De Morgan: ¬(A·B)=¬A+¬B; ¬(A+B)=¬A·¬B.
  • 吸收律：A+A·B=A；A·(A+B)=A。Absorption: A+A·B=A; A·(A+B)=A.
  • 化简思路：先展开/提出公因式（分配律），再用 A+¬A=1、A·¬A=0 消项。Approach: expand or factor first (distributive), then cancel using A+¬A=1 and A·¬A=0.
符号提醒：「·」是 AND（与）、「+」是 OR（或）、「¬」或上划线是 NOT（非）。考试里 AND 有时写作 A ∧ B，OR 写作 A ∨ B，别认错了。Notation: "·" is AND, "+" is OR, "¬" or an overbar is NOT. Exams sometimes write AND as A ∧ B and OR as A ∨ B — don't mix them up.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Boolean algebra is used to simplify logic expressions. De Morgan's laws state that NOT(A AND B) = NOT A OR NOT B, and NOT(A OR B) = NOT A AND NOT B.
例题Example
用分配律和互补律化简 X = A·B + A·¬B。Simplify X = A·B + A·¬B using the distributive law and complements.
提出公因式 A（分配律反向）：X = A·(B + ¬B)。Factor out A (distributive in reverse): X = A·(B + ¬B). B + ¬B = 1（互补律），所以 X = A·1 = A。B + ¬B = 1 (complement), so X = A·1 = A.
练习Practice
提示：直接用德摩根，把「或的否定」变成「否定的与」。Hint: apply De Morgan to turn the negation of an OR into an AND of negations.

用德摩根定律化简 ¬(A + B)。Use De Morgan's law to simplify ¬(A + B).

点开看答案Show answer
¬(A + B) = ¬A · ¬B。¬(A + B) = ¬A · ¬B.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 卡诺图化简 Karnaugh map simplification K-map · grouping 卡诺图 · 圈组
目标：会画 2、3 变量卡诺图，圈相邻的 1，并读出最简表达式。Goal: draw 2- and 3-variable K-maps, circle adjacent 1s, and read off the simplest expression.
真值表一列列看太累，卡诺图（K-map）把它重排成一张方格图，让相邻的格子之间只差一个变量。这样「能合并的 1」会挨在一起，一眼就能圈出来。圈的时候记住三条：圈相邻的 1；圈的大小必须是 2 的幂（1、2、4、8…）；圈越大越简、圈越少越好。圈完读出「圈内所有格子共同的变量」，加起来就是最简表达式。 Reading a truth table column by column is tiring, so the Karnaugh map rearranges it into a grid where adjacent cells differ in only one variable. This puts "mergeable 1s" side by side, so you can circle them at a glance. Three rules: circle adjacent 1s; the group size must be a power of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8 …); the bigger the group, the simpler the term. Then read the variables common to every cell in the group, and add the groups together.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • K-map 是重排后的真值表：2 变量 4 格，3 变量 8 格，4 变量 16 格。A K-map is a rearranged truth table: 2 variables give 4 cells, 3 give 8, 4 give 16.
  • 相邻格：只差一个变量；注意最左最右、最上最下也算相邻（首尾相接）。Adjacent cells differ in one variable; note the leftmost/rightmost and top/bottom edges also count as adjacent (they wrap around).
  • 圈相邻的 1：圈大小必须是 2 的幂（1/2/4/8）；可重叠；每个 1 至少被圈一次。Circle adjacent 1s: group size must be a power of 2 (1/2/4/8); groups may overlap; every 1 must be covered.
  • 读圈：圈内共同的变量留下，会变化的变量消掉；把所有圈相加即最简表达式。Read a group: keep the variables common to it, drop those that change; add all groups for the simplest expression.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A Karnaugh map is a rearranged truth table that groups adjacent 1s. Groups must contain 2, 4, 8 … cells, and larger groups give simpler terms. The simplified expression keeps the variables common to a group and drops those that change.
例题Example
如上方卡诺图（1 在 B=1 那一列），写出最简表达式。Using the K-map above (1s in the B=1 column), write the simplest expression.
两个 1 上下相邻（都含 B=1），圈成一个大小为 2 的组。The two 1s are vertically adjacent (both have B=1), so they form a group of size 2. 这组里 A 从 0 变 1（消掉），B 始终是 1（留下），所以 F = B。In this group A changes 0→1 (dropped) while B stays 1 (kept), so F = B.
练习Practice
提示：找出两个 1 共用的变量。Hint: find the variable the two 1s share.

若 1 在 (A=0,B=0) 和 (A=1,B=0)（左列 B=0），最简表达式是什么？If the 1s sit at (A=0,B=0) and (A=1,B=0) (the B=0 column), what is the simplest expression?

点开看答案Show answer
两格共用 B=0，A 变化消掉，所以 F = ¬B（即 NOT B）。The two cells share B=0 while A changes, so F = ¬B (NOT B).
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 用 NAND/NOR 构造任意门 Building any gate from NAND/NOR NAND · NOR · universal NAND · NOR · 万能门
目标：理解 NAND/NOR 是「万能门」，会用 NAND 搭出 NOT/AND/OR，并说出为什么芯片爱用 NAND。Goal: see why NAND/NOR are universal gates, build NOT/AND/OR from NAND, and explain why real chips prefer NAND.
逻辑门千千万，但工厂里最爱的只有一个：NAND（与非门）。为什么？因为它结构统一、制造简单，而且是万能门——光靠 NAND 就能拼出 NOT、AND、OR，进而拼出一切电路。NOR（或非门）也一样万能。窍门就藏在德摩根定律里：NAND(A,B) = ¬(A·B) = ¬A + ¬B。把两个输入接一起，NAND 就退化成 NOT；NOT 加 NAND 又能变出 AND 和 OR。 There are many logic gates, but factories love one above all: NAND. Why? It is uniform and cheap to build, and it is a universal gate — NAND alone can build NOT, AND and OR, and therefore any circuit. NOR is universal too. The trick hides in De Morgan's law: NAND(A,B) = ¬(A·B) = ¬A + ¬B. Tie both inputs together and NAND becomes NOT; add a NOT to a NAND and you get AND and OR.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • NAND = NOT AND，输出 ¬(A·B)；NOR = NOT OR，输出 ¬(A+B)。NAND = NOT AND, output ¬(A·B); NOR = NOT OR, output ¬(A+B).
  • NAND 和 NOR 都是万能门，只用其中一种就能构造任意逻辑电路。NAND and NOR are universal gates; either one alone can build any logic circuit.
  • 用 NAND 搭 NOT：两输入接一起；搭 AND：NAND 后接 NOT；搭 OR：¬A、¬B 进 NAND（德摩根）。With NAND: make NOT by tying inputs together; AND by following NAND with a NOT; OR by feeding ¬A, ¬B into a NAND (De Morgan).
  • 为什么爱用 NAND/NOR：制造简单、结构统一、成本低，芯片上便于大规模重复。Why NAND/NOR: simple to fabricate, uniform structure, low cost, easy to repeat across a chip.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: NAND and NOR are universal gates: any logic circuit can be built from NAND gates alone. To make NOT, tie both inputs together; to make AND, follow a NAND with an inverter; to make OR, feed inverted inputs into a NAND (De Morgan's law).
例题Example
解释为什么 NAND 被称为「万能门」，并说明如何用它搭出 NOT。Explain why NAND is called a "universal gate" and how to build NOT from it.
「万能门」= 只用这一种门就能构造出所有逻辑功能（NOT、AND、OR…）。"Universal gate" = this one gate alone can build every logic function (NOT, AND, OR …). 搭 NOT：把 NAND 的两个输入接到同一个信号 A 上，输出 = ¬(A·A) = ¬A，就是 NOT。Build NOT: connect both NAND inputs to the same signal A; output = ¬(A·A) = ¬A, which is NOT.
练习Practice
提示：用德摩根 ¬(A·B)=¬A+¬B。Hint: use De Morgan, ¬(A·B)=¬A+¬B.

用 NAND 和德摩根定律说明如何得到 OR（A+B）。Using NAND and De Morgan's law, show how to obtain OR (A+B).

点开看答案Show answer
先各用一个 NAND（两输入接一起）得到 ¬A 和 ¬B，再把它们送进第三个 NAND：输出 = ¬(¬A·¬B) = A + B（德摩根）。所以 A+B = NAND(¬A, ¬B)。First get ¬A and ¬B with two NANDs (inputs tied), then feed them into a third NAND: output = ¬(¬A·¬B) = A + B (De Morgan). So A+B = NAND(¬A, ¬B).
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

第 15 单元小结Unit 15 wrap-up

这一单元两条线并进：一条是让 CPU 更快——RISC 靠简单定长的指令、CISC 靠复杂指令，并行处理用多核、流水线和 SIMD 来提速，虚拟机让一台机器当多台用；另一条是让电路更省——布尔代数和卡诺图帮你化简表达式，NAND/NOR 这两个万能门能搭出一切。记住主线：硬件设计永远在「快」和「省」之间找平衡。This unit ran two threads side by side: making CPUs faster — RISC uses simple fixed-length instructions while CISC uses complex ones, parallel processing speeds things up with multi-core, pipelines and SIMD, and VMs make one machine act as many; and making circuits cheaper — Boolean algebra and K-maps simplify expressions, and the universal NAND/NOR gates build everything. The thread running through it all: hardware always balances "fast" against "cheap".
