CAIE 9618 Topic 16 · 4 站 · 操作系统怎么管内存、管中断，翻译软件如何链接加载CAIE 9618 Topic 16 · 4 stops · how the OS manages memory and interrupts, and how translation software links and loads

路线图Roadmap本单元 4 站，从「操作系统怎么管内存」一路走到「程序怎么被拼装、怎么跨平台运行」4 stops, from "how the OS manages memory" to "how programs are assembled and run across platforms"

  1. 内存管理：分页、分段与虚拟内存Memory management: paging, segmentation & virtual memory
  2. 中断与调度进阶Interrupts and advanced scheduling
  3. 链接器、加载器与库Linkers, loaders and libraries
  4. 中间代码与 JITIntermediate code and JIT

这一单元把「操作系统」和「翻译软件」讲深一层：内存不够用怎么办、CPU 怎么在多个任务间公平排班、编译完之后程序还差哪几步才能真的跑起来。This unit goes one level deeper into the OS and translation software: what to do when memory runs short, how the CPU shares time fairly, and the extra steps after compilation.

1 内存管理：分页、分段与虚拟内存 Memory management: paging, segmentation & virtual memory paging · segmentation · virtual memory 分页 · 分段 · 虚拟内存
目标：分清分页、分段、虚拟内存，并说出它们为什么存在。Goal: tell paging, segmentation and virtual memory apart, and explain why they exist.
想象你有一张 8 格的桌面（内存），却要同时摊开 3 份作业，每份要 4 格——格子根本不够。操作系统有两个办法：一是把桌面切成固定大小的页，作业也切成同样大小的块，谁用哪块随时换着用（这就是分页）；二是干脆把暂时不用的东西先塞回书包（磁盘），假装桌面变大了，要用时再拿回来（这就是虚拟内存）。分段则是按「逻辑」切——代码一堆、数据一堆、栈一堆，每堆大小不一样。 Picture a desk with 8 slots (memory) but 3 assignments each needing 4 slots — there simply isn't room. The OS has two tricks: cut the desk into fixed-size pages, cut each assignment into matching blocks, and swap blocks around as needed (paging); or stash unused bits back in your bag (disk) and pretend the desk is bigger, pulling them out when needed (virtual memory). Segmentation cuts by "logic" — code in one lump, data in another, the stack in another, each a different size.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 分页 paging：内存和进程都切成固定大小的页，页表负责把逻辑地址翻译成物理地址。Paging: memory and processes are cut into fixed-size pages; a page table maps logical to physical addresses.
  • 分段 segmentation：按逻辑块（代码段、数据段、栈）切，各段大小不固定。Segmentation: cut into logical blocks (code, data, stack), each a different size.
  • 虚拟内存 virtual memory：用磁盘空间模拟更大的内存，缺页时执行页置换（换出/换入）。Virtual memory: uses disk to simulate more memory, swapping pages in and out when one is missing.
  • 为什么需要：多个任务互相隔离、不会越界；内存不够用时也能跑更大的程序。Why we need them: tasks stay isolated from each other, and bigger programs can run when memory is short.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Paging divides memory into fixed-size pages, while segmentation splits a program into logical blocks of different sizes. Virtual memory uses disk space to simulate more memory, swapping pages in and out when needed.
例题Example
一个程序需要 6 页，但物理内存只能同时放 4 页，操作系统怎么让它跑起来？A program needs 6 pages but RAM only holds 4. How does the OS let it run?
用虚拟内存：物理内存放不下的页，先放到磁盘的交换区。Use virtual memory: pages that don't fit in RAM go to the swap area on disk. 运行时如果访问的页不在内存（缺页），就执行页置换：把不常用的页换出到磁盘，再把需要的页换入内存。At run time, if a needed page is not in RAM (page fault), a page swap moves a less-used page out to disk and brings the needed one in.
练习Practice
提示：看「块的大小是否固定」。Hint: look at whether block sizes are fixed.

分页和分段最本质的区别是什么？What is the key difference between paging and segmentation?

点开看答案Show answer
分页把内存和进程切成固定大小、彼此相等的页；分段按逻辑意义切（代码/数据/栈），各段大小不固定。Paging cuts memory and processes into fixed, equal-size pages; segmentation splits by logical meaning (code/data/stack), so segments have different sizes.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 中断与调度进阶 Interrupts and advanced scheduling interrupt · scheduling · context switch 中断 · 调度 · 上下文切换
目标：理解中断为什么比轮询高效，并能说出几种调度算法和上下文切换。Goal: see why interrupts beat polling, and name scheduling algorithms and context switching.
CPU 干活飞快，外设（键盘、硬盘）却很慢。如果 CPU 一直傻等、反复问「好了吗好了吗」，那就是轮询，太浪费。更好的办法是中断——外设做完了自己「敲门」（发一个中断信号），CPU 停下手里的事去处理，处理完再回来。当好几个程序都想用 CPU，还得有人「排班」，这就是调度算法。 The CPU is blazing fast but devices (keyboard, disk) are slow. If the CPU just waits and keeps asking "done yet?", that's polling — a waste. Better is an interrupt: the device "knocks" (sends an interrupt signal) when it's ready, and the CPU pauses to handle it, then returns. When several programs want the CPU at once, someone must "draw up a rota" — that's the scheduling algorithm.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 轮询 polling：CPU 反复检查设备状态，浪费 CPU 时间；中断 interrupt：设备主动通知 CPU，效率高。Polling: the CPU keeps checking the device, wasting time; an interrupt: the device notifies the CPU, which is efficient.
  • 中断有优先级：急事（如电源告警）先处理，低优先级的可被更高优先级打断。Interrupts have priorities: urgent ones (e.g. power alarm) go first, and lower ones can be interrupted by higher ones.
  • 调度算法：轮转 RR（每人一个时间片轮流）、最短剩余时间 SRT（谁剩下的活最少先做）、多级队列（把任务分到不同优先级队列）。Scheduling algorithms: Round Robin (a time slice each in turn), Shortest Remaining Time (least work left goes first), multilevel queue (tasks split into priority queues).
  • 上下文切换 context switch：切换进程时保存当前进程的状态（程序计数器、寄存器等），再加载下一个的状态。Context switch: when switching, save the current process's state (program counter, registers) and load the next one's.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: An interrupt is a signal from a device that makes the CPU suspend its current task and run a handler. Interrupts are more efficient than polling because the CPU does not waste time repeatedly checking devices. A context switch saves the state of the current process and loads the state of the next.
例题Example
为什么中断比轮询更节省 CPU 时间？Why does an interrupt save more CPU time than polling?
轮询时 CPU 要不断主动查询设备，大部分查询是白费的。With polling the CPU keeps actively querying the device, and most checks are wasted. 中断只在设备就绪时才通知 CPU，因此 CPU 能把空闲时间用来做别的事，效率更高。An interrupt notifies the CPU only when the device is ready, so the CPU can use its spare time elsewhere — more efficient.
练习Practice
提示：想想进程被暂停后，要恢复它需要哪些信息。Hint: think about what you need to resume a paused process.

上下文切换（context switch）时，操作系统要保存什么？What must the OS save during a context switch?

点开看答案Show answer
要保存进程的当前状态——程序计数器 PC、寄存器内容等，以便稍后能从中断处继续执行。It saves the process's current state — the program counter (PC), register contents and so on — so it can later continue where it left off.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 链接器、加载器与库 Linkers, loaders and libraries linker · loader · DLL 链接器 · 加载器 · 动态库
目标：知道编译之后还差「链接」和「加载」，并能区分静态链接与动态链接。Goal: know that linking and loading follow compilation, and tell static from dynamic linking.
很多人以为编译完就完事了。其实编译只是把你写的 .c/.cpp 翻译成目标文件（.o），里面还可能调用了库函数（比如 printf）。把这些「零件」粘成一个能运行的整体，是链接器（linker）的活。粘好之后，还要靠加载器（loader）把程序从硬盘装进内存，才能真正跑起来。链接有两种粘法：出厂前就粘死（静态链接），或者运行到一半需要时再去取共享库（动态链接）。 Many think compiling is the last step. In fact it only turns your .c/.cpp into an object file (.o), which may also call library functions like printf. Gluing these parts into one runnable whole is the linker's job. Then the loader moves the program from disk into memory so it can actually run. Linking has two glues: fixed at build time (static linking), or fetching a shared library when needed at run time (dynamic linking).
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 编译 compile：源码 → 目标文件（机器码，但地址未定、符号未解析）。Compile: source → object file (machine code, but addresses and symbols unresolved).
  • 链接 link：链接器把多个目标文件 + 库合并成一个可执行文件。Link: the linker merges object files and libraries into one executable.
  • 静态链接 static：库代码直接复制进可执行文件，文件大但独立；动态链接 dynamic：运行时加载共享库（如 Windows 的 .dll、Linux 的 .so），文件小、可共享、省内存。Static linking: library code is copied into the executable — bigger but self-contained; dynamic linking: shared libraries (e.g. .dll on Windows, .so on Linux) load at run time — smaller, shareable, less memory.
  • 加载 load：加载器把程序装入内存，交给 CPU 执行。Load: the loader puts the program into memory and hands it to the CPU.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A linker combines object files and libraries into a single executable, resolving references between them. Static linking copies library code into the executable, while dynamic linking loads shared libraries (such as DLLs) at run time. A loader then loads the program into memory.
例题Example
动态链接相比静态链接有什么优点？What advantage does dynamic linking have over static linking?
多个程序共享同一份库文件，节省磁盘和内存。Several programs share one copy of the library, saving disk and memory. 库更新时不用重新编译程序；但缺点是运行时必须能找到库，否则报错。Libraries can be updated without recompiling; the drawback is the library must be present at run time or it fails.
练习Practice
提示：想想「零件变成品」。Hint: think of "parts becoming a finished product".

链接器（linker）具体做哪件事？What exactly does a linker do?

点开看答案Show answer
把编译产生的多个目标文件与所需的库合并，解析符号引用（比如函数调用地址），生成一个完整的可执行文件。It merges the object files and libraries, resolves symbol references (e.g. function call addresses), and produces one complete executable.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 中间代码与 JIT Intermediate code and JIT bytecode · JVM · JIT 字节码 · Java 虚拟机 · 即时编译
目标：理解中间代码（字节码）是什么，以及 JVM/JIT 如何实现跨平台。Goal: understand intermediate code (bytecode) and how the JVM/JIT achieve portability.
有些语言（比如 C）直接编译成某台机器的机器码，换台电脑就可能跑不了。Java 想了个办法：先编译成一种「中间代码」——字节码（bytecode），它不针对任何具体机器；到了哪台电脑，就由那台电脑上的 JVM（Java 虚拟机）把字节码解释执行，或者用 JIT（即时编译）边跑边翻成那台机器的机器码。于是同一份字节码到处都能跑——「一次编写，到处运行」。 Some languages (like C) compile straight into one machine's machine code, so they may not run on another computer. Java's idea: first compile to an intermediate form — bytecode — tied to no specific machine. On any computer, that machine's JVM (Java Virtual Machine) interprets the bytecode, or a JIT (just-in-time) compiler translates it into that machine's code as it runs. So one bytecode runs everywhere — "write once, run anywhere".
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 中间代码 / 字节码 bytecode：介于源码和机器码之间，与具体机器无关。Intermediate code / bytecode: between source and machine code, independent of any specific machine.
  • 虚拟机解释：JVM 逐条解释字节码执行，通用但较慢。Interpretation: the JVM interprets bytecode line by line — portable but slower.
  • JIT 即时编译：把常用的字节码在运行时翻译成本机机器码，之后直接执行，提速。JIT: translates frequently-used bytecode into native machine code at run time, then runs it directly for speed.
  • 为什么这么设计：跨平台——同一份字节码可在任何装了 JVM 的平台上运行。Why: portability — the same bytecode runs on any platform with a JVM.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Java source is compiled into platform-independent bytecode. The Java Virtual Machine (JVM) then interprets this bytecode, or uses a just-in-time (JIT) compiler to translate it into native machine code at run time, so the same program runs on any platform.
例题Example
为什么 Java 能做到「一次编写，到处运行」？Why can Java run "write once, run anywhere"?
Java 源码先编译成与平台无关的字节码。Java source is first compiled into platform-independent bytecode. 每台机器上的 JVM 负责把字节码翻译成本机机器码执行，所以同一份字节码到处可用。Each machine's JVM translates the bytecode into its own machine code, so the same bytecode runs everywhere.
练习Practice
提示：从「什么时候翻译、要不要反复翻」想。Hint: think about when translation happens and whether it repeats.

JIT（即时编译）和纯解释有什么区别？How does JIT differ from pure interpretation?

点开看答案Show answer
纯解释是每次运行都逐条翻译执行；JIT 把热点代码一次性编译成本机机器码，之后直接执行，更快。Pure interpretation translates and runs line by line every time; JIT compiles hot code into native machine code once, then runs it directly — faster.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —

第 16 单元小结Unit 16 wrap-up

这一单元把系统软件讲深了一层：内存靠分页、分段、虚拟内存来「既隔离又够用」；CPU 靠中断高效响应外设、靠调度算法公平排班，切换进程时要上下文切换；程序从编译到能跑还差「链接」和「加载」两步，链接分静态与动态；Java 这类语言靠字节码 + JVM/JIT 实现跨平台。一条主线：操作系统在幕后做资源管理，让多个程序和平共处、让内存和 CPU 物尽其用。This unit went one level deeper into system software: memory uses paging, segmentation and virtual memory to stay isolated yet sufficient; the CPU responds to devices through interrupts, shares time fairly with scheduling, and context-switches between processes; a program still needs linking and loading after compilation, with static or dynamic linking; and languages like Java use bytecode plus a JVM/JIT for portability. One thread runs through it all: the OS manages resources behind the scenes, letting many programs coexist and making the most of memory and CPU.

这是 Paper 3 的安全进阶——抓住「加密到底怎么工作」这条主线，比死记一堆算法名字重要得多。This is Paper 3 advanced security — grasp how encryption actually works, which matters far more than memorising algorithm names.

1 对称 vs 非对称加密 Symmetric vs asymmetric encryption symmetric · asymmetric · key 对称 · 非对称 · 密钥
目标：分清对称与非对称加密各自的特点，并明白为什么要「混合使用」。Goal: tell symmetric and asymmetric apart, and see why we "mix" them.
想象你寄一个上锁的盒子。对称加密就像用一把钥匙上锁，收件人也得用同一把钥匙开——问题是怎么把这把钥匙安全送到对方手里。于是有了非对称加密：给每人配两把钥匙，一把公开（公钥），一把藏好（私钥）；别人用你的公钥上锁，只有你的私钥能打开，根本不用先递钥匙，代价是算得慢。现实中常混合使用：先用非对称加密安全地传一把「一次性对称钥匙」过去，之后大量数据就用这把对称钥匙快速加密。 Imagine posting a locked box. Symmetric encryption is like locking it with one key — the receiver must use the same key to open it, so how do you get that key to them safely? So we have asymmetric encryption: each person gets two keys, one public and one private; others lock with your public key, only your private key can open it. No key needs to be sent first — the cost is that it is slower. In practice we mix them: use asymmetric encryption to safely send a one-off symmetric key, then encrypt the bulk of the data quickly with that symmetric key.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 对称加密：加密和解密用同一把钥匙，速度快；但钥匙怎么安全传递是难题。Symmetric: the same key encrypts and decrypts, fast; the hard part is delivering the key safely.
  • 非对称加密：公钥加密、私钥解密，解决了密钥分发，但计算慢。Asymmetric: public key encrypts, private key decrypts — solves key distribution but is slow.
  • 混合使用：先用非对称加密传递一把对称密钥，之后用对称加密传输数据——HTTPS 就这么干。Hybrid: use asymmetric to deliver a symmetric key, then symmetric for the data — that is what HTTPS does.
  • 公钥可以公开，私钥绝不能给任何人。The public key may be shared; the private key must never be given out.
小提醒：考试常问「为什么非对称更安全却更慢」——答案就一句：它靠复杂的数学运算，而且双方不必共享同一个密钥。Tip: exams often ask "why is asymmetric safer but slower" — one line: it relies on heavy maths, and the two sides never share the same key.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Symmetric encryption uses the same key to encrypt and decrypt, so it is fast but the key must be shared securely. Asymmetric encryption uses a public key to encrypt and a private key to decrypt, solving key distribution at the cost of speed.
例题Example
为什么网站不全程用非对称加密，而是「先非对称、后对称」混合使用？Why do websites not use asymmetric encryption the whole time, but mix "asymmetric first, symmetric after"?
非对称加密能安全地协商出对称密钥，但计算慢，全程用会拖慢通信。Asymmetric encryption can safely agree a symmetric key, but it is slow, so using it throughout would slow everything down. 所以先非对称传一把对称密钥，之后用对称加密快速传大量数据——既安全又快。So it first uses asymmetric to pass a symmetric key, then symmetric to send data quickly — both secure and fast.
练习Practice
提示：公钥是给大家用的，私钥才藏起来。Hint: the public key is for everyone; the private key is kept hidden.

小明想给小红发密信，又不想事先传钥匙，他应该用谁的什么钥匙加密？Ming wants to send Hong a secret note without passing a key first. Whose key should he encrypt with?

点开看答案Show answer
用小红的公钥加密，小红用自己的私钥解密——因为公钥公开、私钥保密，不用事先递钥匙。Encrypt with Hong's public key; she decrypts with her private key — the public key is open, the private key is secret, so no key needs to be sent first.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 加密算法：从凯撒到 AES/RSA Encryption algorithms: Caesar to AES/RSA Caesar · XOR · DES · AES · RSA 凯撒 · XOR · DES · AES · RSA
目标：认识从古典到现代的几种加密算法，理解「密钥越长越难破解」。Goal: meet the algorithms from classical to modern, and see that longer keys are harder to crack.
最古老的加密之一叫凯撒密码——把每个字母往后移几位（比如 +3，A 变 D）。XOR 加密则把明文和密钥逐位做「异或」运算，速度飞快，适合简单混淆。现代真正用的是升级版：DES 和 AES 是对称加密的主力（AES 现在是主流）；RSA 是非对称加密的代表，它的安全性建立在「把两个大质数相乘容易、反过来分解却极难」这件事上。核心规律只有一条：密钥越长，暴力破解要试的组合越多，就越难破。 One of the oldest ciphers is the Caesar cipher — shift each letter a few places (say +3, A becomes D). XOR encryption combines plaintext with a key bit by bit and is very fast, good for simple scrambling. The modern upgrades are what we really use: DES and AES are the main symmetric algorithms (AES is now standard); RSA is the key asymmetric one, safe because "multiplying two big primes is easy, but factoring the result back is extremely hard". One rule sums it up: the longer the key, the more combinations a brute-force attacker must try, so the harder it is to crack.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 凯撒密码：字母按固定位数移位，是最简单的移位密码，易被破解。Caesar cipher: letters shift a fixed amount — the simplest cipher, easy to break.
  • XOR 加密：明文与密钥逐位异或，再用同一个密钥异或一次即可还原（可逆）。XOR encryption: XOR plaintext with a key bit by bit; XOR again with the same key to recover it (reversible).
  • DES / AES 是常见对称算法（AES 是当前主流）；RSA 是非对称算法。DES/AES are common symmetric algorithms (AES is standard now); RSA is asymmetric.
  • RSA 的安全性基于大整数分解困难；密钥越长越难暴力破解。RSA's safety rests on the difficulty of factoring large integers; longer keys resist brute force better.
小提醒：别死记算法名，要记住这组对应——AES=对称、RSA=非对称，选择题特别爱考。Tip: don't memorise names — just remember this pairing: AES = symmetric, RSA = asymmetric. Multiple-choice loves it.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: The Caesar cipher shifts each letter by a fixed amount, and XOR encryption combines plaintext with a key bit by bit. AES is a widely used symmetric algorithm, while RSA is asymmetric and relies on the difficulty of factorising large numbers.
例题Example
凯撒密码移位 +3 时，ZEBRA 会变成什么？With a Caesar shift of +3, what does ZEBRA become?
Z→C（绕回）、E→H、B→E、R→U、A→D。Z→C (wraps), E→H, B→E, R→U, A→D. 所以密文是 CHEUD。So the ciphertext is CHEUD.
练习Practice
提示：异或规则是「相同为 0，不同为 1」。Hint: XOR gives 0 when bits match, 1 when they differ.

用 XOR 加密时，明文位 1 与密钥位 1 异或的结果是多少？In XOR encryption, what is plaintext bit 1 XOR key bit 1?

点开看答案Show answer
1 XOR 1 = 0（相同为 0）。1 XOR 1 = 0 (matching bits give 0).
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 数字签名与数字证书 Digital signatures and certificates signature · hash · certificate · CA 签名 · 哈希 · 证书 · CA
目标：理解数字签名怎么证明「来源真实 + 未被篡改」，以及数字证书如何把公钥和身份绑在一起。Goal: see how a signature proves "authentic + unaltered", and how a certificate binds a public key to an identity.
普通加密只解决「别人看不懂」，没解决「这封信到底是不是本人发的、有没有被掉包」。数字签名补上这一环：发送方先给消息算一个「指纹」（哈希），再用自己的私钥给这个指纹加密，得到数字签名，随消息一起发出去。接收方用发送方的公钥解开签名、再重新算一遍哈希，两下一对比：一致就说明消息没被改、且确实是发送方签的。那公钥本身怎么确认是真的？靠数字证书——由受信任的认证中心 CA签发，把「公钥 + 持有者身份」绑定在一起，还盖上 CA 自己的签名。 Ordinary encryption only stops people reading the message — it does not prove who sent it or whether it was swapped. A digital signature fills that gap: the sender computes a "fingerprint" (hash) of the message, encrypts that hash with their private key to make the signature, and sends it with the message. The receiver decrypts the signature with the sender's public key, recomputes the hash, and compares: if they match, the message was not changed and really was signed by the sender. And how do we know the public key itself is genuine? Through a digital certificate, issued by a trusted certificate authority (CA), which binds a public key to its owner's identity and carries the CA's own signature.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 数字签名：发送方用私钥签名，接收方用公钥验证——证明来源真实、内容未被篡改。Digital signature: sender signs with the private key, receiver verifies with the public key — proves authenticity and integrity.
  • 流程：先对消息做哈希（摘要），再对哈希用私钥加密得到签名。Flow: first hash the message, then encrypt that hash with the private key to form the signature.
  • 数字证书：由 CA 颁发，把公钥与持有者身份绑定，防止公钥被冒充。Digital certificate: issued by a CA, it binds a public key to its owner to stop the key being impersonated.
  • 加密管「保密」，签名管「认证与完整性」——两者目的不同，常一起用。Encryption gives confidentiality; signatures give authenticity and integrity — different jobs, often used together.
小提醒：记住一句话——私钥签名、公钥验证，正好和「公钥加密、私钥解密」反过来。Tip: remember one line — sign with the private key, verify with the public key, the reverse of "encrypt with public, decrypt with private".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A digital signature is created by encrypting a hash of the message with the sender's private key, and verified with the sender's public key. It proves the message is authentic and has not been altered. A digital certificate, issued by a CA, binds a public key to its owner's identity.
例题Example
接收方收到消息和数字签名后，怎么判断消息有没有被篡改？After receiving a message and its signature, how does the receiver tell if the message was altered?
用发送方的公钥解开签名，得到发送方当初算出的哈希。Decrypt the signature with the sender's public key to get the original hash. 自己再对收到的消息算一次哈希，两者一致说明没被改；不一致说明被改过。Recompute the hash of the received message; if they match it was not changed, if not it was altered.
练习Practice
提示：想一想和「公钥加密、私钥解密」的方向有什么不同。Hint: compare with the direction of "encrypt with public, decrypt with private".

数字签名用的是哪把钥匙签名、哪把钥匙验证？Which key signs, and which key verifies, a digital signature?

点开看答案Show answer
私钥签名、公钥验证。Private key signs, public key verifies.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 TLS/SSL 与 HTTPS TLS/SSL and HTTPS TLS · handshake · HTTPS TLS · 握手 · HTTPS
目标：看懂 TLS 握手流程，知道 HTTPS 就是「HTTP + TLS」。Goal: follow the TLS handshake and know that HTTPS is "HTTP + TLS".
你访问网站时地址栏出现的那把小锁，背后是 TLS（SSL 是它的老名字）。它的作用是在你和网站之间铺一条「安全通道」。过程叫握手：浏览器和服务器先互相打个招呼、协商用哪些加密算法，服务器亮出自己的数字证书证明身份，然后双方用非对称加密的办法安全地协商出一把「会话密钥」（对称密钥）——这一步慢但只做一次；之后所有数据都用这把对称密钥加密传输——这一步快。HTTPS 就是普通 HTTP 套上这层 TLS。 That little padlock in your browser's address bar is TLS (with SSL as its old name). It builds a "secure tunnel" between you and the site. The process is a handshake: the browser and server first greet each other and negotiate which algorithms to use, the server shows its digital certificate to prove its identity, then they use asymmetric encryption to safely agree a "session key" (a symmetric key) — slow, but done only once. After that, all data is encrypted with this symmetric key — fast. HTTPS is just ordinary HTTP wrapped in this TLS layer.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • TLS 握手：协商算法 → 服务器出示证书 → 用非对称加密协商出对称密钥。TLS handshake: negotiate algorithms → server shows its certificate → agree a symmetric key using asymmetric encryption.
  • 之后的数据传输改用对称加密（快）；非对称只用在建立阶段。Later data uses symmetric encryption (fast); asymmetric is only for the setup phase.
  • HTTPS = HTTP + TLS，浏览器地址栏的锁表示连接已被加密。HTTPS = HTTP + TLS; the padlock in the address bar means the connection is encrypted.
  • 证书用来验证服务器身份，防止中间人冒充。The certificate verifies the server's identity and stops impersonation.
小提醒：记握手流程就用三个词——协商 → 证书 → 换对称密钥。Tip: remember the handshake in three words — negotiate → certificate → symmetric key.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: In a TLS handshake, the client and server agree on algorithms, the server presents its certificate, and they use asymmetric encryption to agree a symmetric session key. Data is then encrypted with this symmetric key, which is much faster. HTTPS is HTTP running over TLS.
例题Example
为什么 TLS 握手之后要「换回」对称加密来传输数据？Why does TLS switch back to symmetric encryption for data after the handshake?
非对称加密安全但慢，全程用会拖慢通信。Asymmetric encryption is secure but slow, so using it throughout would slow the connection. 握手阶段已经安全协商出对称密钥，之后用对称加密传输，又快又安全。The handshake has already agreed a symmetric key, so symmetric encryption afterwards is fast and secure.
练习Practice
提示：想想那层加密协议叫什么。Hint: think of the name of the encryption layer.

浏览器地址栏的「锁」图标表示什么？What does the padlock icon in the address bar mean?

点开看答案Show answer
表示浏览器和服务器之间通过 HTTPS（HTTP + TLS）建立了加密连接。It means the browser and server have an encrypted connection via HTTPS (HTTP + TLS).
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 加密的局限与攻击 Limits of encryption and attacks MITM · social engineering · key management 中间人 · 社会工程学 · 密钥管理
目标：认识加密的三大局限——中间人攻击、社会工程学、密钥管理，明白「加密不是万能」。Goal: meet encryption's three limits — MITM, social engineering, key management — and see that encryption is not a cure-all.
加密能防住「偷听」，但防不住三种情况。一是中间人攻击（MITM）：攻击者插在你和网站之间，你以为是网站、网站以为是你，双方的内容他都看得见——所以光加密还不够，还得用证书验证身份。二是社会工程学：人一不留神，骗子一个电话、一封钓鱼邮件，就能把密码骗走，人永远是最薄弱的环节。三是密钥管理：私钥丢了、泄露了、或被偷了，再强的加密也白搭。所以加密只是安全的一环，而不是万能保险。 Encryption stops eavesdropping, but not three things. First, the man-in-the-middle attack (MITM): an attacker slips between you and the site — you think it is the site, the site thinks it is you, and he sees everything — so encryption alone is not enough; you also need certificates to verify identity. Second, social engineering: one careless moment and a scammer's phone call or phishing email can trick a password out of you — people are always the weakest link. Third, key management: if a private key is lost, leaked or stolen, the strongest encryption is useless. So encryption is one part of security, not a magic shield.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 中间人攻击（MITM）：攻击者伪装成通信双方，截获并可能篡改信息。Man-in-the-middle (MITM): the attacker impersonates both parties, intercepting and possibly altering the messages.
  • 社会工程学：利用人的疏忽或信任骗出密码等信息，人是最薄弱的环节。Social engineering: exploiting carelessness or trust to trick out passwords — people are the weakest link.
  • 密钥管理：私钥泄露、丢失或被偷，都会让加密失效。Key management: a leaked, lost or stolen private key defeats the encryption.
  • 加密防「偷听」，但防不住骗人和泄密；安全需要「技术 + 人」一起把关。Encryption stops eavesdropping but not trickery or leaks; security needs both technology and people.
小提醒：考试常见「说一个加密无法防范的威胁」，答 MITM（若无证书验证）或社会工程学最稳。Tip: a common question is "name a threat encryption cannot prevent" — answer MITM (without certificate verification) or social engineering.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Encryption cannot prevent all threats. In a man-in-the-middle attack, an attacker sits between the two parties and impersonates each to the other, so certificates are needed to verify identity. Social engineering exploits human weaknesses, and poor key management can expose keys. Encryption is only one part of security.
例题Example
为什么「只加密、不验证身份」仍然可能被中间人攻击？Why can "encrypt but never verify identity" still fall to a man-in-the-middle attack?
加密只保证传输内容不被偷看，没保证另一端是谁。Encryption only keeps the content from being read; it does not guarantee who is at the other end. 攻击者可以分别和双方建立加密连接，各自冒充对方，从而读到并转发信息。An attacker can open encrypted connections to each side, impersonating each to the other, and so read and relay the messages. 所以还需要数字证书来验证身份。That is why a digital certificate is needed to verify identity.
练习Practice
提示：想想这是「骗人」还是「破译密码」。Hint: is this "tricking people" or "cracking encryption"?

黑客打电话冒充 IT 部门要你的登录密码，这属于哪类攻击？A hacker phones you, pretending to be IT, and asks for your login password. What kind of attack is this?

点开看答案Show answer
社会工程学——利用人的信任骗出信息，而不是靠技术破解加密。Social engineering — using trust to trick out information, not cracking encryption by technical means.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —

第 17 单元小结Unit 17 wrap-up

这一单元把「加密怎么工作」讲透了：对称用同一把钥匙（快），非对称用公钥加密、私钥解密（解决密钥分发），两者混合使用；数字签名靠「私钥签名、公钥验证」证明来源真实，数字证书把公钥和身份绑在一起；TLS 握手先用非对称协商出对称密钥、之后转对称加密，这就是 HTTPS。但加密不是万能——中间人攻击、社会工程学、密钥管理，处处提醒我们安全是「技术 + 人」的事。This unit covered how encryption works: symmetric uses one key (fast), asymmetric encrypts with the public key and decrypts with the private (solving key distribution), and they are mixed; a digital signature uses "sign with private, verify with public" to prove authenticity, while a digital certificate binds a key to an identity; the TLS handshake agrees a symmetric key using asymmetric encryption, then switches to symmetric — that is HTTPS. But encryption is not a cure-all: MITM, social engineering and key management all remind us that security is about technology and people.

第 18 单元 · 人工智能Unit 18 · Artificial Intelligence Paper 3

CAIE 9618 Topic 18 · 6 站 · 让机器「显得会思考」：专家系统、机器学习、神经网络CAIE 9618 Topic 18 · 6 stops · making machines "seem to think": expert systems, machine learning, neural networks

路线图Roadmap本单元 6 站，从「AI 是什么」一路走到「AI 的局限与伦理」6 stops, from "what is AI" to "limitations and ethics"

  1. 什么是 AI：强 AI 与弱 AI，还有图灵测试What is AI: strong vs weak AI, and the Turing test
  2. 专家系统：知识库 + 推理机 + 界面Expert systems: knowledge base + inference engine + interface
  3. 机器学习：监督 / 无监督 / 强化Machine learning: supervised / unsupervised / reinforcement
  4. 神经网络与深度学习Neural networks and deep learning
  5. AI 的应用：语音、图像、语言、推荐、驾驶AI applications: speech, vision, language, recommendations, driving
  6. AI 的局限与伦理AI limitations and ethics

AI 不是魔法，它由「数据 + 规则 + 算力」堆起来。这一单元先分清强弱 AI，再看专家系统、机器学习和神经网络三种造法，最后聊聊它做不到什么、要担什么责任。AI is not magic — it is built from data, rules and computing power. We first tell strong from weak AI, then meet expert systems, machine learning and neural networks, and finally look at what it cannot do and the responsibilities it brings.

1 什么是 AI：强 AI 与弱 AI What is AI: strong vs weak AI strong AI · weak AI · Turing test 强 AI · 弱 AI · 图灵测试
目标：分清「强 AI」和「弱 AI」，并能复述图灵测试在考什么。Goal: tell strong AI from weak AI, and say what the Turing test checks.
很多人一听「人工智能」就想到会自己思考的机器人，那其实是 强 AI——通用智能，像人一样什么都能学，目前还没造出来（还在科幻片里）。现实中你天天用的其实是 弱 AI：只在某一件事上特别厉害，比如人脸识别、下棋、翻译，但换个任务就抓瞎。判断机器够不够「聪明」有个经典考试叫 图灵测试：让人类隔着屏幕跟两边聊天，一边是人、一边是机器，如果人类猜不出哪边是机器，就算通过。 When people hear "artificial intelligence" they picture a robot that thinks for itself. That is actually strong AI — general intelligence that can learn anything like a human, and it does not exist yet (still in sci-fi). What you use every day is weak AI: it is brilliant at one task — face recognition, chess, translation — but useless at anything else. The classic test of "smartness" is the Turing test: a human chats through a screen with two sides, one human and one machine; if the human cannot tell which is the machine, it passes.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 弱 AI（专用）：只会一种任务，如语音助手、推荐、下棋，现在已经满大街。Weak AI (narrow): good at one task — voice assistants, recommendations, chess — now everywhere.
  • 强 AI（通用）：像人一样会真正思考、能学任何任务，目前尚不存在。Strong AI (general): truly thinks and learns any task like a human — does not exist yet.
  • 图灵测试：人类隔着屏幕对话，若无法分辨对方是人还是机器，则机器通过。Turing test: if a human chatting through a screen cannot tell person from machine, the machine passes.
  • AI 不是从天而降，它经历过三次浪潮：1950 年代提出、1980 年代专家系统、2010 年代深度学习的爆发。AI came in three waves: proposed in the 1950s, expert systems in the 1980s, and the deep-learning boom in the 2010s.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Strong AI (general AI) is a machine that can truly think and learn any task like a human, but it does not yet exist. Weak AI (narrow AI) is a system that is good at one specific task. The Turing test checks whether a human cannot tell a machine from a person in conversation.
例题Example
智能音箱能听懂你说的话，还能控制家电。它是强 AI 还是弱 AI？为什么？A smart speaker understands your speech and controls appliances. Is it strong or weak AI, and why?
它只擅长「语音交互」这一件事，离开这个领域就不行了。It is good only at one thing — voice interaction — and fails outside that domain. 所以它是 弱 AI；真正像人一样什么都懂的「强 AI」目前还没实现。So it is weak AI; the general "strong AI" that understands everything like a human does not exist yet.
练习Practice
提示：想想测试的判据。Hint: think about what the test's criterion is.

一个程序通过了图灵测试，说明什么？A program passes the Turing test. What does this show?

点开看答案Show answer
说明在与人类对话时，判断者无法分辨它是人还是机器——它「显得会思考」，但不代表它真的会思考、拥有通用智能。It means a human judge cannot tell it from a person in conversation — it "seems to think", but it does not actually think or have general intelligence.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 专家系统：知识库 + 推理机 + 界面 Expert systems: knowledge base + inference engine + interface knowledge base · inference engine · IF-THEN 知识库 · 推理机 · IF-THEN
目标：说出专家系统的三个组成部分，看懂「IF…THEN」规则，区分正向/反向推理。Goal: name the three parts of an expert system, read IF…THEN rules, and tell forward from backward chaining.
专家系统就是「把某个专家的本事搬进计算机」。它由三块拼成：一是 知识库，装着一条条规则（形如 IF 条件 THEN 结论），就像医生的经验清单；二是 推理机，负责拿这些规则来推结论；三是 用户界面，让普通人能提问、看答案。经典例子是医疗诊断——你输入症状，它按规则一层层推，最后给出「可能是什么病」。它也用在故障诊断、贷款审批等地方。 An expert system "copies a human expert's skill into a computer". It has three parts: a knowledge base holding rules (written IF condition THEN conclusion), like a doctor's checklist; an inference engine that applies those rules to reach conclusions; and a user interface so ordinary people can ask questions and see answers. A classic example is medical diagnosis — you enter symptoms, it chains through rules, and out comes a likely illness. It is also used in fault diagnosis and loan approval.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 三部件：知识库（规则）、推理机（运用规则）、用户界面（人机交互）。Three parts: knowledge base (rules), inference engine (applies them), user interface (interaction).
  • 规则写成 IF…THEN：如 IF 发烧 AND 咳嗽 THEN 疑似感冒。Rules are IF…THEN: e.g. IF fever AND cough THEN possible flu.
  • 正向推理（forward chaining）：从已知事实出发，往前推出结论。Forward chaining: start from known facts and work forward to a conclusion.
  • 反向推理（backward chaining）：从「想证明的结论」倒推，看需要哪些事实支撑。Backward chaining: start from a goal and work back to see which facts are needed.
  • 优点是把专家知识固化、可复制、24 小时不休息；缺点是知识陈旧了要人手动更新、无法自己学习。It captures expert knowledge and never tires, but its knowledge must be updated by hand and it cannot learn on its own.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: An expert system has three parts: a knowledge base (a set of IF…THEN rules), an inference engine (which applies the rules to reach conclusions) and a user interface. Forward chaining works from facts to conclusions, while backward chaining starts from a goal and works back to the facts needed.
例题Example
给出一条诊断规则，并说出推理机在正向推理时先做什么。Give one diagnostic rule, and say what the inference engine does first in forward chaining.
规则：IF 体温>38.5 THEN 疑似发烧。Rule: IF temperature>38.5 THEN possible fever. 正向推理时，推理机把已知事实（比如「体温 39」）拿去和规则的条件匹配，条件满足就得出 THEN 的结论。In forward chaining, the engine matches known facts (e.g. "temperature 39") against the rule's condition, and once it fits, fires the THEN conclusion.
练习Practice
提示：想想「知识放哪、谁在推理、谁来用」。Hint: think "where knowledge lives, who reasons, who uses it".

列出专家系统的三个组成部分，并各用一句话说明。List the three parts of an expert system and describe each in one sentence.

点开看答案Show answer
知识库——存放 IF…THEN 规则；推理机——按规则从事实推出结论；用户界面——让用户输入信息、看到结果。Knowledge base — stores the IF…THEN rules; inference engine — applies rules to facts to reach conclusions; user interface — lets the user enter information and see results.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 机器学习：监督 / 无监督 / 强化 Machine learning: supervised / unsupervised / reinforcement supervised · unsupervised · reinforcement 监督 · 无监督 · 强化
目标：说清三种学习范式的区别，并理解「训练数据、模型、泛化」这条主线。Goal: explain the three paradigms and understand the thread "training data → model → generalisation".
机器学习说白了就是「让程序从数据里自己找规律，而不是靠人一条条写规则」。三种学法：一是 监督学习，像老师给了标准答案，拿带标注的数据去学（比如一堆标好「猫/狗」的照片），学会后做分类或回归；二是 无监督学习，没有标准答案，让程序自己在数据里找结构，比如把相似的东西聚成一堆（聚类）；三是 强化学习，靠「试错 + 奖励」学，做对了给糖、做错了扣分，像训练小狗，AlphaGo 下棋就是这么练出来的。学完的成果叫 模型，模型面对没见过的数据也能答得不错，这个本事叫 泛化。 Machine learning, in plain words, is "letting the program find patterns in data instead of a person writing rules one by one". Three ways to learn: supervised learning has an answer key — it trains on labelled data (e.g. photos marked "cat"/"dog") to classify or regress. Unsupervised learning has no answers — the program finds structure on its own, like grouping similar items together (clustering). Reinforcement learning learns by trial, error and reward — treat when right, punish when wrong, like training a puppy; AlphaGo learned chess this way. The result is called a model; when the model also does well on data it has never seen, that ability is generalisation.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 监督学习：用带标注的数据训练，做分类或回归（如垃圾邮件识别、房价预测）。Supervised learning: trains on labelled data for classification or regression (spam detection, house prices).
  • 无监督学习：数据没标注，让程序找结构，典型是聚类。Unsupervised learning: no labels; the program finds structure, typically clustering.
  • 强化学习：试错 + 奖励反馈，学出一套能拿高分数的策略。Reinforcement learning: trial and error with rewards, learning a strategy that scores highly.
  • 主线：训练数据 → 训练出模型 → 模型要能泛化到没见过的新数据。The thread: training data → train a model → the model must generalise to new data.
  • 数据越多、越干净，模型通常学得越准。More and cleaner data usually gives a more accurate model.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Supervised learning trains on labelled data to perform classification or regression. Unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabelled data, such as clustering. Reinforcement learning learns by trial and error using rewards and penalties.
例题Example
判断下列分别属于哪种学习：垃圾邮件识别、顾客分群、下棋机器人。Classify these: spam detection, customer grouping, a chess-playing robot.
垃圾邮件识别用带标注（是不是垃圾邮件）的数据 → 监督学习。Spam detection uses labelled data (spam or not) → supervised learning. 顾客分群没有现成标签、自动把相似顾客聚一起 → 无监督学习。Customer grouping has no labels and clusters similar customers → unsupervised learning. 下棋机器人靠试错和胜负奖励 → 强化学习。The chess robot learns from trial, error and win/loss rewards → reinforcement learning.
练习Practice
提示：想想「只会背答案、不会举一反三」。Hint: think "memorises answers but can't generalise".

一个模型在训练数据上全对，但一见到新数据就错得离谱，这叫什么问题？A model is perfect on its training data but fails badly on new data. What is this called?

点开看答案Show answer
叫 过拟合（overfitting）——它把训练数据背得太死，没有真正学到规律，泛化能力差。It is overfitting — it memorised the training data too closely without learning the real pattern, so its generalisation is poor.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 神经网络与深度学习 Neural networks and deep learning neuron · activation · deep learning 神经元 · 激活函数 · 深度学习
目标：知道一个神经元在做什么（加权求和 + 激活），并说出深度学习靠什么自动提取特征。Goal: know what one neuron does (weighted sum + activation), and say how deep learning extracts features automatically.
神经网络是模仿大脑的粗线条模型：一个 神经元 接收好几个输入，各自乘上一个「权重」，加在一起，再过一个 激活函数 决定要不要「点火」输出。很多神经元一层一层排起来，就成了多层网络：输入层 → 隐藏层 → 输出层。所谓 深度学习，其实就是「有很多隐藏层的神经网络」。它最厉害的地方是能「层层提取特征」：比如识别一张人脸，底层先认边缘和颜色，中间认眼睛鼻子嘴，顶层才拼出「这是谁」——不需要人事先告诉它看什么特征，它自己一层层挖出来。 A neural network is a rough model of the brain: a neuron takes several inputs, multiplies each by a weight, adds them up, then passes the sum through an activation function to decide whether to "fire". Many neurons stacked into layers make a multi-layer network: input layer → hidden layer → output layer. Deep learning is simply "a neural network with many hidden layers". Its greatest trick is extracting features layer by layer: to recognise a face, the first layers pick out edges and colours, middle layers find eyes, nose and mouth, and the top layer assembles "who this is" — nobody had to tell it which features to look at; it digs them out itself.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 神经元 = 输入 × 权重求和 → 激活函数 → 输出。A neuron = inputs × weights summed → activation function → output.
  • 多层网络：输入层 → 隐藏层（可能很多层）→ 输出层。A multi-layer network: input layer → hidden layers (maybe many) → output layer.
  • 深度学习 = 隐藏层很多层的神经网络，能自动提取越来越抽象的特征。Deep learning = a neural network with many hidden layers that extracts ever more abstract features.
  • 权重是「学」出来的：训练时不断调整，让输出更接近标准答案。Weights are learned: training adjusts them until the output matches the expected answer.
  • 相比传统方法，深度学习省去了人工设计特征的麻烦，但需要海量数据和算力。Deep learning spares us hand-designing features, but needs huge data and computing power.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A neuron takes several inputs, multiplies each by a weight, sums them, and passes the result through an activation function. Deep learning is a neural network with many hidden layers that automatically extracts features layer by layer.
例题Example
用一句话解释「深度学习」和普通神经网络的关系。In one sentence, how is "deep learning" related to an ordinary neural network?
深度学习就是隐藏层很多层的神经网络——「深」指层数多。Deep learning is a neural network with many hidden layers — "deep" means many layers. 正因为层多，它才能自动层层提取特征，而不用人手动设计特征。Because there are many layers, it extracts features layer by layer automatically, with no manual feature design.
练习Practice
提示：先乘、再求和、最后过函数。Hint: multiply, then sum, then pass through the function.

写出一个神经元处理输入的三个步骤（顺序要对）。Write the three steps a neuron uses to process its inputs, in order.

点开看答案Show answer
① 每个输入乘上自己的权重；② 把所有加权结果加总；③ 把总和送进激活函数，得到该神经元的输出。① Multiply each input by its weight; ② add all the weighted results together; ③ pass the sum through the activation function to get the neuron's output.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 AI 的应用：语音、图像、语言、推荐、驾驶 AI applications: speech, vision, language, recommendations, driving NLP · recommender · autonomous 自然语言处理 · 推荐系统 · 自动驾驶
目标：能说出 5 个常见 AI 应用，每个用一句话讲清它在做什么。Goal: name five common AI applications and say in one sentence what each does.
AI 已经悄悄钻进了日常生活。语音识别把你说的话变成文字（手机语音输入、智能音箱）；图像识别看懂图片里有什么（刷脸解锁、医学影像筛查）；自然语言处理让机器理解和生成人类语言（翻译、聊天机器人）；推荐系统猜你喜欢什么，给你推视频、商品（短视频、网购、音乐）；自动驾驶让汽车自己看路、做判断、控制方向盘。它们的共同点：都是「弱 AI」，在各自的小领域里做到极致。 AI has quietly slipped into everyday life. Speech recognition turns your words into text (voice input, smart speakers). Image recognition understands what is in a picture (face unlock, medical scans). Natural language processing lets machines understand and produce human language (translation, chatbots). Recommender systems guess what you like and push videos or products (short videos, shopping, music). Autonomous driving lets a car see the road, decide and steer by itself. Their common thread: they are all "weak AI", doing one narrow job extremely well.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 语音识别：把语音转成文字（语音助手、字幕）。Speech recognition: turns speech into text (assistants, subtitles).
  • 图像识别：识别图片中的物体/人脸（刷脸、安检、医疗影像）。Image recognition: recognises objects or faces in images (unlock, security, medical scans).
  • 自然语言处理（NLP）：理解并生成语言（翻译、问答、聊天机器人）。Natural language processing (NLP): understands and generates language (translation, QA, chatbots).
  • 推荐系统：根据你的行为预测偏好，推送内容或商品。Recommender systems: predict your preferences from your behaviour and push content or products.
  • 自动驾驶：用传感器感知路况并自动决策、控制车辆。Autonomous driving: senses the road with sensors and automatically decides and controls the car.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Common AI applications include speech recognition, image recognition, natural language processing, recommender systems and autonomous driving. Each is an example of weak AI that excels in one specific task.
例题Example
说出两个 AI 应用，并各写一句它做了什么。Name two AI applications and write one sentence on what each does.
推荐系统——根据你过往的观看/购买记录，预测你可能会喜欢的内容并推送给你。Recommender systems — predict what you might like from your watch/purchase history and push it to you. 图像识别——分析照片，识别出里面的人脸或物体。Image recognition — analyse a photo and identify the faces or objects in it.

6 AI 的局限与伦理 AI limitations and ethics bias · black box · privacy 偏见 · 黑箱 · 隐私
目标：说清 AI 的几大局限与伦理问题，并记住「AI 是工具，不是万能的」。Goal: explain AI's key limitations and ethical issues, and remember "AI is a tool, not a magic answer".
AI 不是万能的，也有明显的短板和麻烦。它要「吃」海量数据、烧大量算力，小团队根本养不起；深度学习还是个 黑箱——它能给出答案，却说不出为什么，可解释性差；训练数据里藏着偏见，学出来的模型就会「歧视」；它还盯着你的个人数据，隐私容易受伤；等它越来越能干，一部分工作可能被替代；而一旦 AI 决策出了事（比如自动驾驶撞了车），责任该算谁的也很难说。所以一句话：AI 是工具，用得好是助手，用不好是麻烦，最终拍板的还是人。 AI is not all-powerful — it has clear limits and troubles. It needs vast data and huge computing power, which small teams cannot afford. Deep learning is still a black box: it gives answers but cannot explain why. If the training data is biased, the model learns and amplifies that bias. It also feeds on your personal data, so privacy is easily hurt. As it grows more capable, some jobs may be replaced. And when an AI decision goes wrong (say a self-driving car crashes), who is responsible is far from clear. In one line: AI is a tool — a great helper when used well, a problem when not, and humans must make the final call.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 数据与算力：训练需要海量数据和强大算力，成本高。Data and computing: training needs vast data and heavy computing, which is costly.
  • 黑箱问题：神经网络难以解释「为什么这样判断」，可解释性差。Black box: neural networks can rarely explain "why this decision", so they are hard to interpret.
  • 算法偏见：训练数据有偏见，模型就会学到并放大偏见。Algorithmic bias: if training data is biased, the model learns and amplifies the bias.
  • 隐私：模型训练大量使用个人数据，存在泄露与滥用风险。Privacy: training uses lots of personal data, risking leaks and misuse.
  • 就业与责任：可能替代部分岗位；AI 出错时责任归属难界定。Jobs and accountability: it may replace some jobs; when AI errs, responsibility is hard to pin down.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: AI needs huge amounts of data and computing power, can be a "black box" that cannot explain its decisions, and may learn bias from biased training data. It also raises privacy, employment and accountability concerns, so humans must stay responsible for the final decisions.
例题Example
为什么说「AI 做出的决定可能带偏见」？举一个可能的原因。Why might "AI decisions be biased"? Give one possible reason.
因为模型是从训练数据里学的。Because the model is learned from training data. 如果训练数据本身不公平（比如某类人群样本过少或标签有偏见），模型就会学到这种偏见，并在预测时放大它。If the training data is unfair (e.g. a group is under-sampled or labels are biased), the model learns that bias and amplifies it in predictions.

深度学习模型给出结果却难以解释推导过程；麻烦在于一旦出错（如拒贷、误诊），人们很难查清原因，也难以追责和修正。A deep-learning model gives a result but cannot explain its reasoning; the trouble is that when it errs (e.g. a loan denial or misdiagnosis), people struggle to find the cause, hold anyone accountable, or fix it.

第 18 单元小结Unit 18 wrap-up

这一单元把「AI 怎么让机器显得会思考」讲透了：强 AI（通用智能）还没实现，现实中全是弱 AI（专用）；造 AI 的三条路分别是专家系统（规则 + 推理）、机器学习（监督/无监督/强化）和神经网络（层层提取特征，层多就叫深度学习）。应用满天飞——语音、图像、语言、推荐、驾驶，但 AI 也有黑箱、偏见、隐私这些必须正视的短板。记住一条主线：AI 是工具，不是万能的，最终拍板的还是人。This unit covered how AI makes machines "seem to think": strong AI (general intelligence) does not exist yet, and everything real is weak AI (narrow). The three routes to building AI are expert systems (rules + inference), machine learning (supervised/unsupervised/reinforcement) and neural networks (features extracted layer by layer — deep learning means many layers). Applications are everywhere — speech, vision, language, recommendations, driving — but AI also has black-box, bias and privacy limits we must face. One thread runs through it all: AI is a tool, not a magic answer — humans still make the final call.

这一单元是 Paper 4（上机）的核心思维：先学会「估算算法有多快」，再学会「让函数调用自己」——递归是树、迷宫、数独这些难题最优雅的解法。This unit is the core thinking of Paper 4 (practical): first estimate how fast an algorithm is, then learn to let a function call itself — recursion is the most elegant way to solve trees, mazes and sudoku.

1 算法复杂度与大 O 记法 Algorithm complexity and big-O big-O · growth order 大O · 增长阶
目标：看懂大 O 记法，能按增长速度给常见复杂度排序。Goal: understand big-O and rank common complexities by growth rate.
同一个问题，算法 A 要 1 秒，算法 B 要 1 小时——差别就在复杂度。大 O 记法就像给算法贴一张「饭量」标签：它不告诉你具体吃几口，而是告诉你——菜（输入规模 n）多一倍，饭量大概翻几倍。O(1) 是吃一口就饱（不管多少菜都一步到位），O(n) 是一道菜吃一口（菜多一倍就多吃一倍），O(n²) 是每两道菜都要配一次（菜多一倍吃四倍），O(2ⁿ) 更夸张，多一道菜饭量直接翻倍，n 稍微大一点就撑爆了。 Same problem, algorithm A takes 1 second and B takes an hour — the difference is complexity. Big-O is like an "appetite" label: it doesn't tell you exactly how many bites, but how the appetite grows when the dishes (input size n) double. O(1) is one bite and you're done, O(n) is one bite per dish, O(n²) pairs every two dishes, and O(2ⁿ) doubles with every extra dish — n a little larger and it explodes.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 大 O 描述最坏情况下，运行时间随输入规模 n 增长的速度，不是精确秒数。Big-O describes how the running time grows with n in the worst case, not the exact seconds.
  • O(1) 常数：不管 n 多大都一步到位，比如按下标读数组。O(1) constant: one step no matter how big n is, e.g. reading an array by index.
  • O(log n) 对数：每次砍掉一半，比如二分查找。O(log n) logarithmic: halve the problem each time, e.g. binary search.
  • O(n) 线性：n 个数据就做 n 次，比如从头到尾遍历一遍。O(n) linear: n items means n steps, e.g. one full pass.
  • O(n²) 平方：两层嵌套循环，比如冒泡排序；O(2ⁿ) 指数：每加一个输入工作量翻倍，比如穷举所有子集。O(n²) quadratic: two nested loops, e.g. bubble sort; O(2ⁿ) exponential: work doubles per extra input, e.g. enumerating all subsets.
别记反：增长速度从慢到快是 O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n²) < O(2ⁿ)。大 O 还忽略常数和低阶项，所以 2n+5 和 100n 都记作 O(n)。Don't mix these up: slowest to fastest is O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n²) < O(2ⁿ). Big-O also ignores constants and lower-order terms, so 2n+5 and 100n are both O(n).
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Big-O notation describes the worst-case time complexity of an algorithm, showing how the running time grows as the input size n increases. O(n²) grows much faster than O(log n) for large n.
例题Example
一个算法先遍历一遍数组（n 步），再对每一对元素做一次比较（n² 步），总步数是 n² + n。它的大 O 是多少？An algorithm first passes over the array (n steps), then compares every pair (n² steps), a total of n² + n steps. What is its big-O?
总步数 = n² + n。Total steps = n² + n. n 很大时 n² 占主导，低阶项 n 和常数都可以忽略。When n is large, n² dominates; the lower-order n and constants are ignored. 所以大 O 是 O(n²)。So the big-O is O(n²).
练习Practice
提示：想 n 特别大时，谁的数值最小。Hint: think about which value is smallest when n is huge.

把 O(1)、O(log n)、O(n)、O(n²)、O(2ⁿ) 按「随 n 增长由慢到快」排序。Sort O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n²), O(2ⁿ) from slowest to fastest growth.

点开看答案Show answer
O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n²) < O(2ⁿ)。n 越大，排在右边的把左边的甩得越远。O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) < O(n²) < O(2ⁿ). The bigger n gets, the further the right-hand ones pull ahead.

2 递归的概念 The idea of recursion base case · recursive step 基准情形 · 递归步骤
目标：理解递归的两个必备要素，并知道没有基准情形会怎样。Goal: understand the two required parts of recursion and what happens without a base case.
递归就是「函数调用自己」。想象你站在两面镜子中间——镜子里有镜子，镜子里的镜子里还有镜子，一层套一层。但真实世界必须有尽头：最里面那层不是镜子（是个实物），这个「最里面那层」就是递归里的基准情形（base case），是让递归停下来的终止条件。另一个要素是递归步骤：每次调用都让问题变小一点（比如从 fac(3) 变成 fac(2)），一步步逼近基准情形。缺了任何一个，程序要么停不下来，要么原地打转。 Recursion means "a function calls itself". Imagine standing between two mirrors — a mirror inside a mirror, inside a mirror, layer after layer. But the real world must have an end: the innermost layer is not a mirror (it's a real object). That "innermost layer" is the base case, the stopping condition. The other part is the recursive step: each call makes the problem a bit smaller (fac(3) becomes fac(2)), inching toward the base case. Miss either one and the program either never stops or spins in place.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 递归 = 一个函数直接或间接地调用它自己。Recursion = a function calls itself, directly or indirectly.
  • 基准情形（base case）：终止条件，到了就停止返回，不再继续调用。Base case: the stopping condition — when reached, stop and return instead of calling again.
  • 递归步骤：把问题缩小成「更小的同类问题」，向基准情形逼近。Recursive step: shrink the problem into a smaller version of itself, moving toward the base case.
  • 没有 base case → 无限递归，每次调用都占一块栈空间，最终栈溢出崩溃。No base case → infinite recursion; every call takes stack space until a stack overflow crashes it.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Recursion is when a function calls itself. It must have a base case to stop, otherwise it recurses forever and causes a stack overflow. The recursive step reduces the problem size toward the base case.
例题Example
下面的 countdown 函数里，哪一行是基准情形？如果删掉它会发生什么？In the countdown function below, which part is the base case? What happens if you delete it?
FUNCTION countdown(n : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER IF n = 0 THEN OUTPUT 0 RETURN 0 ENDIF OUTPUT n RETURN countdown(n - 1) ENDFUNCTION
IF n = 0 THEN … ENDIF 是基准情形：n=0 时输出 0 并返回，不再调用。IF n = 0 THEN … ENDIF is the base case: when n = 0 it prints 0 and returns without calling again. 删掉它就会一直调用 countdown(-1)、countdown(-2)…… 永不停止，直到栈溢出。Without it, it keeps calling countdown(-1), countdown(-2)… forever, until a stack overflow.
练习Practice
提示：想想「最里面那层不是镜子」对应什么。Hint: think about what "the innermost layer is not a mirror" maps to.

一个递归函数可以没有 base case 吗？为什么？Can a recursive function exist without a base case? Why?

点开看答案Show answer
不可以。没有 base case 就没有终止条件，函数会一直调用自己，每次调用都占用栈空间，最终栈溢出（stack overflow）导致程序崩溃。No. Without a base case there is no stopping condition, so the function keeps calling itself; each call uses stack space until a stack overflow crashes the program.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 递归示例：阶乘与斐波那契 Recursion examples: factorial and Fibonacci factorial · Fibonacci 阶乘 · 斐波那契
目标：会用递归写出并手算阶乘与斐波那契数列。Goal: write and hand-trace factorial and Fibonacci using recursion.
阶乘 n! = n × (n−1) × … × 1，天然就是个递归定义：fac(n) = n × fac(n−1)，边界是 fac(0) = 1。斐波那契数列 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8… 也是递归的：每一项等于前两项之和，fib(n) = fib(n−1) + fib(n−2)，边界是 fib(0)=0、fib(1)=1。注意斐波那契的递归会重复计算很多东西——fib(4) 要算两次 fib(2)，所以它好看但慢。 Factorial n! = n × (n−1) × … × 1 is naturally recursive: fac(n) = n × fac(n−1) with boundary fac(0) = 1. The Fibonacci sequence 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8… is also recursive: each term is the sum of the previous two, fib(n) = fib(n−1) + fib(n−2) with boundaries fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1. Note that Fibonacci recursion recomputes a lot — fib(4) computes fib(2) twice, so it's pretty but slow.
FUNCTION factorial(n : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER IF n = 0 THEN RETURN 1 ELSE RETURN n * factorial(n - 1) ENDIF ENDFUNCTION FUNCTION fib(n : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER IF n = 0 THEN RETURN 0 ENDIF IF n = 1 THEN RETURN 1 ENDIF RETURN fib(n - 1) + fib(n - 2) ENDFUNCTION
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 阶乘：fac(n) = n × fac(n−1)，基准情形 fac(0) = 1。Factorial: fac(n) = n × fac(n−1), base case fac(0) = 1.
  • 斐波那契：fib(n) = fib(n−1) + fib(n−2)，基准情形 fib(0)=0、fib(1)=1。Fibonacci: fib(n) = fib(n−1) + fib(n−2), base cases fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1.
  • 递归的正确性靠「数学归纳」：先证最小情形成立，再证「若 n−1 成立则 n 成立」。Recursion's correctness rests on induction: prove the smallest case, then prove "if n−1 works, n works".
  • 斐波那契递归有大量重复计算，效率低（指数级），实际常用循环或记忆化。Fibonacci recursion has lots of recomputation and is inefficient (exponential); loops or memoisation are used in practice.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Factorial is defined recursively as fac(n) = n × fac(n−1) with fac(0) = 1. Fibonacci is fib(n) = fib(n−1) + fib(n−2) with fib(0) = 0 and fib(1) = 1.
例题Example
手算 factorial(4) 的展开过程。Trace the expansion of factorial(4) by hand.
fac(4) = 4 × fac(3)fac(4) = 4 × fac(3) = 4 × 3 × fac(2) = 4 × 3 × 2 × fac(1)= 4 × 3 × fac(2) = 4 × 3 × 2 × fac(1) = 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 × fac(0)，而 fac(0) = 1= 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 × fac(0), and fac(0) = 1 回代得到 24。Substitute back to get 24.
练习Practice
提示：从 fib(0) 和 fib(1) 一路往上加。Hint: add up from fib(0) and fib(1).

计算 fib(5)（斐波那契，fib(0)=0，fib(1)=1）。Work out fib(5) (Fibonacci, fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1).

点开看答案Show answer
fib(0)=0，fib(1)=1，fib(2)=1，fib(3)=2，fib(4)=3，所以 fib(5) = 3 + 2 = 5。fib(0)=0, fib(1)=1, fib(2)=1, fib(3)=2, fib(4)=3, so fib(5) = 3 + 2 = 5.

4 递归 vs 迭代 Recursion vs iteration stack overflow · tail recursion 栈溢出 · 尾递归
目标：分清递归和迭代各自的优缺点，知道什么时候该用谁。Goal: weigh up recursion vs iteration and know when to use each.
递归和迭代都能重复做事，但脾气不一样。递归代码简洁、几乎就是数学定义照抄（fac(n) = n × fac(n−1)），可它每调一层都要在栈上记一笔「我还没算完，先记着」，层数一深栈就满了，栈溢出。迭代用循环 + 一个变量，省内存、跑得快，但代码可能不如递归直观。有个折中叫尾递归：如果递归调用是函数的最后一步，编译器可以把它优化成循环，不再堆栈。经验是——树遍历、分治这类天然套娃的问题用递归；简单计数、累加用迭代。 Recursion and iteration both repeat work, but with different tempers. Recursion is short and almost copies the maths definition (fac(n) = n × fac(n−1)), but every layer writes "not done yet, remember me" on the stack; go too deep and the stack overflows. Iteration uses a loop and one variable — cheaper and faster, but sometimes less intuitive. A middle way is tail recursion: if the recursive call is the very last step, the compiler can turn it into a loop, so the stack never grows. Rule of thumb — use recursion for naturally nested problems like tree traversal and divide-and-conquer, iteration for simple counting and summing.
FUNCTION facRec(n : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER IF n = 0 THEN RETURN 1 ENDIF RETURN n * facRec(n - 1) ENDFUNCTION FUNCTION facIter(n : INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER DECLARE result : INTEGER result ← 1 FOR i ← 1 TO n result ← result * i NEXT i RETURN result ENDFUNCTION
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 递归：代码简洁、贴近定义，但每次调用占栈空间，深度太大就栈溢出。Recursion: short and close to the definition, but each call uses stack space; too deep and it overflows the stack.
  • 迭代：循环 + 变量，省内存、速度快，但代码可能不如递归直观。Iteration: loop + variable, cheaper and faster, but sometimes less intuitive.
  • 尾递归：递归调用是最后一步，可被优化成循环、不额外堆栈。Tail recursion: the recursive call is the last step, so it can be optimised into a loop with no extra stack.
  • 用递归：树遍历、分治（归并排序、快速排序）；用迭代：简单循环、层数可能很深的场景。Use recursion for tree traversal and divide-and-conquer (merge sort, quicksort); use iteration for simple loops and possibly deep cases.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Recursion is concise and mirrors the problem, but each call uses stack space and may cause a stack overflow. Iteration uses less memory. Tail recursion can be optimised into iteration by the compiler.
例题Example
上面两个求阶乘的函数，哪个更省内存？递归版有什么风险？Which of the two factorial functions above uses less memory? What is the risk of the recursive one?
facIter 更省内存——它只用一个变量 result，栈上不叠加调用。facIter uses less memory — just one variable result, no stacking of calls. facRec 每层调用都占栈空间，n 很大时可能栈溢出。facRec uses stack space per call, so a large n may cause a stack overflow. 但 facRec 更短、更贴近数学定义，读起来一目了然。But facRec is shorter and closer to the maths, so it reads at a glance.
练习Practice
提示：想「问题是不是天然套娃」。Hint: think "is the problem naturally nested?"

什么情况下应该优先用递归而不是迭代？举一个例子。When should you prefer recursion over iteration? Give an example.

点开看答案Show answer
当问题天然是递归结构时优先用递归，比如遍历二叉树或归并排序这类分治——递归代码更清晰，几乎照抄定义；而简单累加、计数用迭代更省内存。Prefer recursion when the problem is naturally recursive, like traversing a binary tree or divide-and-conquer such as merge sort — the code is clearer and almost copies the definition; simple summing and counting are cheaper with iteration.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 递归遍历二叉树 Traversing a binary tree recursively pre-order · in-order · post-order 前序 · 中序 · 后序
目标：能对一棵二叉树写出前序、中序、后序三种遍历结果。Goal: write the pre-order, in-order and post-order traversals of a binary tree.
遍历二叉树就是「按某种顺序把每个节点访问一遍」。访问有三个动作：看根、逛左子树、逛右子树，三种遍历就是这三种动作的三种排列——前序根最先（根左右）、中序根在中间（左根右）、后序根最后（左右根）。用递归写这个最自然：对每个节点，先处理自己（根），再递归处理左子树、右子树，顺序换一下就是另一种遍历。特别记住：二叉搜索树的中序遍历结果是从小到大排好序的。 Traversing a tree means visiting every node in some order. Visiting has three actions: look at the root, walk the left subtree, walk the right subtree. The three traversals are three orderings of those actions — pre-order visits the root first (root, left, right), in-order in the middle (left, root, right), post-order last (left, right, root). Recursion is the natural way: at each node, handle yourself (root), then recurse into the left and right subtrees — swap the order and you get another traversal. Remember: in-order traversal of a binary search tree gives the values in sorted order.
PROCEDURE preOrder(node) IF node = NULL THEN RETURN ENDIF OUTPUT node.data preOrder(node.left) preOrder(node.right) ENDPROCEDURE
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 前序（pre-order）：根 → 左 → 右。Pre-order: root → left → right.
  • 中序（in-order）：左 → 根 → 右；二叉搜索树里结果升序。In-order: left → root → right; sorted ascending in a binary search tree.
  • 后序（post-order）：左 → 右 → 根；常用于先处理完孩子再处理自己（如删除树）。Post-order: left → right → root; used when children are handled before the node (e.g. deleting a tree).
  • 递归模板都一样：处理根 + 递归左子树 + 递归右子树，只是「处理根」的位置不同。The recursive template is the same — handle root + recurse left + recurse right — only the position of "handle root" changes.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Pre-order visits the root, then the left subtree, then the right. In-order visits left, root, right (giving sorted output for a binary search tree). Post-order visits left, right, then root.
例题Example
对上面那棵树写出前序、中序、后序遍历。Write the pre-order, in-order and post-order traversals of the tree above.
前序（根左右）：先 A，再左子树 B(D,E)，再右子树 C(F) → A B D E C F。Pre-order (root, left, right): A, then left subtree B(D,E), then right C(F) → A B D E C F. 中序（左根右）：左 D B E，根 A，右 C F → D B E A C F。In-order (left, root, right): left D B E, root A, right C F → D B E A C F. 后序（左右根）：左 D E B，右 F C，根 A → D E B F C A。Post-order (left, right, root): left D E B, right F C, root A → D E B F C A.
练习Practice
提示：记住「中序 = 左根右」。Hint: remember "in-order = left, root, right".

一棵树：P 是根，Q 是 P 的左孩子、R 是右孩子，Q 又有两个孩子 S、T。写出中序遍历。A tree: P is the root, Q is P's left child and R the right child; Q has two children S and T. Write the in-order traversal.

点开看答案Show answer
中序（左根右）：先 Q 的左子树 S，再 Q，再 T，然后根 P，最后右子树 R → S Q T P R。In-order (left, root, right): Q's left subtree S, then Q, then T, then root P, then right subtree R → S Q T P R.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 回溯法简介 Introduction to backtracking backtracking · eight queens 回溯 · 八皇后
目标：理解回溯的思想，能描述它怎么解迷宫、数独、八皇后。Goal: understand backtracking and describe how it solves mazes, sudoku and the eight queens.
回溯（backtracking）就是「试着走，走不通就退回来换一条」。像走迷宫：每到岔口先随便选一条路，一路走到底；碰到死胡同，就原路退回上一个岔口，换另一条再试。它和递归是天生一对——递归负责「往前试下一步」，撤销负责「退回上一步」。这套「选择 → 递归 → 撤销」的框架，能解一大类难题：八皇后（在棋盘放 8 个互不攻击的皇后）、迷宫、数独、图的哈密顿路径，全是它。 Backtracking is "try a path, and back up when it fails". Like a maze: at each fork pick a path and go to the end; hit a dead end, retreat to the last fork and try another branch. It pairs naturally with recursion — recursion tries the next step forward, and an undo step retreats. This "choose → recurse → undo" framework solves a whole class of hard problems: the eight queens (place 8 queens that don't attack each other), mazes, sudoku and Hamiltonian paths in graphs.
PROCEDURE Solve(position) IF IsSolution(position) THEN OUTPUT position RETURN ENDIF FOR EACH move IN PossibleMoves(position) IF Valid(move) THEN MakeMove(move) Solve(Next(position, move)) UndoMove(move) ENDIF NEXT move ENDPROCEDURE
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 回溯 = 深度优先搜索 + 撤销：一步步做选择，做不下去就退回并撤销上一步。Backtracking = depth-first search + undo: choose step by step, and when stuck retreat and undo the last choice.
  • 三步框架：选择 → 递归试探 → 撤销，循环往复直到找到解或试完所有可能。The three-step frame: choose → recurse to try → undo, repeated until a solution is found or all options are exhausted.
  • 经典问题：八皇后、迷宫、数独、图的哈密顿路径。Classic problems: eight queens, mazes, sudoku and Hamiltonian paths in graphs.
  • 用递归实现最自然：递归往前探路，返回时撤销，栈自动记住「退到哪」。Recursion fits best: recursion probes forward, unwinds on return, and the stack remembers where to back up to.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Backtracking explores candidate choices one by one, and when a choice leads to a dead end it undoes that choice and tries the next one. It is used for problems like the eight queens, mazes and sudoku.
例题Example
简述回溯法是怎么解数独的。Briefly describe how backtracking solves sudoku.
从第一个空格开始，依次尝试填 1 到 9。Start at the first empty cell and try digits 1 to 9 in turn. 每个数字检查是否违反行、列、宫规则；合法就填下，并递归去填下一个空格。Check each digit against the row, column and box rules; if valid, place it and recurse into the next empty cell. 若某个空格 1 到 9 都填不了，说明前面填错了，就退回撤销上一个填法，换下一个数字，直到填满或证明无解。If a cell can't take any digit, an earlier choice was wrong, so back up and undo the last placement and try the next digit — until the grid is full or proven unsolvable.
练习Practice
提示：围绕「走一步、标记、死胡同退回」组织答案。Hint: build the answer around "step, mark, retreat at a dead end".

简述回溯法解决迷宫问题的基本步骤。Outline the basic steps of solving a maze with backtracking.

点开看答案Show answer
① 从起点向一个方向走一步，标记当前位置；② 若到达终点则成功；③ 若前方是墙或死胡同，退回上一步换一个方向再试；④ 反复进行，直到找到出口或所有路都试完仍无路可走。① Step from the start in one direction and mark the position; ② if you reach the exit, success; ③ if blocked or in a dead end, retreat one step and try a different direction; ④ repeat until the exit is found or every path has been tried.
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

第 19 单元小结Unit 19 wrap-up

这一单元把「怎么衡量和运用递归」讲透了：先用大 O 记法估算算法随输入 n 增长的速度，再理解递归的两个要素——基准情形（停下）和递归步骤（缩小），拿阶乘、斐波那契练手，然后对比递归 vs 迭代（简洁但占栈 vs 省内存），接着用递归遍历二叉树（前序/中序/后序），最后见识回溯——递归最漂亮的用法，一步走不通就退回换路，解八皇后、迷宫、数独。记住一条主线：递归 = 基准情形 + 缩小问题；回溯 = 递归 + 撤销。This unit covered how to measure and use recursion: estimate an algorithm's growth with big-O, understand recursion's two parts — a base case (to stop) and a recursive step (to shrink) — practise on factorial and Fibonacci, weigh recursion vs iteration (short but stack-hungry vs memory-light), then traverse binary trees recursively (pre/in/post-order), and finally meet backtracking — recursion at its finest, retreating to try another path for the eight queens, mazes and sudoku. One thread ties it together: recursion = base case + shrink; backtracking = recursion + undo.

这一单元把编程从「会写代码」带到「会组织代码」——面向对象、文件和异常，都是 Paper 4 上机题里反复出现的高频考点。This unit takes you from "can write code" to "can organise code" — OOP, files and exceptions are all frequent Paper 4 practical topics.

1 编程范式：过程式、面向对象、声明式 Programming paradigms: procedural, OOP, declarative procedural · OOP · declarative 过程式 · 面向对象 · 声明式
目标：分清三种编程范式，考试能一句话说清「面向对象」和「过程式」的区别。Goal: tell the three paradigms apart and explain the difference between OOP and procedural in one sentence.
同样是「接一杯水」：过程式像给机器人列步骤——1 拿杯子、2 放水龙头下、3 开水、4 关水；面向对象把这些事交给「杯子」这个对象，直接喊 杯子.接水()；声明式更省事，只要说「我要一杯水」就行，具体怎么做由系统自己决定。SQL 就是典型的声明式——你写 SELECT ... 描述「要哪些数据」，而不写「怎么去翻表」。 Same "get a glass of water": procedural is like listing steps for a robot — 1 take cup, 2 put under tap, 3 turn on, 4 turn off; OOP gives the job to the "cup" object, just call cup.fill(); declarative is lazier — just say "I want a glass of water" and the system decides how. SQL is declarative — you write SELECT ... to say which data you want, not how to search the table.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 过程式：把问题拆成一步步指令（函数 + 顺序执行），C 语言是代表。Procedural: break a problem into step-by-step instructions (functions run in order) — C is the classic.
  • 面向对象：围绕「对象」组织，数据（属性）和行为（方法）捆在一起，Java、Python 是代表。OOP: organise around "objects" that bundle data (attributes) and behaviour (methods) — Java and Python.
  • 声明式：只描述「要什么」，不写「怎么做」——SQL、函数式编程都是。Declarative: describe what you want, not how to get it — SQL and functional programming.
  • 三种不是互斥的，Python 就能混着写；但「面向对象」是 Paper 4 的绝对重点。They are not exclusive — Python mixes them; but OOP is the big Paper 4 focus.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A procedural program is a list of step-by-step instructions. In object-oriented programming, data and the methods that operate on it are grouped together into objects. Declarative programming states what should be computed rather than how.
例题Example
说说「面向对象」和「过程式」编程最核心的区别。State the core difference between OOP and procedural programming.
过程式把程序看成「一条条指令/函数」，按顺序执行。Procedural sees a program as a list of instructions/functions run in sequence. 面向对象把「数据 + 操作数据的方法」封装成对象，程序是对象之间的消息传递。OOP wraps data and its methods into objects; the program is objects passing messages.
练习Practice
提示：想想「谁来做这件事」。Hint: think about "who does the work".

下面哪个是「声明式」？A) 先洗菜再切菜 B) SELECT name FROM students C) 定义一个 Car 类并调用 run()Which is declarative? A) wash then chop B) SELECT name FROM students C) define a Car class and call run()

点开看答案Show answer
B 是声明式——它只说明「要 name 这一列」，没说怎么找；A 是过程式，C 是面向对象。B — it only says "give me the name column", not how; A is procedural, C is OOP.
— 第 1 站完成 —— Stop 1 done —
2 类与对象（封装） Classes and objects (encapsulation) class · object · encapsulation 类 · 对象 · 封装
目标：能说出「类 = 蓝图、对象 = 实例」，并用伪代码定义一个类。Goal: state "class = blueprint, object = instance" and define a class in pseudocode.
把「类」想成一张盖房子的图纸：图纸上画了房子有什么（属性，比如几扇窗）和能干什么（方法，比如开门）。但图纸本身不是房子——照着它造出来的每一栋，才是能住人的对象（实例），同一张图纸能造出很多栋不同的房子。封装的意思是：电路、水管藏在墙里，你只需要用「开关」「水龙头」这些接口，不用关心里面怎么绕。 Think of a class as a house blueprint: it says what a house has (attributes, like windows) and what it can do (methods, like open the door). The blueprint is not a house — each actual house built from it is an object (instance), and one blueprint makes many different houses. Encapsulation means the wiring and pipes are hidden in the walls; you only use the "switch" and "tap" interface without caring how it is wired inside.
CLASS Student PRIVATE name : STRING PRIVATE age : INTEGER PUBLIC PROCEDURE NEW(newName, newAge) name ← newName age ← newAge ENDPROCEDURE PUBLIC PROCEDURE study() OUTPUT name, " is studying" ENDPROCEDURE ENDCLASS
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 类 class = 蓝图；对象 object = 按蓝图造出来的实例，可以有多个。Class = blueprint; object = an instance built from it — there can be many.
  • 类里有属性 attributes（数据，如 name、age）和方法 methods（行为，如 study()）。A class holds attributes (data, e.g. name, age) and methods (behaviour, e.g. study()).
  • 封装 encapsulation：把数据藏在内部，只通过方法暴露「接口」，外部不能直接乱改。Encapsulation: hide the data inside, expose only an interface via methods; outsiders cannot change it directly.
  • 伪代码里 PRIVATE 表示私有（外部看不到），PUBLIC 表示公开（可被调用）。In pseudocode PRIVATE means hidden, PUBLIC means callable from outside.
提示：考试常问「封装的好处」——记住一句话：隐藏内部细节、保护数据、修改内部不影响外部。Tip: exams love "benefits of encapsulation" — one sentence: hides internal detail, protects data, and lets you change the inside without affecting the outside.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Encapsulation means hiding the internal state of an object and only allowing access through its methods. This protects the data and makes the code easier to maintain, because internal changes do not affect other parts of the program.
例题Example
用伪代码定义一个 BankAccount 类，含属性 balance 和方法 deposit。Define a BankAccount class in pseudocode with attribute balance and method deposit.
用 CLASS 声明类，用 PRIVATE 声明属性 balance。Declare the class with CLASS and the attribute with PRIVATE. 写方法 deposit 让余额增加，方法里用 ← 赋值。Write the method deposit to increase the balance, using ← for assignment.
练习Practice
提示：注意「属性」和「方法」要分开写。Hint: keep attributes and methods separate.

判断题：一个类只能创建一个对象。True or false: a class can create only one object.

点开看答案Show answer
错。类像图纸，可以照它创建很多个对象（实例），每个对象的属性值可以不同。False. A class is a blueprint — you can create many objects (instances), each with different attribute values.
— 第 2 站完成 —— Stop 2 done —
3 继承与多态 Inheritance and polymorphism inheritance · polymorphism · override 继承 · 多态 · 重写
目标：说清「继承」和「多态」各是什么，以及 override 和 super 的作用。Goal: explain inheritance and polymorphism, and what override and super do.
继承就像孩子继承父母——「狗」和「猫」都是「动物」，它们自动拥有动物的一切（会呼吸、有名字），这叫复用，不用每个类都重写一遍。但狗叫「汪汪」、猫叫「喵」，同一个方法名 speak() 在两个类里表现不同，这就是多态，靠方法重写 override 实现。如果子类里想临时借一下父类的原始版本，用 super 调用即可。 Inheritance is like children inheriting from parents — "Dog" and "Cat" are both "Animal", so they automatically get everything an animal has (breathing, a name). That is reuse: no need to rewrite it for every class. But a dog goes "woof" and a cat "meow" — the same method name speak() behaves differently in each class. That is polymorphism, achieved by method overriding. If a subclass wants the parent's original version, it calls super.
记住这几点：Remember:
  • 继承：子类（subclass）继承父类（superclass）的属性和方法，还能自己加新的。Inheritance: a subclass inherits the superclass's attributes and methods, and can add its own.
  • 多态：同一方法名，在不同子类里被重写（override），表现不同。Polymorphism: the same method name is overridden in different subclasses to behave differently.
  • override 用相同签名重写父类方法；super 用来调用父类被重写的版本。Override rewrites a parent method with the same signature; super calls the parent's overridden version.
  • 好处：代码复用、好扩展、好维护——加一个新「动物」不用改已有的类。Benefits: reuse, easy to extend and maintain — add a new "animal" without touching existing classes.
提示：分清两者——继承是「是」的关系（狗是动物），多态是「同名不同表现」。Tip: inheritance is an "is-a" relation (a dog is an animal); polymorphism is "same name, different behaviour".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: Inheritance allows a subclass to reuse the attributes and methods of its superclass, and to add new ones. Polymorphism allows the same method name to behave differently in different subclasses, usually through method overriding.
例题Example
Dog 继承 Animal 并重写了 speak()，那么调用 dog.speak() 会执行哪个版本？Dog inherits Animal and overrides speak(). Which version runs when dog.speak() is called?
Animal 里的 speak() 输出「动物在叫」；Dog 重写了 speak()。Animal.speak() prints "an animal makes a sound"; Dog overrides speak(). 调用 dog.speak() 时执行 Dog 自己重写的版本，而不是父类的——这就是多态。Calling dog.speak() runs Dog's own overridden version, not the parent's — that is polymorphism.
练习Practice
提示：想想方法名相同、行为不同的例子。Hint: think of one name, different behaviour.

判断题：子类继承父类后，只能原封不动用父类的方法，不能改。True or false: after inheriting, a subclass can only use the parent's methods unchanged.

点开看答案Show answer
错。子类可以重写（override）父类方法，让同名方法有不同表现，这正是多态。False. A subclass can override a parent method so the same name behaves differently — that is polymorphism.
— 第 3 站完成 —— Stop 3 done —
4 文件处理 File handling OPENFILE · text · binary 打开文件 · 文本 · 二进制
目标：会写「打开—读/写—关闭」的文件处理流程，并分清文本/二进制和三种模式。Goal: write the open–read/write–close flow and tell text/binary and the three modes apart.
文件就像一本书：先得打开它，才能读或写，用完必须关上，不然别人用不了、数据也可能没存上。剑桥伪代码里有四个命令：OPENFILE（打开，指定 READ/WRITE/APPEND 模式）、READFILE（读）、WRITEFILE（写）、CLOSEFILE（关）。文本文件存的是能直接看的字符；二进制文件存的是原始字节，图片、可执行程序都是这种，得用专门程序解读。 A file is like a book: you must open it to read or write, and you must close it when done — otherwise others can't use it and data may not be saved. Cambridge pseudocode has four commands: OPENFILE (specify READ/WRITE/APPEND mode), READFILE, WRITEFILE, CLOSEFILE. Text files hold readable characters; binary files hold raw bytes — images and executable programs — and need special programs to read.
OPENFILE "data.txt" FOR READ READFILE "data.txt", line OUTPUT line CLOSEFILE "data.txt"
记住这几点：Remember:
  • OPENFILE 打开，READFILE 读，WRITEFILE 写，CLOSEFILE 关闭——用完一定要关。OPENFILE opens, READFILE reads, WRITEFILE writes, CLOSEFILE closes — always close when done.
  • 三种打开模式：READ 只读、WRITE 写入（会覆盖）、APPEND 追加（加在末尾）。Three modes: READ read only, WRITE write (overwrites), APPEND add to the end.
  • 文本文件存字符；二进制文件存原始字节（图片、程序）。Text files store characters; binary files store raw bytes (images, programs).
  • 逐行读取：在循环里反复 READFILE，直到读到文件末尾（EOF）。Read line by line: READFILE repeatedly in a loop until end of file (EOF).
提示：记一个易错点——以 WRITE 模式打开已有文件会把原内容清空覆盖，想保留就用 APPEND。Tip: a common trap — opening in WRITE mode wipes the old contents; use APPEND to keep them.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: A file must be opened before it is read from or written to, and it must be closed afterwards so the data is saved and the file is released for other programs. Text files store characters, while binary files store raw bytes.
例题Example
写伪代码：打开 data.txt 读取第一行并输出，最后关闭文件。Write pseudocode to open data.txt, read the first line, output it, then close the file.
OPENFILE "data.txt" FOR READ READFILE "data.txt", line OUTPUT line CLOSEFILE "data.txt"
先用 OPENFILE ... FOR READ 打开（只读模式）。First open with OPENFILE ... FOR READ (read only). READFILE 把一行读进变量 line，再 OUTPUT 输出。READFILE reads a line into line, then OUTPUT prints it. 最后 CLOSEFILE 关闭文件。Finally CLOSEFILE closes the file.
练习Practice
提示：注意打开模式。Hint: watch the open mode.

判断题：要往一个已有文件末尾加一行数据，应该用 WRITE 模式打开。True or false: to add a line to the end of an existing file, open it in WRITE mode.

点开看答案Show answer
错。WRITE 会覆盖原内容，追加应该用 APPEND 模式。False. WRITE overwrites; to add to the end use APPEND.
— 第 4 站完成 —— Stop 4 done —
5 异常处理 Exception handling try · catch · finally 异常 · 捕获 · 收尾
目标：理解 try-catch-finally 的执行顺序，并能举出三种常见异常。Goal: understand try-catch-finally order and name three common exceptions.
程序运行时出错，叫异常（exception）——比如除以 0、要打开的文件根本不存在、数组越界。如果不处理，程序会直接崩溃，用户看到一屏报错。用 try-catch-finally 就能兜底：把可能出错的代码放进 try；真出错了就跳到 catch 里「善后」，而不是崩溃；finally 里的代码无论如何都会执行，专门用来收尾（关文件、释放资源）。 An exception is a runtime error — dividing by zero, opening a file that does not exist, or an array index out of range. Unhandled, the program simply crashes and the user sees an error screen. try-catch-finally catches it: put risky code in try; if it fails, jump to catch to handle it instead of crashing; finally runs no matter what and is used for cleanup (closing files, freeing resources).
记住这几点：Remember:
  • try：放可能出错的代码；catch：出错时执行的处理；finally：无论如何都执行。try holds risky code; catch handles the error; finally always runs.
  • 常见异常：除以 0、文件不存在、下标越界。Common exceptions: divide by zero, file not found, index out of range.
  • 好处：程序不会突然崩溃，能给出友好提示，还能在 finally 里善后。Benefit: no sudden crash — you give a friendly message and clean up in finally.
  • 顺序：try 里一报错，就跳过 try 剩余代码进 catch；没报错则跳过 catch；最后都走 finally。Order: on error, the rest of try is skipped and catch runs; if no error, catch is skipped; finally always runs last.
提示：finally 不是「必须」，而是「需要收尾时」才用；但考语义时记住「无论是否异常都执行」。Tip: finally is for cleanup, not mandatory; but in semantics remember "runs whether or not an exception occurs".
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: An exception is an error that occurs while a program is running. Using try-catch-finally, the code in try is attempted; if an exception occurs, control passes to catch to handle it; the finally block always executes, so it is used to release resources.
例题Example
下面这段 try-catch 里，如果 try 中的除零发生，会输出什么？In this try-catch, if the division by zero happens, what is printed?
try: x = 10 / 0 print("A") except: print("B") finally: print("C")
10/0 抛出除零异常，try 里后面的 print("A") 被跳过。10/0 raises a division error, so print("A") is skipped. 进入 except，输出 B；最后 finally 输出 C。所以结果是 B、C。except runs and prints B; finally prints C. Result: B then C.
练习Practice
提示：先判断有没有异常。Hint: first decide whether an exception occurs.

判断题：finally 块只有在 catch 执行后才会执行。True or false: the finally block runs only after catch runs.

点开看答案Show answer
错。finally 无论如何都执行——即使没出异常、catch 没执行，finally 也会运行。False. finally always runs — even if no exception occurred and catch did not run.
— 第 5 站完成 —— Stop 5 done —
6 用 Python 写 OOP 示例 Writing OOP in Python class · __init__ · self 类 · 构造 · 实例
目标：用 Python 写一个完整的类（属性 + 方法），创建对象并调用，和伪代码对应起来。Goal: write a full Python class (attributes + methods), create an object, call it, and map it to pseudocode.
Paper 4 上机常考 Python/Java/VB，所以要把前面的概念落成真代码。Python 里：__init__ 是构造函数，self 代表「这个对象自己」，self.name 就是对象的属性，方法用 def 定义。对照伪代码：DECLARE 对应 self.xxx 属性，PROCEDURE 对应 def，← 对应 =。写好类后，用 Student("Amy", 16) 就能实例化出一个对象，再用 对象.方法() 调用。 Paper 4 practical often uses Python/Java/VB, so turn the concepts into real code. In Python: __init__ is the constructor, self means "this object", self.name is an attribute, and methods use def. Mapping to pseudocode: DECLARE → self.xxx attributes, PROCEDURE → def, ← → =. Once written, Student("Amy", 16) instantiates an object, then call object.method().
class Student: def __init__(self, name, age): self.name = name self.age = age def study(self): print(self.name, "is studying") amy = Student("Amy", 16) # create an object amy.study() # prints: Amy is studying
记住这几点：Remember:
  • class 定义类，__init__ 是构造方法，self 指向当前对象，self.name 是属性。class defines the class; __init__ is the constructor; self is the current object; self.name is an attribute.
  • def 定义方法；实例化用 类名(参数) 创建对象；调用用 对象.方法()。def defines a method; instantiate with ClassName(args); call with object.method().
  • 对应关系：伪代码 DECLARE → Python 属性，PROCEDURE → def，← → =，OUTPUT → print。Mapping: DECLARE → attribute, PROCEDURE → def, ← → =, OUTPUT → print.
  • Java/VB 写法不同但思想一样：类 = 蓝图，对象 = 实例，方法 = 行为。Java/VB differ in syntax but the idea is the same: class = blueprint, object = instance, method = behaviour.
提示：Paper 4 里 __init__ 的双下划线最容易写漏，而且 self 是每个方法的第一个参数，别忘。Tip: in Paper 4 the double underscores in __init__ are easy to miss, and self must be the first parameter of every method.
🗣 考场英文怎么说：🗣 How to say it in the exam: In Python, a class is defined with the class keyword; __init__ is the constructor that sets up attributes; self refers to the current instance. An object is created by calling the class, and methods are called using dot notation.
例题Example
给下面的 Student 类补一个方法 introduce()，让它输出 "My name is Amy, I am 16"。Add a method introduce() to Student that prints "My name is Amy, I am 16".
def introduce(self): print(f"My name is {self.name}, I am {self.age}")
用 def 定义方法，第一个参数写 self。Define the method with def, self as first parameter. 用 print 加 f-string，把 name 和 age 拼进一句话。Use print with an f-string to combine name and age.
练习Practice
提示：属性要写在 __init__ 里。Hint: attributes go inside __init__.

补全代码：执行 amy = Student("Amy", 16) 之后，如何调用方法让 amy 学习？After amy = Student("Amy", 16), how do you call a method to make amy study?

点开看答案Show answer
写 amy.study()——对象名.方法名()，会输出 "Amy is studying"。amy.study() — object.method(), which prints "Amy is studying".
— 第 6 站完成 —— Stop 6 done —

第 20 单元小结Unit 20 wrap-up

这一单元把「写代码」升级成「组织代码」：过程式、面向对象、声明式是三种思路；类是蓝图、对象是实例，封装藏起细节、继承复用父类、多态同名不同表现；文件要开-读写-关；异常用 try-catch-finally 兜底。最后落到 Python 真代码——这些正是 Paper 4 上机题的核心套路。This unit upgraded "writing code" to "organising code": procedural, OOP, declarative are three ways to think; a class is a blueprint and an object is an instance, with encapsulation hiding details, inheritance reusing parents and polymorphism giving one name many behaviours; files follow open–read/write–close; exceptions are caught with try-catch-finally. It all lands in real Python code — the core of Paper 4 practical questions.

Weak AI masters one task; strong AI (general) does not exist yet.

O(n²)平方，冒泡排序quadratic, bubble sort

必背递归两要素：基准情形（终止条件）+ 递归步骤（缩小规模）；factorial(n) = n × factorial(n−1)，factorial(0) = 1。二叉树遍历：前序（根左右）、中序（左根右）、后序（左右根）。OOP：类 = 蓝图、对象 = 实例、封装 = 隐藏内部、继承 = 子类复用父类、多态 = 方法重写。异常处理用 try-catch-finally。Essentials recursion: a base case (stop) + a recursive step (shrink); factorial(n) = n × factorial(n−1), factorial(0) = 1. Tree traversals: pre-order (root-left-right), in-order (left-root-right), post-order (left-right-root). OOP: class = blueprint, object = instance, encapsulation = hide internals, inheritance = subclass reuses parent, polymorphism = method overriding. Exceptions use try-catch-finally.

考前最后一扫Final sweep before the exam

闭眼也要写得出的五样东西：① 补码三步（写正数→取反→加 1）；② 伪代码的 IF/FOR/WHILE/PROCEDURE 写法；③ 六个逻辑门真值表；④ SQL 的 SELECT-FROM-WHERE；⑤ 递归的「基准情形 + 递归步骤」。这五样覆盖了四张卷的骨架分。Five things you must write with your eyes closed: ① two's complement (positive → flip → add 1); ② the IF/FOR/WHILE/PROCEDURE pseudocode; ③ the six logic-gate truth tables; ④ SQL SELECT-FROM-WHERE; ⑤ recursion's "base case + recursive step". These five cover the backbone marks of all four papers.

学习资源 · 免费又好用的 5 组Resources · 5 free, useful groups

第一组能动手玩（建立手感），第二组是官方大纲与真题，后面是看课、刷题和纸笔练习。外链都已实测可达。Group 1 is hands-on (build the feel), group 2 is official syllabus & past papers, then courses, practice and paper-and-pen drills. All links are verified.

A-Level 计算机科学（9618）怎么学最省力？这门课四张卷，两卷考「懂」（Paper 1/3 术语），两卷考「做」（Paper 2 写伪代码、Paper 4 上机写程序）。所以学习要两条腿走路：一边用下面的可视化工具建立直觉，一边动手写伪代码和 Python。建议顺序：先玩第一组的逻辑门和二分查找可视化，把抽象概念变成画面，再回单元正文，效率会高很多。 How to study A-Level Computer Science (9618) most efficiently? Two papers test understanding (Papers 1 & 3, terminology), two test doing (Paper 2 pseudocode, Paper 4 coding). So learn on two legs: build intuition with the visual tools below, and write pseudocode/Python by hand. Suggested order: play with the logic gates and binary-search visualisations first, turn abstract ideas into pictures, then return to the unit text — it is far more efficient.
访问提示：下面有些站点在境外（BBC、YouTube 等），国内访问可能较慢或需要特殊网络，不是必须的——用「第一组」的可视化工具 + 「第二组」的官方真题，就足够学好这门课了。 Access note: some sites below are overseas (BBC, YouTube) and may be slow or need special network access from mainland China — they are not required. The group-1 visual tools + group-2 official papers are enough.

第一组 · 动手玩（建立手感）Group 1 · Hands-on

这几个工具能把抽象概念变成能点、能拖的画面，先玩十分钟再读正文。These tools turn abstract ideas into clickable pictures — play for ten minutes before reading the text.

CircuitVerse circuitverse.org 拖拽逻辑门搭电路，自动生成真值表，还能搭全加器、时序电路。学单元 3、15 必备。Drag logic gates to build circuits, auto-generate truth tables, even build adders and sequential circuits. Essential for units 3 and 15. VisuAlgo visualgo.net 排序、查找、链表、栈、队列、二叉树、图算法全部有动画，一步步看数据怎么动。学单元 9、10、19 的神器。Animated sorting, searching, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees and graphs — watch the data move step by step. A gem for units 9, 10 and 19. Online Python online-python.com 浏览器里直接跑 Python，不用装环境。Paper 4 上机就用 Python，这里先练手。Run Python right in the browser, no install. Paper 4 uses Python, so practise here first. 思科二进制游戏 cisco.com 用二进制数快速翻牌记分，练熟「二进制↔十进制」的肌肉记忆，几分钟就能上手。Flip cards in binary to score fast — build muscle memory for binary↔denary in minutes. CS50 cs50.harvard.edu 哈佛的免费计算机入门课，讲得很生动（有中文字幕）。适合 A-Level 学完后继续深挖。Harvard's free intro to CS, engaging and clear. A great next step after A-Level.

学习路线建议Suggested route

① 玩「第一组」逻辑门 + VisuAlgo 各十分钟建立手感 → ② 按单元顺序读正文，每站做例题和练习 → ③ 学完用「速查表」tab 复习 → ④ 刷「第二组」历年真题，对照评分标准找差距 → ⑤ Paper 4 前用 Online Python 把伪代码翻译成真代码跑一遍。① Play with the group-1 logic gates and VisuAlgo for ten minutes each → ② read the units in order, doing the examples and practice → ③ revise with the cheat-sheet tab → ④ do the group-2 past papers against the mark schemes → ⑤ before Paper 4, translate your pseudocode into real Python and run it.

先懂原理，再记术语，最后才是刷题Understand the idea, learn the term, then practise

这门课四张卷：Paper 1/3 靠术语（理论，背 + 理解），Paper 2 靠伪代码（纸面写算法），Paper 4 靠上机（真写程序）。配图和「说人话」负责帮你懂；🗣 考场英文怎么说 帮你拿 Paper 1/3 的分；例题和练习帮你拿 Paper 2/4 的分。Four papers: Papers 1 & 3 test terminology (theory), Paper 2 tests pseudocode (writing algorithms on paper), Paper 4 tests coding on a computer. The diagrams and "in plain words" boxes make you understand; the 🗣 How to say it in the exam boxes win Paper 1/3 marks; the examples and practice win Paper 2/4 marks.

下一步：回到 A-Level 数学预习站、物理站 或 化学站；想从更基础处复习，去 IGCSE 计算机科学站；要规划英语去 雅思学习指南。Next: head back to the A-Level Maths site, Physics or Chemistry; for an easier starting point open the IGCSE Computer Science site; or plan your English with the IELTS study path.
